Job Description:
Job Summary
To lead the end-to-end ownership, growth and operational oversight of Independent Contractor and Introducer relationships across the full relationship lifecycle, from recruitment and onboarding through to business development, performance management, ongoing monitoring and exit.
The role is accountable for building a sustainable and productive IC adviser network by driving adviser acquisition, practice growth, lead generation, sales productivity, retention and commercial performance while ensuring adherence to contractual, conduct, regulatory, risk and governance requirements.
The Head: Independent Contractor Relationships serves as the designated owner of Independent Contractor and Introducer relationships and is responsible for maintaining strong adviser engagement, supporting business development initiatives, enhancing adviser productivity, and enabling the growth of assets, revenue and client acquisition opportunities across the adviser channel.
The role is accountable for ensuring that all required governance and monitoring activities are completed, evidence is maintained, commercial and conduct risks are identified and escalated timeously, and relationship outcomes align with the organisation's strategic and commercial objectives.
Job Description
Relationship Ownership and Lifecycle Management
Act as the named owner of the Introducer relationship throughout its lifecycle, from onboarding to exit.
Provide day-to-day oversight of the Introducer relationship to ensure agreed expectations, services and obligations are clearly understood and managed.
Maintain regular engagement with relevant internal stakeholders to support effective relationship governance and operational delivery.
Ensure that the relationship remains aligned to business, risk, conduct and governance expectations.
Introducer Management Workbook and Documentation
Ensure the Introducer Management Workbook is completed, maintained and periodically refreshed.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date records relating to the Introducer relationship, including monitoring evidence, risk updates, contractual information and governance submissions.
Ensure all required documentation is available to support reviews, audits, governance forums and management reporting.
Ongoing Monitoring and Risk Oversight
Monitor the Introducer relationship on an ongoing basis, including services performed, adherence to contractual terms, and consistency of remuneration with agreed pricing arrangements.
Ensure mandatory monitoring activities are performed and documented, including Introducer performance, changes in risk profile and conflict-of-interest attestations where applicable.
Identify emerging risks, control gaps, conduct concerns or performance issues relating to the Introducer relationship.
Escalate concerns appropriately and ensure agreed mitigation actions are tracked to resolution.
Governance, Escalation and Risk Mitigation
Initiate risk mitigation actions where required, including escalation of concerns and lock-up or suspension of the Introducer pending committee approval, where applicable.
Prepare or support submissions to relevant governance forums where decisions or approvals are required.
Ensure that relationship decisions are supported by appropriate evidence, documented rationale and alignment to internal governance requirements.
Work closely with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Sales, Operations and business stakeholders to ensure effective control and oversight.
Exit Management
Manage approved exit actions end-to-end once approved by the relevant governance forums.
Ensure exit activities are documented, coordinated and completed in line with agreed governance and operational requirements.
Support business continuity and risk mitigation during the exit process.
Business Development Accountability
Recruitment and Network Growth:
The Head Independent Contractor Relationships is accountable for building and maintaining a productive adviser network by:
Recruiting quality IC advisers.
Onboarding advisers into the Absa IC model.
Growing adviser footprint in targeted regions and market segments.
Identifying succession and replacement opportunities where advisers exit.
Lead Generation and Pipeline Management
Working with IC’s on activity planning and leads. The Head Independent Contractor Relationships therefore has accountability to:
Generate and distribute qualified leads.
Develop referral and introducer channels.
Create prospecting opportunities for advisers.
Monitor conversion of leads into business.
Revenue and Sales Growth
While IC’s write the business, the Head Independent Contractor Relationships is accountable for creating an environment that drives:
New business sales.
Increased assets under management.
Insurance premium growth.
Cross-selling opportunities.
Improved adviser productivity
IC Practice Development
Facilitate business development strategies and practice management support by:
Coaching IC on business planning.
Improving prospecting disciplines.
Supporting client segmentation strategies.
Building sustainable books of business.
Helping IC’s increase income and productivity.
Relationship and Stakeholder Management
The Head Independent Contractor Relationships acts as the primary interface between the business and advisers by:
Managing IC relationships.
Resolving issues and escalations.
Coordinating support across Operations, Risk, Compliance and Product teams.
Ensuring advisers can focus on sales and client acquisition.
Commercial Governance
Balance commercial objectives with governance and risk oversight and accountable for:
Monitoring adviser conduct.
Ensuring FAIS compliance.
Managing introducer and adviser risks.
Escalating issues early.
Protecting the sustainability of revenue streams.
Preferred Education:
Relevant Bachelor’s degree in Commerce, Business Management, Finance, Risk Management, Law, Compliance, Economics, Financial Planning, or a related field.
Fais Representative – RE5 qualification
Postgraduate qualification or professional certification advantageous (e.g. CFP, CFA, PMP, CISA, ACCA).

Proven experience in managing third-party, intermediary, introducer, broker, adviser, partner or external business relationships.
Strong understanding of sales environments within regulated financial services, including the need to balance commercial outcomes, conduct risk, governance and client protection.
Experience in relationship lifecycle management, including onboarding, monitoring, performance review, risk escalation and exit management.

Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive relationships, identify risks early and drive timely escalation and resolution.
Experience in maintaining governance documentation, monitoring frameworks, registers, workbooks or similar control tools.

Job Description:
JOB SPECIFICATION
The Chief Executive Officer will have overall accountability for the strategy, commercial performance, profitability, growth and market positioning of the Hollard Group Risk business unit.
The role will lead the business across the full Group Risk value chain, including distribution, broker relationships, client management, product, underwriting, pricing, claims, reinsurance and service delivery, working closely with the Group’s actuarial, finance, risk, compliance, technology and other enabling functions. The CEO will also ensure that the business unit’s systems and technology capabilities are scalable, integrated and aligned to commercial, operational and customer priorities.
KEY DELIVERABLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Business Unit Strategy
Develop and execute the Hollard Group Risk business unit strategy within the broader Group strategy.
Define the business unit’s growth, profitability and market positioning objectives.
Identify opportunities across Group Life, Disability, Critical Illness, Funeral and related employee-risk solutions.
Develop strategies for new business growth, retention and portfolio optimisation.
Anticipate changes in the South African Group Risk and employee-benefits market and translate these into business opportunities.
Develop competitive differentiation through proposition, service, technology, data and execution.
P&L and Commercial Performance
Own the business unit P&L and deliver agreed financial and strategic targets.
Drive sustainable premium and earnings growth.
Manage profitability across products, clients, brokers and portfolios.
Ensure disciplined pricing and underwriting including optimising expense and operating efficiency.
Monitor claims experience, persistency, new business strain and other key portfolio metrics.
Identify underperforming portfolios and implement appropriate corrective action.
Provide regular performance reporting and insight to Group executives and the Board including all appropriate governance structures.
Broker and Distribution Leadership
Build trusted, long-term relationships with major brokers and intermediaries.
Establish a clear “easy to do business with” proposition.
Understand broker requirements across pricing, underwriting, service, claims, technology and implementation.
Develop relationships at senior leadership level within major broker organisations.
Monitor broker satisfaction, retention and business flows.
Work closely with sales and distribution teams to grow targeted broker relationships.
Reinsurance Strategy and Relationships
Develop strong strategic relationships with key reinsurers.
Participate in negotiations on treaty structures, pricing, terms and capacity.
Ensure reinsurance arrangements support the business unit’s growth and risk appetite.
Ensure emerging portfolio risks are appropriately considered in the reinsurance strategy.
Work with the Group’s actuarial and risk functions to optimise the use of reinsurance and capital.
Maintain effective relationships with both local and international reinsurance partners.
Underwriting, Pricing and Portfolio Management
Set the commercial direction and appetite for the Hollard Group Risk portfolio within approved Group risk parameters.
Work closely with the Chief Actuary / Actuarial function on portfolio performance and pricing adequacy.
Oversee major and complex underwriting decisions.
Monitor portfolio concentration, accumulation and emerging risks.
Balance competitiveness with long-term portfolio sustainability.
Product and Proposition
Lead the development of a differentiated Hollard Group Risk proposition.
Ensure products respond to changing employer and employee needs.
Identify opportunities for innovation across Group Risk and adjacent employee-benefit propositions.
Explore opportunities to integrate risk benefits with health, wellness and retirement solutions.
Use data, technology and AI to improve underwriting, pricing, claims and customer experience.
Ensure propositions are commercially attractive while remaining operationally viable.
Client and Employer Leadership
Maintain executive relationships with major corporate clients and employer groups.
Act as executive sponsor for strategically important clients.
Participate in significant tenders, renewals and client negotiations.
Ensure client requirements are reflected in the business unit’s proposition and service model.
Lead executive-level resolution of material client issues.
Claims and Customer Experience
Ensure claims capability supports the strategic positioning of the business.
Monitor claims trends and identify emerging portfolio risks.
Ensure appropriate service standards for brokers, employers and members.
Use claims insights to inform underwriting, pricing and product strategy.
Operational Excellence and Transformation
Ensure the business unit has an efficient, scalable operating model.
Partner with Group technology and operations functions to deliver business-unit priorities.
Drive appropriate digitisation, automation, analytics and AI adoption.
Ensure technology investment is aligned to measurable commercial and customer outcomes.
Governance, Risk and Regulatory Management
Operate the business unit within the Group’s approved governance and risk frameworks.
Ensure compliance with applicable South African insurance and financial-services legislation and Group policies.
Ensure material risks and issues are escalated appropriately.
Participate in relevant Board and executive governance forums.
Maintain appropriate relationships with regulatory and industry stakeholders.
Promote a culture of responsible risk-taking and strong governance.
Leadership and Organisation
Lead and develop a high-performing Hollard Group Risk leadership team.
Attract and retain high-quality insurance, actuarial, underwriting, claims and commercial talent.
Develop succession plans for critical positions.
Build a culture of:
customer and broker centricity, commercial discipline, technical excellence, accountability, innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Required Knowledge and Experience
Minimum 10 years' experience within the Group Risk, Life Insurance, Employee Benefits or broader Financial Services sector.
A minimum of 5 years’ experience in a senior leadership capacity, including at least 3 years in an executive-level role with accountability for strategic execution, financial performance and people leadership.
Proven track record of managing a significant P&L/business portfolio and delivering sustainable growth and profitability.
Extensive experience working with brokers and employee-benefit consultants.
Strong understanding of reinsurance.
Experience across underwriting, pricing, claims and portfolio management.
Strong commercial and financial acumen.
Experience operating within a regulated financial-services environment.
Experience engaging with senior executives and Boards.
Advantageous
Experience across Group Life, Disability and Critical Illness.
Experience with large corporate schemes and tenders.
Experience managing strategic broker relationships.
Experience negotiating with reinsurers.
Experience in employee benefits, health or retirement ecosystems.
Experience leading digital, data or AI-enabled transformation.
CRITICAL LEADERSHIP CAPABILITIES
Commercial leadership
Ability to translate market opportunities into profitable growth and sustainable shareholder value.
Broker leadership
Ability to build deep relationships with brokers and create a genuinely differentiated ease-of-doing-business proposition.
Insurance expertise
Strong understanding of Group Risk economics, underwriting, pricing, claims, actuarial principles and reinsurance.
Strategic leadership
Ability to anticipate market changes and position the business unit ahead of them.
Reinsurance capability
Ability to engage credibly with sophisticated reinsurers and translate reinsurance capacity and economics into commercial opportunities.
Customer leadership
Ability to understand employer and employee needs and convert these into compelling propositions.
Transformation leadership
Ability to use technology, data and AI to improve the economics and experience of the business.
Governance
Ability to operate within Group governance while retaining sufficient entrepreneurial freedom to grow the business.
People leadership
Ability to create a high-performing organisation with strong technical and commercial capability.

Provide general support to Warehouse, Production, Logistics and Quality functions as required.

Job Description
We require assistance recruiting a Laboratory Manager / Quality Manager to take responsibility for laboratory operations, technical oversight, staff management and the quality management system.
The successful candidate will oversee testing across seed, plant, feed, food, molecular, GMO, chemical and food-safety applications within the laboratory’s approved scope. This is a hands-on management role requiring practical laboratory testing, data analysis and interpretation alongside leadership and quality management responsibilities.
Key responsibilities
Plan and manage daily laboratory operations, workloads and resources to meet agreed turnaround times.
Supervise, develop and assess laboratory staff, ensuring personnel are competent and authorised for assigned activities.
Personally perform assigned laboratory testing and interpret data within documented competence and technical authority.
Oversee technical review and authorised release of results, ensuring failed controls, unusual results and non-conforming work are investigated before release.
Maintain and improve the quality management system in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025, ISTA, DALRRD and other applicable requirements.
Coordinate internal audits, accreditation assessments, management reviews, proficiency testing and corrective actions.
Maintain effective document control, sample traceability and accurate laboratory records.
Manage equipment calibration and maintenance, facilities, stock, suppliers and laboratory expenditure.
Ensure compliance with laboratory health and safety procedures, data integrity standards, confidentiality and POPIA requirements.
Manage customer enquiries and complaints, monitor performance and report significant risks and improvement priorities to senior management.
Candidate profile
Candidates should demonstrate:
Strong technical knowledge of laboratory methods, method verification or validation, quality control, data interpretation and result review.
Working knowledge of ISO/IEC 17025 and ISTA requirements applicable to the laboratory’s scope.
Practical laboratory competence and the ability to remain actively involved in bench work.
Strong leadership skills, including work allocation, coaching, competence assessment and performance management.
The ability to investigate non-conformances, establish root causes and implement effective corrective actions.
Strong planning, organisational and problem-solving skills, with consistently high standards of documentation.
Clear communication skills and the ability to engage professionally with employees, customers, auditors and senior management.
Sound understanding of laboratory safety, data integrity, confidentiality and secure release of results.
Commercial awareness, including budget, stock and turnaround-time management.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, laboratory information systems and routine performance reporting.
High personal integrity, sound judgement and a commitment to impartial technical decisions and transparent reporting.
Qualifications
MSc/PhD with minimum 4 years' relevant experience in an ISO17025 accredited laboratory.

Job Description:
Job Description
Turn Your Commercial Experience into Entrepreneurial Impact
Are you a financially astute business professional who understands more than just the numbers?
Perhaps you are a financial analyst, commercial manager, finance leader, business operator or entrepreneur with a strong understanding of how business finance, strategy, sales, and operations work together. You may have reached a point in your career where you are looking for something different: an opportunity to use your experience to guide business owners, develop entrepreneurs and create measurable impact.
If you have run your own business, understand the realities of entrepreneurship and are ready to move from analysing or managing businesses to helping entrepreneurs build stronger ones, this could be the career change you have been looking for.
Raizcorp is looking for a seasoned, well-rounded business professional to join us as a business coach.
This is a full-time, salaried role in which you will coach a portfolio of entrepreneurs across every area of their businesses, including finance, strategy, sales, marketing, operations, people and personal development.
You do not need any previous coaching experience. Raizcorp will train you in our internationally recognised coaching methodology. What you do need is substantial business experience, strong commercial judgement, empathy for entrepreneurs and a genuine desire to help others succeed.
What you’ll do
Hold structured monthly one-on-one coaching sessions with entrepreneurs.
Help business owners interpret their financial information and use it to make better commercial decisions.
Guide entrepreneurs in strengthening their strategies, sales approaches, marketing activities, operational systems and people practices.
Facilitate business simulations and group learning sessions using Raizcorp’s proven programmes and methodology.
Manage a defined portfolio of entrepreneurs and track progress in areas such as revenue, profitability, business capability and founder development.
Challenge entrepreneurs to think critically, evaluate trade-offs and take accountability for their decisions.
Connect the different areas of a business so entrepreneurs can make integrated, forward-looking decisions.
Remain informed about economic conditions, market shifts and regulations that may affect entrepreneurs and their businesses.
Collaborate closely with other coaches and specialists to support each entrepreneur’s development journey.
This role may be a strong fit for you if you are:
A financial analyst or finance professional who has developed a strong understanding of business operations and commercial decision-making.
A commercial or operational leader who wants to use your experience in a more purpose-driven role.
A current or former entrepreneur who understands both the rewards and pressures of building a business.
An experienced business professional looking for a meaningful career change.
Someone who enjoys developing people, asking insightful questions and helping others arrive at better decisions. Empathy in this role is super important.
Motivated by the opportunity to influence real business results rather than simply report on them.
What you’ll need
Between 10 and 15-plus years of experience across corporate, commercial and entrepreneurial environments.
Experience owning or running your own business at some point in your career. This is a non-negotiable requirement.
Strong financial and commercial acumen, with the ability to interpret business performance beyond the income statement.
Experiential depth in business finance, strategy and sales.
A practical understanding of how marketing, operations, people and finance influence one another.
The ability to identify patterns, challenge assumptions and help entrepreneurs evaluate business trade-offs.
High emotional intelligence and genuine empathy for the realities of entrepreneurship.
A mature, accountable and non-judgemental approach.
Strong communication and facilitation skills.
An organised, systematic and proactive working style.
Confidence using technology and business systems, including Microsoft 365 or Microsoft Office and learner management systems.
A commerce-related tertiary qualification. An MBA or other master’s-level qualification will be an advantage.
A valid driver’s licence and your own vehicle.
What you’ll gain
The opportunity to turn years of commercial and entrepreneurial experience into meaningful impact.
A career in which you work directly with entrepreneurs and their businesses every day.
Formal training in an internationally recognised business-coaching methodology.
Continuous professional development and exposure to businesses across different industries and stages of growth.
The opportunity to influence revenue, profitability, founder capability and long-term business sustainability.
A supportive, fiercely caring team culture that backs the jockey—the entrepreneur—not only the horse.
A rare opportunity to build a new career without leaving the world of business behind.

Job Description
We are looking for a sharp, versatile content professional who can research and write exceptionally well and design learning content beautifully.
This role is ideal for someone who sits at the intersection of research, writing, learning, Content development and design — whether your background is in copywriting, content development, graphic design, instructional design, or a related field. What matters most is that you can take complex ideas, shape them into clear learning content, and present them in a way that is engaging, intelligent, polished and effective for the target audience.
You will help us create and improve learning material used in online, virtual and in-person learning environments. This includes everything from slide decks, workbooks and facilitator material to digital learning elements, filmed products and platform-based content.
We need someone who is both conceptually strong and creatively capable — someone who can think clearly, write with precision, structure learning effectively, and produce content that looks professional and lands well with the audience.
What you will do
Develop, update and maintain learning content and learning elements for a wide range of Raizcorp programmes and interventions
Research newly assigned topics, subjects, or concepts, and develop a structured learning framework and key concepts for them.
Create content for both virtual and face-to-face learning experiences
Write, edit and refine learning material so that it is Effective, clear, engaging and aligned to purpose
Design and format learning content so that it is visually strong, easy to use and professional
Review content developed by others, including internal stakeholders, external service providers and AI-supported outputs
Help maintain and improve instructional design standards, processes and templates
Manage the development flow of learning content, including tracking progress and coordinating with subcontractors where required
Contribute to digital learning content for internal platforms and learning products
Update slide decks, manuals, learning elements and related content assets
Conduct research and contribute fresh ideas to improve the quality and impact of our learning design
Incorporate stakeholder and user feedback into revised content
Support the maintenance of learning dashboards and content development systems
What we are looking for
At least 5 years’ experience in content development, learning design, instructional design, copywriting, editorial work, graphic design, or a related field
Strong academic performance in English at school or tertiary level.
A relevant 3-year qualification in fields such as writing, communications, education, instructional design, graphic design, multimedia design, marketing, language practice, journalism, or similar
Ability to interpret scanned briefs and translate them into appropriate outputs through targeted questioning
A strong portfolio of work that shows your writing ability, thinking ability and design capability
Excellent written English and the ability to write clearly, intelligently and professionally
Strong visual design ability and the ability to create polished, well-structured content
Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office and Adobe Suite
Confidence using AI tools such as ChatGPT to support content development and refinement
A sound understanding of how adults learn, how content should flow, and how to make learning practical and engaging
At least a basic understanding of business and commercial concepts
Strong planning, organisation and deadline management
The kind of person who will do well in this role
You are intellectually strong and enjoy working with ideas
You can take complexity and turn it into something clear
You care about words, structure, flow and presentation
You are creative, but also disciplined and detail-oriented
You can work at pace without losing quality
You are comfortable giving feedback, receiving feedback and improving work collaboratively
You build trust easily and can work well with a range of stakeholders
You take ownership and have a strong standard for what good work looks like
Why this role matters
This role plays an important part in shaping the quality of learning experiences across the business.

Staff Supervision & Shift Management
Coordinate and supervise warehouse and cold-store personnel across the shift.
Plan staffing requirements for normal operations, weekends and public holidays.
Manage staff schedules, attendance, timekeeping and registers.
Monitor staffing costs and ensure wages remain within approved budgets.
Allocate responsibilities and ensure employees perform according to their respective roles.

Identify short-dated stock promptly to reduce wastage.
Verify expiry dates of picked products.
Account for stock wastage and breakages.
Conduct regular spot checks on stock handling and storage practices.
Ensure cold stores remain organised, clean and ready for the following shift.

Ensure cold-store temperatures are maintained between 4°C and 7°C.

Ensure chilled products remain within the required temperature-controlled environment.
Conduct random temperature checks on products after vehicle loading.

Ensure compliance with food safety, quality and hygiene procedures.
Complete all relevant records, reports and documentation accurately and timeously.
Participate in internal audits and ensure corrective actions are implemented.

About the Role
Reporting to the Head of HR and Operations, you will be responsible for developing and maintaining technical competency across Operations, Maintenance and Quality.
You will establish machine-specific technical standards, develop SOPs and training material, provide practical on-the-job training and coaching, assess employee competence and ensure identified technical skills gaps are addressed.
The role will work closely with Production, Maintenance, Engineering and Quality to ensure employees can safely and effectively operate equipment, maintain equipment-care standards and consistently achieve required product quality.

Define technical knowledge and practical competency requirements for critical converting machines and roles.
Develop structured, machine-specific technical training.
Deliver practical on-the-job training and coaching on the manufacturing floor.
Develop theoretical and practical technical assessments.
Assess employees against defined competency standards and formally sign off competence.
Identify competency gaps and coordinate retraining, coaching and reassessment.
Develop and maintain technical skills matrices by machine, employee and shift.
Drive multi-skilling and reduce dependency on individual technical experts.
Facilitate knowledge transfer from experienced operators, artisans, Engineering, Quality and OEMs.
Develop and maintain machine-specific SOPs, technical standards, training material and assessments.
Ensure technical documentation covers machine operation, safety, start-up, shutdown, changeovers, set-up, centre lining and critical operating parameters.
Build operator capability in troubleshooting and structured problem solving.
Develop employee understanding of OEE, availability, performance and quality.
Improve operator capability relating to waste, yield, speed losses and minor stops.
Support root-cause analysis and loss-elimination activities.
Embed 5S and continuous improvement principles.
Develop operator capability in equipment inspection, basic equipment care and autonomous maintenance.
Build capability in first-line fault identification and correct technical escalation.
Use recurring breakdowns and equipment failures to identify technical competency gaps.
Develop operator understanding of product specifications and critical quality requirements.
Build capability in conducting in-process quality checks and identifying defects.
Ensure employees understand how machine settings and process conditions affect finished-product quality.
Use complaints, non-conformances, rejects, rework and recurring quality failures to strengthen technical standards and training.
Minimum Requirements
Relevant technical qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Chemical/Process Engineering or a related manufacturing discipline; or
Recognised trade qualification such as Millwright, Fitter, Electrician or Instrumentation Technician, supported by strong manufacturing experience.
Minimum of 8 years' practical technical or operational manufacturing experience.
Assessor SETA accredited; a moderator accreditation would be an advantage.
Significant hands-on experience within paper/tissue converting operations.
Strong technical understanding of converting machinery, processes, maintenance and quality.
Demonstrated experience in machine operation, set-up, optimisation and troubleshooting.
Ability to practically transfer technical knowledge to employees.
Ability to develop technical assessments and evaluate employee competence.
Strong understanding of how machine settings, equipment condition, maintenance practices and raw-material characteristics affect quality, waste, reliability, speed and output.
Highly Advantageous Experience
Experience across multiple high-speed tissue converting technologies.
Previous experience as a Senior Operator, Technical Specialist, Process professional, Production professional, Engineering professional or Maintenance professional.
Exposure to tissue mill operations and parent-reel quality.
Understanding of tissue characteristics including GSM, moisture, strength, bulk, stretch and reel quality.
Practical experience with LEAN, TPM, WCM or similar operational excellence systems.
Experience working with OEMs on equipment commissioning, optimisation or troubleshooting.
This role would particularly suit an experienced tissue converting professional who has developed deep technical knowledge through hands-on manufacturing experience and now wants to use that expertise to build capability across an operational team.
Formal training experience is not essential. What matters is your ability to understand the equipment, troubleshoot technical problems, establish clear operating standards and ensure employees can demonstrate competence in practice.

Job Description:
The Criminal Fraud Investigator (CFI) is embedded in the Consular Section and works under the direct supervision of the Overseas Criminal Investigator- (OCI). The incumbent conducts sensitive, routine, and complex criminal investigations of counterfeit/forged travel documents, human trafficking, and smuggling, U.S. fugitive extraditions, identity theft, bribery, extortion, conspiracy, misrepresentation, malfeasance, and terrorist travel. To facilitate these investigations, the incumbent builds relationships with contacts of all levels throughout the region to include but not limited to relationships with the respective police forces, immigration agencies, airport security, and prosecutors’ offices, etc. The incumbent is also responsible for working level liaison with U.S. law enforcement agencies and U.S. attorney’s offices throughout the United States and its territories. Incumbent may also manage non-RSO Locally Engaged Staff (LE Staff) when they are involved in supporting criminal investigations within the DSS purview as well as fulfilling interagency requests for investigative support that perpetuate national security interests. Incumbent can also work under the direction of the Senior Regional Security Officer (RSO) with concurrence from the OCI. The CFI is managed by the OCI who is supported by the Overseas Criminal Investigations Division (DS/INV/OCI) in Washington DC.
MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
The incumbent will develop and execute anti-fraud training programs for authorities in their Area of Responsibility (AOR) and internal staff. These trainings will include investigative techniques that support the above listed criminal investigations. Incumbent may have national responsibilities beyond their post’s AOR, and this may include supporting investigations and trainings regionally with OCI approval.
Criminal Investigations - Required to conduct sensitive, routine, and complex criminal investigations which will primarily focus on consular cases involving counterfeit/forged documents, human trafficking and smuggling, terrorism, identity theft, bribery, extortion, conspiracy, misrepresentation, and malfeasance. At the direction of the OCI, the incumbent may also assist with FBI, DEA, USMS, USSS, or other U.S. law enforcement agency investigations. Some investigations may require the incumbent to travel, either with the OCI or independently while investigating leads. The incumbent will track investigative activity in a case tracking system and will be responsible for completing detailed and timely written reports on his/her investigations. Incumbent will brief the RSO, Consular Chief, OCI and Fraud Prevention Manager on the status and outcome of his/her investigations. Incumbent will coordinate with the Fraud Prevention Unit to conduct research of criminal organizations who traffic in documents for the purpose of alien smuggling and trafficking. The incumbent’s investigations will influence a decision to arrest, detain, or criminally prosecute an individual under U.S. or local criminal law. As part of the incumbent’s casework, he/she will be required to conduct professional, independent, and/or joint subject interviews with the U.S. law enforcement representatives. The incumbent will assist in ensuring that all official reports of investigation and evidence is transferred to host government or other foreign law enforcement authorities to aide in criminal prosecution, while following Department policies for releasing visa and other controlled information as directed under 9 FAM, 12 FAM, and U.S. law. The incumbent may also be required to provide testimony in local or U.S. courts for criminal trial purposes.
Training - Incumbent is responsible for researching, developing, and presenting training materials related to DSS’ criminal investigations program and post’s anti-fraud efforts, covering topics that include but are not limited to regional/global fraud trends, fraudulent document identification, document security features, impostor detection, human trafficking, foreign terrorist fighter travel, irregular migration, etc.
Liaison -The incumbent will be required to establish and maintain professional relationships throughout all levels of host-nation law enforcement agencies, host-nation immigration and airport authorities, prosecutors and various other government entities and the private sector as appropriate.
Administration and Analysis- The incumbent will monitor local open sources and law enforcement reporting to collect criminal intelligence for the development of investigations and training programs. The incumbent will be required to independently manage and maintain all program equipment and assets, to include assistance in procurement requests for training materials and travel.
Qualifications and Evaluations
Requirements:
All selected candidates must be able to obtain and hold a:
Public Trust security clearance.
All selected candidates will be subject to a background investigation and may be subject to a pre-employment medical exam.
Selected candidate must be able to begin working within a reasonable period of time 12 weeks upon receipt of agency authorization and/or clearances/certifications or their candidacy may end.
Education Requirements:
FOR THE EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS APPLICANTS MUST MEET EITHER OPTION 1 OR OPTION 2 TO QUALIFY.
Experience:
Option 1:
A minimum of five (5) years working in a professional capacity in a related criminal or investigative field within the local government or experience working in conjunction with the U.S. or government in the field(s) of criminal justice, security, or administrative investigations, or court processes with emphasis on technical, analytical or procedural investigations and/or applied operations with a concept of needs focused on identification, interception, interruption, or denial of criminal activities is required.
Option 2:
A minimum of eight (8) years of relevant professional experience as listed in Option 1.
Education:
Option 1:
Completion of a Bachelor’s Degree from a recognized university in any of the following fields: Law, Law Enforcement, Security, International Relations, Politics, or Criminal Justice and Forensics is required.
Option 2:
Completion of Secondary School education.
Job Knowledge:
A good working knowledge of documentary sources of information and familiarity with pertinent local laws such as invasion of privacy, marriage, divorce, etc. is necessary.
Knowledge about criminal activities and modus operandi of criminal organizations within the AOR.
The work requires a comprehensive command of local criminal law, judicial proceedings, analytical and legal research, as well as the ability to produce reports of investigations based on investigative efforts.
The incumbent must be able to rapidly coordinate large scale, high profile investigations for both host nation and U.S. law enforcement and maintain a cadre of key contacts with a like interest in program goals.
Basic knowledge of U.S. travel document concerns, objective ideas in respect to the overall fraud trends, methods, and strategies in visa and passport fraud.
Skills And Abilities:
Critical and independent thinker; self-starter, strong interpersonal skills, and the ability to work as a team toward a common goal.
Strong computer skills, (word processing, spreadsheet management, presentations software) are required.
Incumbent will use analytical computer software such as i2 link analysis, or open source internet investigative tools to secure digital evidence and should be able to manipulate data exports from DOS databases for analytical review/import.
Must have skills to speak in public and do public presentations on a regular basis.
The incumbent must be able to write detailed and accurate reports in English that require little to no correction.

Job Description:
Description
If you believe that “good enough” never is, that a swab result can tell a whole story, and that great quality is built on habits, checklists and the occasional well-timed audit — you may have just found your next move.
The Role (or your chance to keep Montego’s promise on every plate)
As our Quality Assurance Coordinator, you’ll be the trusted right hand to the SHEQ Manager, making sure our food safety and quality assurance standards aren’t just written down — they’re lived, every shift. From sampling and lab results to internal audits and corrective action, you’ll keep our standards sharp and our records watertight.
You’ll also lead a small team, train the wider floor on getting it right first time, and be the calm, methodical presence when a customer complaint or a mock recall needs proper investigation. Based across Graaff-Reinet (Dry & Treats) and Centurion, you’ll help make “Better Every Day” a measurable, provable thing.
What you’ll be doing (besides being brilliant)
Quality Control
Complete swabs and samples per the sampling schedule — hand, surface, air plates and water — and send them to the external lab for testing
Work with the SHEQ Manager to identify corrective action for results outside range, implement it (training, water treatment, cleaning) and take follow-up samples to prove it worked
Complete all required water samples, including full SANS 241 analysis, and submit to the external lab
Make sure the Quality Controller’s checks are done on time and submitted correctly
Send raw-material samples that fail internal micro testing to the external lab for retesting, along with any tests requested by the Nutrition & Development Specialist
Calibrate relevant equipment, keep the Master Calibration Sheet current and coordinate recalibration where needed
Administration
Verify the accurate completion of checklists and documents — cleaning checklists, water activity and moisture forms, and production pack information (with the Production Assistant)
Deliver training such as Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) and pest control, set the assessments, and keep attendance and results on record
Train Quality Controllers on the right checklists and documentation
Draft and update checklists and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and communicate changes to stakeholders with records kept
Inspect product return categories and verify the Returns Inspection Form and capture wastage on the relevant waste stream.
Lead customer complaint investigations — contacting customers, liaising with Engineering, Production and the Veterinary Surgeon, and feeding lab analyses through to Customer Service
Run and maintain internal audit schedules, report findings to the HOD and SHEQ Manager, capture them on the Master Gap List and follow up on corrective action with evidence before closing
Support the QA team during food safety incidents and mock recalls and actively participate in external audits
Raise Purchase Requisitions (PRs) for consumables, chemicals, reagents and supplier calibrations
Investigate non-conformances, gather physical evidence and draft reports with recommendations for the SHEQ Manager
People Management
Manage the attendance and performance of your team against expected standards
Offer day-to-day guidance and support — and, where needed, appropriate disciplinary action
Grow your people through on-the-job training and honest feedback
Play your part in interviewing, selecting and appointing new team members
Hold regular meetings and keep communication open and ongoing
Approve team leave and manage overtime where applicable
Live and demonstrate the Company Culture, bringing its six themes into the workplace
Hygiene, Housekeeping & Health and Safety
Adhere to Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and Food Safety (FSSC 22000) standards
Identify hazards, put corrective and preventative measures in place, and report risks to Management
Keep to personal hygiene standards and maintain a clean, tidy work area at all times
Lend a hand with cleaning across areas during shutdown and maintenance
Requirements
What you’ll need to bring
A Certificate or Diploma in Food Safety or Quality Assurance, or equivalent (NQF Level 5 or 6)
A Degree in Food Safety or Quality Assurance, or equivalent (NQF Level 7) — advantageous
3 years of quality assurance experience in a food manufacturing environment
A valid Code B driver’s licence, and certification as an internal Auditor — advantageous
Proficiency in MS Office and confidence drawing samples and swabs
Sound knowledge of food safety standards, GMP training and assessment, internal audit processes and internal and external lab tests
Skills that make things happen
Proficiency in MS Office
Drawing of samples and swabs
Clear communication and time management
Facilitation, training and assessment
Monitoring and problem-solving
And the behaviours that make it stick
Meticulous attention to detail and accuracy
Calm and effective under pressure
Flexible and adaptable
Methodical, with a healthy suspicion of “good enough”

Job Description:
Role Overview
Provide end-to-end commercial and administrative support across Purchase Order (PO) activity and transporter (road/rail haulage) administration contracts, performance monitoring, weight/mass reconciliation, and general commercial admin ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant transactions between the mine/commercial team, suppliers, and transporters.
This role sits at the intersection of procurement admin and logistics/contract admin, so the ideal candidate needs strong numerical accuracy, systems literacy, and the discipline to manage recurring reconciliations without errors slipping through.
Key Responsibility Areas
Purchase Order (PO) Administration
Raise, amend, and close POs on the SAP/procurement system
Match POs to supplier quotes, contracts, and delivery notes
Follow up on outstanding/overdue POs with suppliers and internal stakeholders
Reconcile PO values against invoices (3-way match: PO – GRN – Invoice)
Resolve PO/invoice discrepancies (price, quantity, tax) with procurement/finance
Maintain PO tracking register/dashboard (open, closed, overdue, value)
Support month-end PO accrual reporting
Transporter Contract & Performance Administration
Maintain and file all transporter contracts (SLAs, rate schedules, validity periods)
Track contract renewal dates and flag expiries in advance
Monitor transporter performance against agreed KPIs (on-time delivery, turnaround time, breakdown/downtime, complaints, accident/incident rate)
Compile weekly/monthly transporter scorecards
Log and follow up on non-conformances or penalty clauses (demurrage, late delivery penalties)
Coordinate performance review meetings with transporters and commercial/logistics management
Support tender/rate negotiation admin (rate comparison sheets, historic performance input)
Weight/Mass Reconciliation ("Weight Difference")
Capture weighbridge (loading point) vs destination (offloading point) mass
Calculate weight variances (loss/gain) per load, per transporter, per route
Apply moisture/quality adjustment factors where relevant
Raise claims/debit notes against transporters for out-of-tolerance shortages
Maintain a weight variance log/trend report by transporter and route
General Admin Support
Filing and document control (contracts, PODs, weighbridge tickets, certificates)
Data entry and record maintenance across systems/spreadsheets
Preparing routine reports for the commercial/logistics team
Ad hoc support tasks as assigned (BEE , Credit application)
Detailed Task List
Raise, amend, and close Purchase Orders (POs).
Match POs, Goods Received Notes (GRNs), and invoices, and flag any differences.
Follow up on outstanding POs and prepare aging reports.
Capture weighbridge information and compare loads against destination weights.
Calculate and report weight variances by transporter and route.
Raise shortage claims and debit notes when required.
Maintain and update the transporter contract register.
Monitor contract expiry dates and send renewal alerts.
Prepare transporter performance scorecards and track KPIs.
Attend transporter review meetings and record minutes and action items.
Assist with month-end PO accruals and prepare accrual schedules.
Maintain proper filing and document control for contracts, POs, and related documents.
Prepare ad hoc reports and summaries for management.
Core Competencies & Skills Required
Technical
Strong numerical/analytical ability (percentages, ratios, variance calculations)
Advanced Excel (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, pivot tables, IF/SUMIFS, basic dashboards)
SAP/procurement system exposure (SAP)
Understanding of basic contract terms (SLAs, penalty clauses, Incoterms is a plus)
Basic understanding of coal logistics (weighbridge processes, moisture content, tonnage, rail vs road haulage)
Behavioural
High attention to detail and accuracy under repetitive workload
Strong follow-up discipline and deadline management
Assertive but professional communication (chasing suppliers/transporters)
Comfortable escalating issues without being confrontational
Organized, methodical, good document control habits
KPIs / Performance Measures
% of POs processed within SLA (e.g., 48 hours)
PO/invoice match accuracy rate
Weight variance reporting turnaround (same day/next day)
Number of unresolved weight variance claims older than 30 days
Contract renewal alerts issued (100% before expiry, e.g., 60 days prior)
Transporter scorecards delivered on time (monthly)
Error/rework rate on reconciliations
6- 2 Year Succession & Development Plan
Year 1 – Foundation & Competence
Focus: Master the core admin, build systems fluency, establish accuracy and consistency.
Full onboarding on ERP/PO system and weighbridge/reconciliation process
Shadow senior staff on transporter contract reviews for first quarter
Complete internal Excel/data accuracy training
Independently manage full PO cycle and daily weight reconciliation by month 6
Begin compiling monthly transporter scorecards unsupervised by month 9
Milestone review at 12 months: competency sign-off on PO admin, weight reconciliation, and basic contract administration
Year 2 – Growth & Ownership
Focus: Take ownership of transporter relationship admin and start analytical contribution.
Lead transporter performance review meetings (with management oversight)
Take primary responsibility for contract renewal tracking and rate negotiation support
Introduce/refine variance trend dashboards (moving from manual to automated reporting)
Cross-train on adjacent function (e.g., basic procurement sourcing or logistics scheduling)
Contract Management Fundamentals / Commercial Acumen for Non-Commercial Roles
Milestone review at 24 months: demonstrated ability to manage transporter relationships and identify cost/variance-saving opportunities

Job Description:
Introduction
Lead the development, approval and continuous improvement of Private Label packaging across assigned categories, ensuring it is consumer-focused, commercially viable, fit for purpose, compliant, quality assured and aligned with Clicks sustainability objectives.
Provide technical leadership across the packaging value chain, strengthen supplier performance, deliver cost and sustainability benefits, and develop junior packaging capability.
Job description
Job Objectives:
Packaging Development and Innovation
Lead the development and improvement of primary, secondary and tertiary packaging across assigned Private Label categories.
Translate commercial, brand, consumer, product-protection, supply-chain and sustainability requirements into technically viable briefs and specifications.
Evaluate packaging formats, materials, components, inks and print technologies to improve functionality, quality, sustainability, lead time or cost.
Drive packaging milestones from approved brief to commercial launch by coordinating approvals and supplier deliverables, resolving delays and escalating launch risks.
Provide technical guidance to New Product Development Buyers, Category Buyers, Brand, Product Developers, Designers and Technologists.
Technical Quality, Specifications and Compliance
Define, review and approve packaging specifications, artwork requirements, proofs, print standards, production trials and technical testing before release.
Manage online print approvals and verify colour consistency against approved Private Label brand standards across proofs, press outputs and production batches.
Ensure packaging is fit for purpose, protects product integrity and meets applicable legal, labelling, environmental, internal and quality requirements.
Maintain controlled packaging specifications, approvals and test records; investigate non-conformances, lead root-cause analysis and verify corrective action.
Apply risk-based food-contact, packaging-quality, Good Manufacturing Practice and GS1 requirements appropriate to the product and packaging application.
Sustainability and Extended Producer Responsibility
Implement the Clicks packaging strategy and integrate sustainability requirements into new and existing developments.
Drive design for recycling, material reduction, packaging elimination, reuse and responsible recycled-content opportunities without compromising safety, quality or performance.
Support applicable South African Plastics Pact and internal circularity targets.
Maintain accurate packaging composition and volume data for Extended Producer Responsibility reporting and assess changes against applicable requirements and the national Recyclability by Design guideline.
Commercial and Supplier Management
Source, assess and approve packaging suppliers and printers within delegated authority based on technical capability, quality, compliance, capacity, service and commercial criteria.
Maintain approved-supplier records and scorecards, conduct risk-based assessments or audits, and ensure contract manufacturers use approved sources unless an authorised alternative is agreed.
Lead technical and commercial negotiations, including packaging rebate arrangements, and ensure agreed terms are documented, accurately calculated and realised.
Manage technical relationships with artwork agencies, printers, converters, packaging manufacturers and laboratories.
Deliver value-engineering opportunities that improve cost, quality, availability or supply resilience.
Project and Stakeholder Leadership
Govern concurrent packaging workstreams, ensuring clear ownership, dependencies, decision points and progress control from briefing to launch.
Report progress, risks, decisions and actions to relevant stakeholders and facilitate alignment among internal teams, contract manufacturers, suppliers, printers and artwork agencies.
Escalate unresolved technical, compliance, quality, cost or timeline risks with an evidence-based recommendation.
People Leadership and Capability Development
Prioritise and review work for the Junior Packaging Technologist and/or Regulatory Packaging Technologist, setting clear objectives, timelines and quality expectations.
Provide coaching, technical guidance and performance feedback, and promote consistent methods, templates, specifications and lessons learned across the Private Label technical team.
Key Success Measures
At least 95% of agreed packaging critical-path milestones are achieved by their approved dates, with no packaging-driven launch delay unless formally accepted through change control.
Specifications, artwork, proofs, trials and approvals are completed to agreed turnaround times, and packaging readiness is confirmed before the production or launch gate.
Critical-path risks and forecast delays are recorded, communicated and escalated with an agreed recovery action and accountable owner.
At least 95% of online print approvals are completed within the agreed turnaround time, with colour references and decisions recorded before production release.
At least 98% of production print samples meet the approved Private Label brand colour standard on first assessment. Contract manufacturers must contain and report material deviations within one working day, with corrective action and re-approval completed before production resumes or stock is released.
Packaging specifications and technical records remain current and controlled, while defects, repeat failures and avoidable rework are reduced.
Approved cost, value-engineering, sustainability and design-for-recycling objectives are achieved without compromising compliance or quality.

Job Description:
We're looking for an experienced Senior Sales Operations Manager to help scale our GTM processes and systems vision, lead GTM enablement, build our commercial librarian function, and serve as the central point of cross-functional gravity between Commercial Operations, Product Management, and Business Operations. You'll report to the Global Head of Commercial Operations and Deal Desk, and you'll have real latitude to shape how this function grows.
What you'll own
The Opportunity Lifecycle, end-to-end. You'll own the stages, activities, statuses and system interface of our opportunity lifecycle across our full product portfolio, every transaction type, and every route-to-market. If it touches how a deal moves from first identification to closed-won, you'll help design and envision how it evolves operationally to enable greater intuitiveness and scale.
Our systems vision. You'll support the systems strategy underpinning our commercial target operating model — helping translate "how we want to sell" into "how the platform actually works" across the entire opportunity lifecycle.
Enablement and adoption across GTM. You'll lead the learning, enablement and adoption of systems, operations and processes across GTM — turning new processes into habits people use, not just policies they tolerate.
The central librarian function. You'll build out our central "librarian" function: the curated home for commercial and knowledge artefacts across GTM, so the right playbook, template or precedent is always one search away, not buried in someone's inbox.
Cross-functional alignment. You'll be the connective tissue between GTM, Commercial Operations, and key business partners — especially Product Management and Business Operations — ensuring decisions in one function don't quietly break another.
Qualification and Experience
Education: Minimum of a bachelor's degree in business administration or a closely related professional discipline.
Solid experience, minimum of 7 years, in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or Commercial Operations, ideally within a B2B SaaS, financial services, or professional/fund services environment
Hands-on comfort with CRM/CPQ platforms (Salesforce strongly preferred) and a genuine interest in how business operations should be designed and how systems should operate to deliver effective outcomes
Experience designing or evolving opportunity/pipeline stages, qualification methodology, or deal governance frameworks
A track record of building enablement or training programmes that move adoption, not just tick a compliance box
Strong instincts for information architecture — you like things organised, findable, and current
Confidence operating cross-functionally with Product Management and Business Operations stakeholders, including when priorities compete
Comfort with ambiguity — you'll be helping define parts of this role as you go, not following a fixed playbook
What will make you thrive here
You are a team player, someone who is excited to form a vision, share it, and influence others to go on that journey with you
You enjoy building things from scratch more than maintaining what already exists
You think in processes and systems, but you never lose sight of the impact these will have on the underlying end-user community
You're a natural connector — cross-functional friction doesn't frustrate you; it energises you
You want to grow into a broader Rev Ops leadership remit as this function scales

Job Description:
Picture yourself brightening someone’s day. When you join our Hotels team, that’s exactly what you’ll do every time you come to work! As a Reservations Supervisor, you’re not just supervising daily reservations operations – you’re spreading the light and warmth of hospitality by delivering memorable experiences that make the stay for every guest.
Here's what you'll do during a typical day:
Groups/Events
Own the end-to-end group reservations process, from initial block set-up through to rooming list management, amendments, and final departure reconciliation.
Responsible for preparing and finalizing all Group Resumes, ensuring that accurate and complete operational details are handed over to the Operations Team.
Liaise closely with the Sales, Events, and Commercial teams to ensure group blocks are accurately loaded, tracked, and updated in line with contracted terms and cut-off dates.
Manage group inventory and rooming lists with a high level of accuracy, proactively flagging pick-up risk, attrition, or contractual discrepancies.
Act as the key point of contact for group bookers and travel partners on reservations-related queries, ensuring a smooth and professional guest journey from booking through to arrival.
Coordinate meetings, conferences and events, acting as the main client contact.
Liaise with clients on menus, timings, setups, equipment and special requests.
Prepare and issue Event Orders, ensuring accurate communication to relevant teams.
Coordinate with Food & Beverage and Operations to ensure smooth event delivery.
Follow up on final requirements and communicate any changes promptly.
Manage and confirm final client payments, ensuring accurate records and handover.
Production
Build and maintain relationships with film, television and content production companies, production houses, agencies and location partners, positioning the hotel as a preferred accommodation partner.
Identify and convert accommodation opportunities across cast, crew, technical teams and production executives, with particular focus on extended stays and project-based business.
Track upcoming Film & TV productions and filming activity in Cape Town, proactively targeting opportunities and building a strong production pipeline.
Work closely with the wider commercial team on production-specific rates, contracting and account strategies to grow this segment and secure repeat business.
Internal Processes
Own and continuously refine reservations SOPs, ensuring the team's PMS and CRS workflows are accurate, efficient, and aligned to Hilton brand standards.
Lead on training and onboarding of reservations agents on process, systems, and quality standards.
Conduct regular quality checks on reservations accuracy (rate loading, guest profiles, special requests, billing instructions) to minimize revenue leakage and guest-experience errors.
Identify and implement process improvements that reduce manual work and improve accuracy across the reservations function.
Team & Commercial Support
Provide day-to-day supervision and support to reservations agents, stepping in on complex or escalated bookings as needed.
Act as a key link between Reservations and the Commercial team, ensuring group and production data flows cleanly into wider commercial decision-making, including RFP and rate strategy conversations.
Skills & Experience Required
Essential
Minimum 2–3 years' experience in a hotel reservations environment, with direct exposure to group bookings and block management.
Proven experience with a hotel PMS and CRS (OnQ / OnQ Revenue & Inventory / PEP or equivalent Hilton systems strongly preferred; Opera experience also relevant). Strong working knowledge of GDS booking channels and OTA extranets.
Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and the ability to build and maintain clean production and pace reports.
Solid grasp of core hospitality revenue concepts, including ADR, RevPAR, occupancy, and pace, sufficient to interpret and contribute to production reporting.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to liaise directly with travel partners, group bookers, and senior stakeholders.
Personal Attributes
Locally curious and personality-driven, in keeping with the Canopy brand ethos, with genuine pride in representing the Longkloof neighbourhood to guests.
Organised and process-minded, but comfortable adapting quickly when group or production needs shift.
A natural collaborator, equally comfortable working closely with the Reservations Manager on daily operations and with the Commercial Director on production insight.
Reporting Line
This role reports directly to the Reservations Manager for day-to-day operations, workflow, and people management. Given the strategic weight of the Groups and Production elements of the role, a dotted line runs into the Commercial Director, ensuring production insight, group performance, and process improvements are visible at a commercial leadership level and feed directly into the hotel's broader revenue and sales strategy.
It would be advantageous in this position for you to demonstrate the following capabilities and distinctions:
Knowledge of the hotel property management systems
Previous experience in the Reservations/Sales function within the hotel/leisure sector
Relevant degree or other qualification in a business discipline

Company Details: The South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) is an agency of the Department of Transport (DoT), established on 01 October 1998, following the enactment of the now repealed South African Civil Aviation Authority Act, 1998 (Act No. 40 of 1998). This Act was replaced by the Civil Aviation Act,...read more2009 (Act No. 13 of 2009), which came into effect on 31 March 2010. As outlined in the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA), 1999 (Act No. 1 of 1999) (as amended by Act No. 29 of 1999), the SACAA is a Schedule 3A public entity. The PFMA designates the SACAAs Board of Directors as the organisations Accounting Authority responsible for governance, while the Minister of Transport is the Executive Authority. The Civil Aviation Act provides for the establishment of a stand-alone authority, mandated with controlling, promoting, regulating, supporting, developing, enforcing, and continuously improving levels of safety and security throughout the civil aviation industry. The Industrial Engineer drives operational efficiency and productivity across the quick-service restaurant (QSR) network by applying industrial engineering principles to optimise processes, labour deployment and capacity planning.
The role analyses workflow, service times and resource utilisation to design and implement standardised operating procedures, reduce waste, and improve throughput, cost and customer experience across restaurant operations.

Stakeholder collaboration & training – partner with operations teams to roll out new standards and train store teams on optimised processes.

A minimum of 2–3 years' experience as an Industrial Engineer, preferably within a quick-service restaurant (QSR), retail, hospitality or other high-volume operations environment.
Demonstrated experience in process optimisation, work study, labour and capacity modelling, and continuous improvement (Lean / Six Sigma).
Practical experience managing improvement projects end-to-end and partnering with operational stakeholders to implement and sustain change.
Bachelor's Degree – BEng / BSc (Eng), NQF Level 7 (required)
Lean Six Sigma certification – Green or Black Belt (advantageous)
Project Management certification (advantageous)
Experience with Industrial engineering principles, methods and tools , time-and-motion and work-measurement techniques, and workforce/demand modelling, Process mapping, simulation and layout design.

Experience with Health, safety and food-safety standards (advantageous)

Communicate with the unit manager, so that he / she is informed of activities and problems

Provide input and standards in formulating patient care policy and procedures in the hospital
To ensure the provision of a safe, clean and secure environment for patients, staff and visitors.

Garden Route National Park

NQF Level 8 in Environmental Management, Conservation Biology, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science or equivalent relevant qualification.
Minimum 6–8 years’ relevant experience in conservation management, protected area planning, environmental compliance or biodiversity governance.
Demonstrated experience in management effectiveness assessments (e.g., METT/METTS).
Experience coordinating reporting linked to international environmental conventions (e.g., UNESCO, RAMSAR, MPA governance).
Experience working within conservation agencies, environmental public sector or protected area systems.
Valid Driver License, own vehicle position involves extensive travel.
Must be physically fit.
Knowledge & Skills Required
Strategic coordination and systems oversight.
Conservation governance and compliance management.
Environmental reporting and policy interpretation.
Stakeholder engagement with national departments and global bodies.
Analytical thinking and synthesis of multi-park data.
Planning, organising and multi-stakeholder coordination.

Master’s degree in environmental management, Conservation Planning, Marine or Biodiversity Science, or related field.
Postgraduate qualification in Environmental Law, Compliance or Protected Area Management.
Certification in Monitoring & Evaluation or Environmental Impact / Compliance Auditing.
Responsibilities
Forward Planning, Strategic Alignment and System Integration (Parks Division)
Lead and direct forward planning to ensure proactive alignment of conservation planning, compliance and reporting priorities across the Parks Division.
Provide strategic oversight and direction through structured engagement with all national parks to proactively identify, prioritise, and address emerging conservation planning, management effectiveness, and compliance risks and opportunities.
Develop an integrated annual and medium-term work programme for conservation planning, international reporting and management effectiveness across parks.
Ensure alignment between Park Management Plans, divisional priorities, and SANParks strategic conservation objectives.
Identify systemic risks, capacity gaps and priority interventions affecting implementation of conservation mandates across parks.
Provide strategic guidance to parks on planning reviews, international obligations and compliance readiness.
Conservation Planning and Management Effectiveness Oversight
Drive and oversee a coordinated, organisation-wide approach to assessing Park Management Plan implementation, enabling informed strategic decision-making and continuous improvement.
Lead the consolidation and strategic interpretation of evaluation outcomes, ensuring annual summary reports and provide clear governance assurance to divisional and executive structures.
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of management effectiveness assessments, including METT/METTS processes, across the Parks Division.
Lead the tracking and monitoring of corrective actions arising from assessments, audits and internal reviews.
Establish a standardised divisional system to monitor implementation progress against approved conservation plans.
Conservation Compliance and Standards Assurance Across Parks
Develop and institutionalise conservation standards, compliance tracking and assurance mechanisms across the Parks Division.
Ensure adherence to environmental legislation, policies, biodiversity governance requirements and approved management plans.
Drive the identification, escalation, and resolution of systemic compliance risks across the SANParks estate through targeted corrective interventions.
Provide consolidated executive assurance reporting on conservation compliance and standards implementation across SANParks parks.
International Conservation Obligations and Heritage Site Reporting
Drive a standardised approach to annual assessments and reporting for SANParks-managed World Heritage Sites, including Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape, Khomani Cultural Landscape and other identified key sites.
Develop and oversee the coordination of consolidated SANParks reporting for parks contributing to the: Cape Floristic Region
Ensure compliance with UNESCO reporting protocols, management effectiveness expectations and periodic review requirements.
Lead and oversee SANParks’ institutional engagement and responses to international information requests and monitoring processes, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and governance assurance.
Wetland (RAMSAR) and Marine Protected Area Governance Coordination
Drive and manage Parks Division engagement with the DFFE RAMSAR Secretariat on wetland reporting and compliance matters. Manage RAMSAR Information Sheet (RIS) updates, requests and formal responses for SANParks-managed sites, including Wilderness Lakes, Langebaan Lagoon, Agulhas Plain Wetlands and other key sites.
Represent Parks Division operations in national marine and estuarine governance structures, including Working Group 7 (Marine & Estuarine) and National Coastal Committee.
Lead and direct coordinated strategic input into national MPA and coastal governance frameworks on behalf of SANParks, parks division.
MPA & Estuarine Conservation Planning Integration Across Parks
Represent Parks Operations in development and review of Marine Protected Area and Estuarine Management Plans across relevant national parks.
Integrate planning inputs between Park Planning, Scientific Services and park management teams.
Ensure marine and estuarine plans align with biodiversity priorities, legislative requirements and international conservation best practice.
Lead the monitoring of implementation progress and support adaptive management reviews across the Parks Division.
