Job Description:
A growing digital agency based in Port Elizabeth builds and maintains a portfolio of web-based products for a range of clients. The team operates lean, moves quickly and gives developers the opportunity to become genuinely involved in the projects they work on.
This is an entry-level opportunity for someone with exceptional potential rather than an established developer with years of experience. The client is looking for that rare individual who is naturally curious, technically minded and able to learn quickly. You may be self-taught, recently qualified or still building your commercial experience. What matters most is that you can demonstrate an aptitude for development, a genuine interest in technology and the determination to work through problems rather than waiting for someone else to provide the answer.
You will initially work alongside experienced team members, learning the existing systems, assisting with maintenance and developing your technical capability. As your knowledge and confidence grow, you will be given increasing responsibility for projects and features of your own.
The salary will start between R10,000 and R15,000 per month, based on your current ability. The company follows a straightforward performance-based growth model: the faster you learn, contribute and make yourself valuable to the business, the sooner you can be considered for increased responsibility and salary progression.
What’s in it for you
An opportunity to begin or accelerate your career in software development
Direct guidance and practical exposure to experienced developers
The chance to work on live web-based products rather than only internal training exercises
Increasing project responsibility as your skills develop
Exposure to Ruby on Rails, relational databases and modern web-development practices
Experience using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude and Codex
A clear path toward becoming an independent developer and, over time, progressing into a senior or technical leadership role
A stable, office-based working environment in Port Elizabeth
Salary growth linked to learning, contribution and the value you bring to the team
Minimum Requirements
Matric certificate
Valid driver’s licence
Some practical exposure to software or web development
A basic understanding of programming concepts and how web applications work
Evidence of genuine interest in development, such as personal projects, coursework, freelance work, GitHub repositories or applications you have built
The ability and willingness to learn Ruby on Rails
A basic understanding of databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL or another relational database would be advantageous
Comfortable using AI development tools while still reading, questioning and understanding the code they generate
Strong problem-solving ability and willingness to research solutions independently
Able to accept feedback, apply what has been taught and avoid repeatedly requiring guidance on the same issue
Reliable, responsible and willing to take ownership of assigned work
A completed university qualification is not required. Candidates who started but did not complete a degree or diploma will still be considered, provided they have Matric, a valid driver’s licence and can demonstrate the aptitude and commitment required for the position.
Key Responsibilities
Learning the company’s existing systems, development standards and project workflows
Supporting the maintenance of existing web-based projects
Assisting with bug fixes, testing and smaller development tasks during the initial learning period
Building and updating website features, administrative systems and back-end functionality
Working with Ruby on Rails, PostgreSQL and related web technologies
Reading and reviewing existing code to understand how applications have been structured
Using AI-assisted development tools responsibly and reviewing generated code critically
Testing work thoroughly before it is submitted or released
Investigating technical problems and attempting practical solutions before escalating
Applying feedback from senior team members and continuously improving the quality of your work
Taking ownership of increasingly complex tasks, features and projects as your capability develops
Maintaining the projects and features assigned to you once you are ready to work more independently
The Type of Person Who Will Succeed
You do not need to know everything when you start, but you must be someone who learns quickly and takes responsibility for your own development. You should enjoy experimenting, researching, asking thoughtful questions and figuring out how things work.
The right person will not use AI simply to produce code they do not understand. You will be expected to read the output, question it, test it and explain what it does. You should be comfortable making mistakes while learning, but equally committed to applying feedback and improving each time.
This opportunity will suit someone who is hungry to build a long-term development career and understands that greater responsibility and salary progression will be earned through demonstrated growth, consistent contribution and increasing value to the business.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The main purpose of the Payroll Accountant role is to oversee payroll operations across multiple countries within Zutari. The focus will be on payroll tasks, processing of payroll-related journals, preparation of payroll-related accruals, provisions and reconciliations.
The Payroll Accountant will support the Payroll Analyst in ensuring accurate and timely payroll processing and general ledger accounting. The Payroll Accountant role requires knowledge of accounting treatment of various transactions and reconciliations.
The role has direct impact on financial reporting accuracy, audit readiness, compliance, and the integrity of payroll-related general ledger balances. Whilst this role does not have any direct reports it has a requirement to be able to operate independently and as such a high level of accountability is required
Role responsibilities
General Ledger Accounting for Payroll:
Prepare, review, and post payroll-related journal entries accurately and within agreed reporting timelines.
Ensure payroll costs, employer contributions, deductions, provisions, and liabilities are correctly allocated to the general ledger.
Maintain the integrity of payroll-related general ledger accounts through accurate classification, coding, and posting.
Verify that payroll outputs are correctly translated into accounting entries and reflected in the financial records.
Payroll Balance Sheet Reconciliations:
Prepare and review reconciliations for all payroll-related balance sheet accounts, including salaries control accounts, statutory liabilities, benefit deductions, payroll clearing accounts, leave provisions, bonus accruals, and other payroll-related provisions.
Investigate reconciling items, unusual balances, and aged items and ensure timeous resolution.
Substantiate payroll-related balances with complete supporting schedules and audit-ready documentation.
Monitor reconciliation quality and escalate unresolved or material items.
Month-End and Year-End Payroll Close:
Coordinate payroll-related month-end close activities to ensure all payroll accounting entries are complete, accurate, and posted on time.
Prepare payroll accruals, provisions, prepayments, and adjustment journals as required for monthly reporting.
Support year-end close activities by preparing final payroll accounting schedules, reconciliations, and supporting working papers.
Ensure payroll-related ledger balances are accurately reflected in financial reporting and year-end audit submissions.
Ledger Alignment and Payroll-to-Finance Interface:
Ensure accurate alignment between payroll system outputs, payroll reports, third-party schedules, and the general ledger.
Statutory and Third-Party Ledger Accountability:
Reconcile statutory deductions, benefit contributions, and third-party payroll liabilities to supporting schedules and ledger balances.
Ensure payroll-related liability accounts are accurately recorded and cleared in line with payment cycles.
Investigate differences between payroll reports, payment schedules, and ledger balances and resolve discrepancies.
Audit and Compliance Support:
Prepare payroll-related audit schedules, reconciliations, journals, and supporting documents for internal and external audit purposes.
Maintain a clear and complete audit trail for all payroll accounting entries and reconciliations.
Respond to payroll accounting queries raised by auditors, finance leadership, and compliance stakeholders.
Analysis and Reporting:
Analyse payroll ledger movements and identify unusual trends, misallocations, or accounting anomalies.
Provide commentary on payroll-related account movements during month-end and year-end reporting cycles.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of payroll accounting reports and management information.
Process Improvement and Systems Support:
Recommend improvements to payroll accounting processes, controls, and ledger reconciliation practices.
Support the documentation and maintenance of payroll accounting procedures, month-end checklists, and reconciliation standards.
Contribute to process standardisation that improves financial accuracy, transparency, and reporting efficiency.

Completed articles - advantageous
Postgraduate qualification in accounting, taxation, or finance will be advantageous

Demonstrated practical experience in:

accruals, provisions, and month-end accounting

Experience working in an integrated ERP, payroll, and HRIS environment

Job Description:
Job Purpose
To ensure effective control, management, accounting, and reporting of the company's fixed assets across all regions nationally. The role is responsible for maintaining the fixed asset register, ensuring compliance with accounting standards and company policies, safeguarding company assets, coordinating asset verification processes, and supporting accurate financial reporting and audit requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Manage and maintain the national fixed asset register by ensuring all asset acquisitions, transfers, disposals, impairments, and retirements are accurately recorded, classified, and supported by the appropriate documentation. Ensure the register remains complete, accurate, and aligned to financial records.
Administer the fixed asset accounting process including asset capitalization, depreciation calculations, useful life reviews, residual value assessments, impairment assessments, and asset disposals in accordance with IFRS, accounting standards, and company policies.
Perform monthly reconciliations between the fixed asset register and the General Ledger, investigating discrepancies, processing corrective entries, and ensuring all balances are accurately reflected in financial reports.
Provide financial control over capital expenditure (CAPEX) by reviewing project expenditure, validating asset capitalization criteria, monitoring project closures, and ensuring approved capital projects are accurately transferred into the fixed asset register upon completion.
Process purchase orders and investment orders within SAP to support the acquisition, capitalization, and management of fixed assets and capital expenditure projects across the business.
Manage CAPEX approval workflows by coordinating the submission, review, routing, and authorization of capital expenditure requests in line with approved budgets, policies, and delegated authority limits.
Monitor and control capital expenditure projects, ensuring that approved CAPEX spending is accurately tracked, recorded, and capitalized upon project completion.
Process weekly supplier payments through SAP, prepare CAPEX payment forecasts, and validate payment runs to ensure timely settlement of supplier obligations while maintaining cash flow visibility and financial control.
Prepare and analyse CAPEX expenditure reports and forecasts, monitoring budget utilization and highlighting potential risks, variances, and overspending to management.
Prepare weekly and monthly Stanfleet reporting, including fuel, repairs, maintenance costs, and related journals, ensuring the accurate recording, allocation, and reconciliation of fleet-related assets and expenses.
Coordinate annual and cyclical asset verification programmes across all operational sites to confirm the existence, location, condition, and ownership of assets. Investigate variances, losses, and unrecorded assets, and recommend corrective actions to management.
Establish and monitor fixed asset control procedures to safeguard company assets, minimize financial risk, improve asset visibility, and ensure compliance with internal control requirements and governance standards.
Prepare and analyse monthly, quarterly, and annual fixed asset reports including depreciation reports, capital expenditure analyses, asset movement schedules, asset ageing reports, and management reporting packs to support business decision-making.
Partner with operational, procurement, engineering, IT, and finance teams to ensure all fixed asset transactions are accurately recorded and that asset-related activities are executed in accordance with approved policies and procedures.
Support budgeting and forecasting processes by providing insights into asset replacement requirements, planned capital investments, depreciation forecasts, and asset lifecycle costs to assist with strategic financial planning.
Lead audit engagements relating to fixed assets by preparing audit schedules, providing supporting documentation, resolving audit queries, and implementing recommendations arising from internal and external audits.
Monitor compliance with accounting standards, statutory requirements, and company policies by conducting regular reviews of asset-related transactions and ensuring consistency in the application of accounting treatments across all business units.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives within the fixed asset management environment by identifying process inefficiencies, implementing automation opportunities, improving reporting capability, and enhancing asset governance and control frameworks.
Provide technical guidance and training to finance and operational teams on fixed asset policies, capitalization principles, asset tracking requirements, and compliance obligations to improve understanding and adherence across the business.
Identify and mitigate asset-related risks by monitoring asset utilisation, reviewing asset performance trends, ensuring timely disposal of redundant assets, and escalating significant control weaknesses or financial risks to management.

Duties and Responsibilities
Accounts Payable

Perform monthly supplier statement reconciliations.
Investigate and resolve supplier queries and discrepancies.
Prepare creditor payment schedules for review and approval.

Monitor outstanding invoices and follow up on missing documentation.
Accounts Receivable
Process and allocate payments accurately.
Maintain debtor accounts and ensure balances are reconciled.

Job Description:
Purpose of Job
Accountable for developing and applying advanced data science, statistical modelling, forecasting and pricing analytics to support Sasol’s Integrated Power portfolio, including generation, demand, market exposure, commercial risk, portfolio optimisation and value creation.
The role develops analytical models, forecasting methodologies, scenario tools and decision-support outputs to improve commercial decision-making across the power portfolio. ETRM enablement, SAWEM readiness support, energy management analytics, Power BI and Aveva PI are positioned as future-facing application areas or enabling toolsets where this capability may be applied; prior exposure to these areas would be advantageous.
The role serves as the specialist analytics interface between Integrated Power, trading, asset management, commercial, finance, digital and operational teams, converting complex generation, load, market, metering, contractual, pricing, financial and risk data into reliable insight, measurable value opportunities and defensible commercial decisions
Key Accountabilities
Advanced Analytics, Statistical Modelling and Decision Support
Develop and maintain statistical models, analytical tools and scenario engines to support Integrated Power decision-making.
Convert generation, demand, market, pricing, metering, contractual, financial and risk data into actionable commercial insight.
Analyse portfolio positions, market exposure, imbalance risk and optimisation opportunities across Sasol’s contracted and future power portfolio.
Develop dashboards, analytical outputs and management reports that support operational, commercial and executive decision-making.
Identify value creation opportunities through improved forecasting, pricing insight, resource allocation and portfolio optimisation.
Forecasting, Pricing Analytics and Portfolio Optimisation
Develop, test and improve load, generation, renewable supply, price and imbalance forecasting methodologies.
Apply pricing analytics to assess market signals, tariff structures, bilateral pricing, imbalance exposure and commercial optimisation options.
Support short-, medium- and long-term portfolio optimisation across internal generation, renewable PPAs, market purchases, customer commitments and future trading positions.
Track forecast accuracy, model performance and variance drivers, and recommend improvements to data, assumptions and methodologies.
Quantify commercial impacts of forecast error, curtailment, constraints, outages, price movements and imbalance positions.
Support the optimal deployment of electrons by providing insight into when, where and how Sasol’s power resources should be contracted, allocated, dispatched or hedged.
ETRM Enablement, SAWEM Readiness and Market Analytics
Data Governance, Performance Measurement and Value Tracking
Establish structured datasets, assumptions registers, model documentation and version control for key analytical outputs.
Maintain data quality checks, exception reporting and governance over analytical inputs and outputs.
Measure performance against forecasts, portfolio strategies, pricing assumptions, optimisation cases and realised commercial outcomes.
Track value creation opportunities, benefits realisation and analytical recommendations implemented by the business.
Support auditability, assurance and governance of models, data sources, assumptions and decision-support outputs.
Stakeholder Collaboration and Capability Building
Work with trading, commercial, asset management, finance, digital, operations and external partners to translate business questions into analytical solutions.
Build internal capability by documenting methodologies, training users and embedding repeatable analytical processes.
Provide analytical input into business cases, investment decisions, contract evaluations and market-readiness activities.
Communicate insights clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders through dashboards, reports, presentations and decision papers.
Reduce dependency on external advisors by developing sustainable internal analytics capability for Integrated Power.
Key Working Interfaces
Integrated Power business building, asset management, supply chain, information management, commercial, trading and portfolio management teams.
Finance, risk, legal, assurance and internal control functions requiring analytical input, commercial insight and governance over assumptions.
Digital, data, ETRM, metering, forecasting, Aveva PI, Power BI, energy management and reporting teams responsible for data integration, model enablement and system implementation.
Generators, IPPs, customers, service providers and external advisors where analytical inputs are required for portfolio, contract, market-readiness or energy management decisions.
Market, system and network operators where relevant to future market participation, data requirements, settlements or commercial exposure analysis.
Knowledge and Capability Requirements
Strong capability in data science, advanced analytics, statistical modelling, optimisation, forecasting and scenario analysis.
Experience working with time-series, operational, market, financial or commercial datasets to support business decision-making.
Ability to develop pricing analytics, forecast models, portfolio scenarios, dashboards and decision-support tools.
Working knowledge of electricity, energy, commodity, trading, optimisation or similar commercial environments would be advantageous.
Exposure to ETRM systems, electricity market platforms, SAWEM, Power BI, Aveva PI or energy-market reform would be advantageous.
Exposure to energy management, energy efficiency, demand-side management, site energy performance or energy consumption analytics would be advantageous.
Strong data governance discipline, including model documentation, assumption management, validation, auditability and version control.
Ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders through reports, dashboards and decision papers.
Qualifications and Experience
University Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Economics, Finance, Business Analytics or a related quantitative discipline.
9 years of experience
Competencies
Customer Centricity: Engages with internal customers and stakeholders to understand business requirements and provide analytical insight that supports informed commercial and operational decisions.
Business Acumen: Applies understanding of the Integrated Power business, electricity markets, portfolio value drivers, pricing, forecasting and commercial risk to produce relevant decision-support outputs.
Commercial Agility: Uses analytics, modelling and scenario assessment to support timely, evidence-based commercial decisions in a dynamic market environment.
Technical and Analytical Excellence: Builds robust analytical models, forecasts, dashboards and optimisation tools, while ensuring assumptions, data quality and outputs are properly tested and governed.
Delivery Excellence: Creates practical, reliable and repeatable analytical solutions that support delivery against business priorities, project milestones and value-creation objectives.
Partnership: Works collaboratively across Integrated Power, trading, asset management, finance, digital, operations and external partners to convert complex data into actionable insight.
Develop Self: Maintains and develops knowledge of data science, electricity markets, ETRM systems, SAWEM readiness, Power BI, Aveva PI and related analytical tools.
Builds Talent: Shares methods, documents models, supports users and helps build sustainable internal analytics capability.
Inspirational: Communicates analytical findings clearly and confidently to technical and non-technical stakeholders, enabling sound business decisions.
Collaborative: Initiates collaboration, removes barriers to cross-functional working and engages inclusively across business, digital and operational teams.

Slicing & Bagging Operations
Operate and monitor slicers, baggers, conveyors and related equipment safely and efficiently.
Set and adjust equipment to achieve required product specifications and throughput.
Ensure bread is correctly sliced, packed and sealed with minimum product damage and waste.
Verify correct packaging materials and product specifications are used.
Monitor equipment for abnormalities, jams and defects and report/escalate immediately.
Quality, Coding & Food Safety
Conduct routine quality checks and ensure products meet required specifications.
Verify correct batch/date coding and ensure codes are clear, accurate and legible.
Identify, isolate and report non-conforming product.
Maintain GMP, HACCP, food-safety, hygiene and product-integrity standards.
Prevent contamination and foreign-material risks.
MECP – Clean as You Go
Apply the MECP (Clean as You Go) principle throughout the shift.
Keep equipment, conveyors, floors and work areas clean, organised and free from product build-up and waste.
Clean spills and product remnants immediately.
Follow cleaning schedules and work instructions.
Maintain the workstation to the required MECP and hygiene standards.
Ensure the area is handed over to the next shift in a clean, safe and production-ready condition.
Production & Equipment
Achieve planned production targets and maintain efficient product flow.
Minimise downtime, product losses and packaging waste.
Complete required production and quality records accurately.
Perform authorised operator checks and basic adjustments.
Report equipment faults and assist Maintenance during breakdowns and planned maintenance when required.
Health & Safety
Comply with all safety procedures and PPE requirements.
Never bypass or interfere with machine guards or safety devices.
Report unsafe conditions, incidents, near misses and equipment defects immediately.
Follow applicable lock-out/tag-out requirements.
Maintain a safe working environment.
Teamwork & Communication
Work effectively with Production, Quality and Maintenance teams.
Participate in shift handovers and communicate production, quality and equipment issues.
Follow reasonable instructions from the Supervisor/Team Leader.
Support colleagues to maintain smooth and efficient production.
SHIFT, PUBLIC HOLIDAY & OVERTIME REQUIREMENT
The employee is required to work according to the approved production roster, which may include day/night shifts, weekends and public holidays. The employee may also be required to work overtime from time to time due to production requirements, operational demands, breakdowns, maintenance, increased production volumes or other business needs. Such work will be managed in accordance with applicable company policies, employment agreements and legislation.
MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
Grade 12 or equivalent preferred.
Previous bakery, food manufacturing or production experience advantageous.
Experience operating slicing, bagging or packaging equipment advantageous.
Basic literacy and numeracy skills.
Good communication, teamwork, attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
Strong awareness of food safety, MECP, quality

Pernod Ricard South Africa is one of six African market companies to proudly fly the flag of the Pernod Ricard Group.

The French-based Pernod Ricard Group is the world co-leader of the wine and spirits industry, delivering on leading premium brands such as Chivas Regal, Jameson Whiskey, ABSOLUT vod...read moreka and G.H.Mumm Champagne. 

Pernod Ricard South Africa was established in 1994, following the birth of South Africa’s democracy and the lifting of international trade sanctions. Over the past 20 years, it has grown significantly within the local market and still continues to thrive.

Pernod Ricard South Africa is part of a network of 80 international market companies that promote both the Group’s international brands and manages local and regional brands like Red Heart Rum and Olmeca Tequila. 

With headquarters in Cape Town and regional offices across the country, the Pernod Ricard South Africa family employs more than 270 proud employees. 

As the "creators of conviviality” and backed by sound business values and a belief in building lasting relationships, the respected Pernod Ricard tradition continues to be carried forward with vibrancy and passion by the men and women behind Pernod Ricard South Africa.

OUR VISION
Our vision at Pernod Ricard South Africa is "Authentic Brands and Authentic People creating the most respected spirits company in South Africa".

We also support Pernod Ricard’s global ambition to become No.1 in the industry worldwide. This means commitment to being at the forefront of driving growth in the wine and spirits industry. This is a mind-set of those who dare to create, to innovate and to change the rules. This is why innovation is at the heart of our local and global strategy.

Authentic Brands, Authentic People 

From original recipes and ingredients to time-honoured production processes, each premium Pernod Ricard brand is steeped in rich heritage. It is with this legacy in mind that we aim to stay true to our authentic origins. Pernod Ricard is not just a company - it is a business partnership, friendship and most of all, it is a family.

Paul Ricard, one of the company founders, always told his employees: "This business is yours as much as mine. Together we will rule the market”.

To this day, Pernod Ricard’s growth and on-going success is not only a result of leading premium brand offerings, but also attributed to the exceptional people who work together to make it all possible.

Every person who works for Pernod Ricard is unique. Their individual authenticity is valued. Our people are centred, value relationships based on transparency, trustworthiness, honesty and reliability. Pernod Ricard people are genuine in their interaction with one another and their external relationships are personal, have substance and are enduring.

At Pernod Ricard South Africa we don’t just sell spirits; we also have spirit. We are authentic people, selling authentic brands and are proud of it.

Job Description:
Role Overview
We are looking for an experienced WAN, Check Point Firewall & Azure Networking Engineer to join our technology team. The successful candidate will be responsible for the design, implementation, administration, monitoring, troubleshooting and optimisation of enterprise network and security environments.
The role requires strong hands-on experience across WAN technologies, Check Point firewalls and Microsoft Azure networking, with a focus on network availability, performance, security and resilience.
Key Responsibilities
WAN & Network Infrastructure
Design, configure and support enterprise WAN and LAN network environments.
Manage WAN connectivity, routing and network performance.
Troubleshoot complex network connectivity and performance issues.
Configure and manage routing protocols such as BGP and OSPF.
Monitor network availability, capacity and performance.
Work with service providers to resolve connectivity and circuit-related incidents.
Support network changes, upgrades and migrations.
Ensure network infrastructure meets availability, performance and security requirements.
Check Point Firewall
Install, configure, administer and maintain Check Point firewalls.
Manage firewall policies, NAT, VPNs, access rules and security configurations.
Perform firewall rule reviews and optimisation.
Troubleshoot firewall and network security incidents.
Monitor firewall performance, logs and security events.
Implement security changes in accordance with change management processes.
Support high-availability firewall environments.
Ensure firewall configurations comply with organisational security standards.
Azure Networking
Design, implement and support Microsoft Azure networking environments.
Configure and manage:
Azure Virtual Networks (VNet)
Subnets
Network Security Groups (NSGs)
Azure Firewall
Route Tables / UDRs
VPN Gateway
ExpressRoute
Load Balancers
Private Endpoints
VNet Peering
Support hybrid connectivity between on-premises infrastructure and Azure.
Troubleshoot Azure network connectivity and routing issues.
Assist with Azure network migrations and cloud transformation initiatives.
Implement secure and scalable Azure network architectures.
Technical Requirements
Strong hands-on experience with WAN technologies and enterprise networking.
Strong Check Point Firewall administration and troubleshooting experience.
Strong Microsoft Azure Networking experience.
Good understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN and network security.
Experience with BGP, OSPF and routing protocols.
Experience with network monitoring and troubleshooting tools.
Understanding of high availability and disaster recovery principles.
Experience supporting hybrid cloud environments.
Strong knowledge of network security principles and best practices.
Qualifications & Certifications
Relevant degree, diploma or technical qualification in IT, Networking or a related field.
Check Point certification such as CCSA/CCSE would be advantageous.
Microsoft Azure networking certification such as AZ-700 would be advantageous.
Cisco certification such as CCNA/CCNP would be beneficial.
Key Competencies
Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.
Excellent problem-solving ability.
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to work under pressure in a production environment.
Strong documentation and reporting skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a technical team.
Strong understanding of ITIL and change management processes.
Excellent attention to detail and security awareness.
Experience
8+ years' experience in enterprise networking and infrastructure.
Proven experience supporting WAN environments.
Strong hands-on Check Point Firewall experience.
Strong experience with Azure Networking and hybrid cloud environments.
Experience working in large, complex enterprise environments is advantageous.

Job Description:
Purpose of Role:
SPARK Schools teachers drive scholar achievement by maintaining high expectations for classroom culture, behavior and academic growth for all scholars. This role requires the ability to teach across multiple subjects and grade levels with confidence, adapt to different school cultures quickly and hold high expectations for scholar behaviour and achievement from the first moment of deployment.

Deployment may be same-day, next-day, or advance-planned. The educator must be prepared to travel to any school in the network at short notice.
This role sits within the Centre of Excellence pipeline and may transition into a permanent school-based role upon mutual agreement.
This is not a passive cover role. The Locum Generalist Educator is expected to deliver prepared lesson plans, manage classrooms with authority and care and integrate into the existing school team as a functional, contributing member — even on short-term engagements.
Requirements
Responsibilities:
Instructional Delivery
Uphold behavioural expectations, routines and classroom culture from the first period of the first day, whether working inside or outside the classroom
Flex across any slot or block of the PLM model as needed, providing responsive support wherever scholars and staff require it

Prepared to step into any role at or at the level of educator, including: classroom teacher, blended learning facilitator, co-teacher, small group tutor, experience lab TA, homework support facilitator or exam invigilator

The ICT Contracts Specialist is accountable for the end-to-end lifecycle management of ICT contracts, including contract planning, drafting support, review, negotiation facilitation, execution, performance monitoring, renewal, variation, issue resolution and close-out. The role ensures that ICT services, software, hardware, cloud, cybersecurity and managedservice contracts are commercially sound, legally and regulatory compliant, risk-managed, auditable and aligned to DBSA governance, SCM requirements, service delivery objectives and value-for-money principles. The incumbent acts as the central contract and vendor-performance specialist for ICT, working with ICT, SCM, Legal, Risk, Finance, business stakeholders and service providers to ensure contractual obligations, SLAs, KPIs, data protection, security, licensing, service credits, penalties, exit provisions and renewal decisions are actively managed.
Key Responsibilities
KEY PERFORMANCE AREAS
Contract Management
Coordinate contract signature processes and ensure all contractual documentation is complete, compliant, and properly archived.
Review and negotiate ICT contracts and amendments in collaboration with ICT business units, SCM and Legal.
Track key contract milestones, deliverables, expiry dates, renewals, termination periods, guarantees, insurance requirements, and other contractual obligations.
Liaise with internal stakeholders, service providers, contractors, suppliers, and third parties to obtain required documentation and facilitate contract execution.
Escalate and manage potential contract-related legal risks and disputes in collaboration with ICT business units to Legal and Risk.
Monitor contract renewals, expirations, and compliance with terms and conditions.
Review and analyse contract terms, conditions, and obligations to ensure compliance with internal policies, governance standards, legal frameworks and industry practices.
Service Level Agreement Monitoring and Document Management
Create dashboard to monitor SLA performance to track contractor and service provider performance against contractual deliverables, milestones, KPIs, and service level agreements.
Document service level agreements and assist with monitoring contract compliance, performance milestones and deliverables in collaboration with ICT and business units.
Conduct regular contract audits and performance reviews to identify risks, trends, variances, and underperformance.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance contract performance, compliance, governance, and value realisation.
Facilitate SLA reviews for contractor and service provider performance and implement corrective action plans where required.
Prepare, maintain, and manage accurate central repository of all ICT contract files, registers, and ensure proper classification, version control, audit readiness, and secure record storage.
Keep a record of reported service provider challenges and the tracking of performance issues, corrective actions, and follow-up activities.
Manage relationships with ICT vendors and service providers and document all vendor engagements in alignment with contractual obligations.
Risk and Compliance Management
Contribute to the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of contract management frameworks, policies, procedures, controls, and governance standards.
Liaise with Internal Audit, Legal, Procurement, and Risk teams to ensure alignment with governance and compliance requirements.
Identify contract-related risks in ICT engagements and facilitate mitigation strategies to minimise operational, legal, and financial exposure this including training stakeholders on contract management processes.
Maintain compliance with legal, regulatory, and internal governance requirements.
Support audit processes and provide documentation as required.
Monitor adherence to governance, documentation, approval, record-keeping requirements and data protection and privacy laws (e.g., POPIA).
Procurement and Sourcing Support
Collaborate with procurement teams to design, manage, and oversee ICT tenders and sourcing strategies, ensuring that all processes are aligned with ICT processes.
Support the tender process by validating and applying both technical and support contract award processes.
Contribute to procurement planning by identifying ICT needs and providing inputs into the sourcing needs plan.
Reporting and Monitoring
Support governance submissions, management reviews, and audit processes through the preparation of accurate and comprehensive documentation and reporting inputs.
Generate dashboards, reports, and performance insights to support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.
Contribute to the enhancement and implementation of digital contract management systems, trackers, and reporting tools to improve process efficiency, data integrity, and reporting accuracy.
Prepare regular reports on contract status, SLA performance, and vendor compliance.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date contract documentation.
Key Measurements of Outputs
Contract register maintained at 100% completeness and updated within agreed turnaround times after execution, variation, renewal or termination.
Percentage of ICT contracts with current, approved SLAs, KPIs, ownership, renewal dates, termination notice periods, risk ratings and obligation trackers recorded.
Renewals, expiries and termination notices proactively flagged within the agreed lead time, with no avoidable missed renewal, lapse or unmanaged rollover.
SLA and vendor performance dashboards produced accurately and on time, including service credits, penalties, breaches, corrective actions and trend analysis.
Contract compliance reviews, audits and vendor performance review meetings completed in accordance with the approved schedule.
Contractual risks, disputes, non-compliance findings and performance issues documented, escalated and resolved within agreed governance timeframes.
Quality of contract review inputs, procurement support, negotiation preparation and governance submissions, as assessed by line management and key stakeholders.
Compliance with PFMA, PPPFA, SCM policies, POPIA, information security, ICT governance and internal approval requirements evidenced through audit-ready records.
Improvement initiatives implemented to strengthen contract lifecycle management, reporting accuracy, vendor performance, cost control and value realisation.
Stakeholder satisfaction with contract management support, responsiveness, advisory quality and vendor governance coordination.
Expertise & Technical Competencies
QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
Minimum Qualification
Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent NQF Level 7 qualification in Law, Commercial Law, Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Business Administration/Management, Information Technology, Information Systems or a related field.

Company Details: In Africa our strategy is to grow Diageo’s leadership across beer and spirits by providing brand choice across a broad range of consumer motivations, profiles, and occasions. We are focused on growing beer faster than the market and accelerating the growth of spirits through continued inves...read moretment in infrastructure and brands with mainstream spirits being critical to realising the potential of the region. Local sourcing is a key element of our strategy in Africa: it directly supports our commercial operations, while indirectly supporting our position by bringing wider benefits to society as a whole. Our markets The region comprises Nigeria, East Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Burundi, Rwanda and South Sudan), Africa Regional Markets (including Ghana, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Angola and a sorghum beer business in South Africa) and South Africa (including Republic of South Africa and Mozambique). Supply operations We operate 12 breweries in Africa, four sites that produce sorghum beer in South Africa, cider plants and five facilities which provide blending and malting services. In addition, our beer and spirits brands are produced under licence by third-parties in 19 African countries. In the year ended 30 June 2016 we sold our 25% interest in a brewery in South Africa. Route to consumer In Africa our largest businesses are in Nigeria, where we own 54.3% of a listed company whose principal brands are Guinness, Orijin, Harp and Malta, and in East Africa, where we own 50.03% of East African Breweries Limited (EABL). EABL produces and distributes beer and spirits brands to a range of consumers in Kenya and Uganda, and owns a 51% equity in Serengeti Breweries Limited located in Tanzania. Within Africa Regional Markets, we have wholly owned subsidiaries in Cameroon, Ethiopia and Reunion and majority-owned subsidiaries in Ghana and the Seychelles. Angola is supplied via a third party distributor. In South Africa and Mozambique we sell spirits, beer, cider and ready to drink products through wholly owned subsidiaries, following the termination of the agreement with Heineken and Namibia Breweries Limited in December 2015. Diageo has agreements with the Castel Group who license, brew and distribute Guinness in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Gambia, Gabon, Ivory Coast, Togo, Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali and Guinea. Diageo sells spirits through distributors in the majority of other sub-Saharan countries. Sustainability and Responsibility The issues we address differ between markets but a key issue in many is illicit alcohol. We work closely with governments and regulators on this significant public health issue and specific local issues, such as drink driving in South Africa or bringing in a minimum legal drinking age in Ghana. Our aim everywhere is to promote responsible drinking as part of a balanced lifestyle. Our overall approach is to consider the broader context of our contribution as a local taxpayer, employer and member of the community. Our recent work to assess human rights impacts throughout the value chain was piloted in Kenya. We source 73% of agricultural materials locally and we work with more than 50,000 local farmers for our agricultural inputs. Fifteen of our production sites in Africa are in water-stressed areas, so we focus closely on managing water efficiently and enhancing access to clean water to surrounding communities through our pan-African Water of Life programme. This year we launched the Water Blueprint in East Africa, to address water stewardship in this water-stressed area. Our new Sustainable Agriculture Strategy will play an important part in strengthening our longstanding and mutually beneficial relationships with farmers and communities.

Company Details: Cape Union Mart International (Pty) Ltd has been equipping South African adventurers since 1933, and is South Africa's favourite outdoor adventure store. Stocking everything one needs for outdoor pursuits - including hiking, camping, trail running, mountain biking, snow sports, travel and mor...read moree - Cape Union Mart is an essential first step in every adventure. Cape Union Mart has stores across South Africa, and in Namibia and Botswana. The history of Cape Union Mart dates back to 1933 when the late Philip Krawitz, grandfather of the current Chairman, founded the business on the corner of Corporation and Mostert Street in Cape Town. Cape Union Mart originated as an "Army and Navy Store" and became famous for its "everything from an anchor to a toothpick" product range. Sandwiched between two of South Africa 's largest retailers, Woolworths and OK Bazaars, Cape Union Mart realised that it had to offer something different. Apart from an extensive range of merchandise, the store became known as "the friendly store" and focused on building unique relationships with its customers. During the war years, Cape Union Mart supplied visiting troops with some of the luxuries and necessities associated with the military. Passing whaling ships and foreign fishermen were also catered for with a unique array of merchandise from around the world. In the post-war years, the company grew and prospered under Arthur Krawitz who took over the business from his father in the late 1940's. The company became famous for non-seasonal merchandise and specialised in selling summer clothing to people touring overseas in winter. and vice versa. Cape Union Mart was the first importer of many famous products such as Levi Jeans, Hong Kong anoraks, Norwegian socks and Gore-Tex foul weather clothing.

Job Description
FEM is seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Operational Accountant to join the Operational Finance team. Reporting to the Operational Finance Manager, the successful candidate will provide financial oversight across pension and claims accounting processes, ensuring the accuracy, validity and completeness of transactions and payments. The role supports financial governance, operational controls, reconciliations, reporting and audit requirements while contributing to the integrity of pension and claims-related financial information and compliance with regulatory and internal control requirements.
Key Responsibilities
The key responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:
Validate pension awards, extensions, commutations and related calculations in accordance with COIDA, internal policies and approved procedures.
Review and validate pension and claims-related payments, ensuring accuracy, completeness, compliance with Delegation of Authority requirements and appropriate supporting documentation prior to payment release.
Perform and review bank and account reconciliations, investigate variances and ensure timely resolution of reconciling items.
Process and review journals and accounting entries, maintaining appropriate supporting documentation and audit trails.
Ensure the integrity of pension and claims-related financial information through effective controls, monitoring and analysis.
Prepare management reports, financial analyses and commentary on pension and claims expenditure, highlighting trends, risks and key drivers.
Support month-end and year-end activities, including reporting, reconciliations and financial governance requirements.
Support internal and external audits by providing accurate records, supporting documentation and timely responses to audit queries.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, process optimisation and the enhancement of controls within the Operational Finance function.
Education Requirements
Minimum:
CIMA or SAIPA Qualification or BCom Accounting, BCompt, BCom Financial Management or equivalent (NQF Level 7)
Ideal:
Degree with Accounting as a major.
Relevant professional accounting designation or progress toward such designation.
Training and Knowledge
Minimum:
Knowledge of financial accounting principles and practices.
Functional computer literacy, including proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
Knowledge of balance sheet reconciliations and creditor payment processes.
Understanding of financial controls and governance requirements.
Ideal:
Knowledge of the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA).
Exposure to financial systems within a financial services or insurance environment.
Understanding of financial governance, audit requirements and regulatory compliance.
Experience Requirements
Minimum:
3 to 4 years' experience in a financial accounting, finance operations or operational finance role.
Ideal:
Experience in pension administration, claims accounting, finance operations or payment validation environments.
Experience within a financial services, insurance or compensation fund environment.
Experience performing financial analysis, reconciliations and payment controls.
Key Competencies
Analytical thinking and problem-solving.
Attention to detail and accuracy.
Financial control and risk awareness.
Planning, organising and time management.
Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Accountability, integrity and sound judgement.
Continuous improvement and process optimisation mindset.

Job Description
A Cloud Security Specialist plays a crucial role in safeguarding the cloud infrastructure and data. This position requires a blend of technical expertise, security knowledge, and problem-solving skills to implement and maintain security protocols in cloud environments.
DESCRIPTION
Conduct threat analysis on cloud environments.
Uses data collected from a variety of agnostic and native cloud security and application security tools (e.g., Cloud Security Posture Management, Web Application Firewalls, API Compliance, Static Code Analysis Tools, Source Composition Analysis tools, Data Security Posture Management) to analyze events that occur within production and non-production environments for the purposes of mitigating threats and improving compliance.
Perform risk assessments and test adherence to core security tenets for any systems which process or store vendor data, customer data, employee data or any data deemed valuable and sensitive.
Maintain and update the multi-cloud security standards assessments for the organization.
Design security solutions to address known vulnerabilities in cloud infrastructure, API endpoints, web applications or other network reachable systems across the estate.
Define and implement cyber security threat use cases.
Review violations of cyber security procedures and discuss procedures with violators to ensure violations are not repeated.
Coordinates with the SOC teams by offering the necessary functional guidance for avoiding malicious activities.
Is a key resource during cyber incident response.
Coordinate monitoring of networks or systems for security breaches or intrusions.
Develop response and recovery strategies for security breaches.
Supports the team with research and source analysis.
Offer all the necessary support to cyber security initiative through predictive and reactive analysis.
Works with customers, vendors and internal resources for problem resolution and security advisories.
Must articulate the emerging cloud security trends to the security operations centre team members.
Identify or implement solutions to information security problems.
Leverages industry best practices and standards for improvements and optimization, such as NIST and CIS, as well as cloud specific standards such as the AWS Best Practices Framework for Security and Microsoft Azure Security Benchmark.
Provides technical advice and consultation to the business.
Recommend information security enhancements to management.
Acquires and applies knowledge of business processes, procedures, policies and practices.
Communicates effectively regarding cloud security related activities.
Participates in systems handover process.
Participates in software and/or hardware upgrades.
Adds assets to the Web Application Firewall for Layer 7 protection.
Refines Firewall rulesets.
Train users and promote security awareness to ensure system security and to improve server and network posture.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE
Matric
Relevant diploma or degree in technology or business-related field
3 or more years of experience as a Cloud Security Analyst/Engineer
AWS Security Speciality
AWS Cloud Practitioner
AWS Solutions Architect
Experience with cloud security assessments, cloud-native security controls, risk assessment, web application firewalls, information gathering, and reporting.
ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE
Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP) from ISC2
Intermediate or Advanced API Security knowledge (Using Burp Suite, or other app sec tools)
Certified Ethical Hacker, or equivalent course
CompTIA Security+
AZ-900 (Microsoft Azure Fundamentals)
SC-900 (Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals)
AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Adminstrator)
SC-100 (Microsoft Cybersecurity Architect)
COMPETENCIES REQUIRED
Critical thinking/problem-solving
Oral/written communication
Teamwork/ collaboration
Strong security research skills
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) – Terraform and Cloudformation
Scripting – Bash, Python and Powershell

Job Description:
Purpose of the role
The QA and Support Analyst reports to QA and Support Lead. You play a critical, dual role in keeping Unifi's platforms robust and reliable. You will work across the entire software lifecycle, proactively planning and testing new features to catch bugs before they reach our users, while reactively troubleshooting live software and production issues.
By bridging the gap between quality assurance and software support, you keep our frontline teams running smoothly and make life easy for our clients across Africa.
Responsibilities
Write and execute manual test cases that mimic how frontline teams and clients use our systems in the real world.
Thoroughly test new features before release, signing them off only when they deliver a seamless and reliable client experience.
Investigate and resolve first- and second-line application support issues within agreed timelines.
Use SQL queries, system logs (Elasticsearch/Kibana), and monitoring tools to find out what is causing system issues.
Clearly document bugs and support requests in Jira so developers can understand and fix them quickly.
Check system fixes to ensure existing features stay stable and new updates don't introduce new problems.
Review bug trends and support ticket patterns to spot recurring problems and recommend simple, permanent fixes.
Translate complex technical problems into simple, jargon-free explanations to keep users and business stakeholders updated.
Partner with developers, product team, and support leads to speed up bug fixes and improve testing processes.
Participate in a shared weekend and standby roster (approximately once every six weeks) to resolve critical, out-of-hours production issues.
Requirements
3–5 years' experience in software QA, application or production support
Hands-on experience investigating and resolving issues in business applications or software
Hands-on experience using SQL to investigate application issues, validate data and troubleshoot problems
ISTQB Certification advantageous but not required
A proven ability to write clear test scenarios and identify software flaws manually
Experience with ticketing platforms like Jira, and logging/monitoring tools like Elasticsearch, Kibana, or similar
Strong problem-solving skills, you enjoy digging into problems, asking why and finding the root cause of the problem
A good understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and how software moves from development into production
Able to work independently while connecting with developers, product teams and Unifi users to get things done
A clear communicator who can explain technical issues simply and keep people informed until the problem is resolved
Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and pride in getting things right
Willing to be on standby approximately once every six weeks, or when needed, to help keep our systems running smoothly
Curious, willing to learn and comfortable questioning things when they don't make sense
Excited by the opportunity to build and support technology that makes life easy for people across Africa

Job Title: Senior Manager – Platform, Architecture & Modernisation Advisory
Job Description:
Job Description
The opportunity
Technology leaders are facing a new architecture problem.
Cloud, data, AI, enterprise platforms and increasingly agentic systems can no longer be treated as separate transformation agendas. Decisions made across these layers determine an organisation's speed of innovation, technology economics, resilience, interoperability and ability to scale AI safely.
Deloitte Africa Engineering, AI & Data Advisory is looking for an exceptional
Senior Manager – Platform, Architecture & Modernisation Advisory
to help executives navigate these decisions and translate them into executable transformation programs.
This is not a conventional enterprise architecture or solution architecture role.
It is a senior consulting and practice-building position for someone who can
challenge technology strategy, make complex architecture choices understandable to executives, create investable modernisation pathways and mobilise engineering teams to execute them
.
Your mandate
As capability steward, you will build and lead Deloitte Africa's Advisory proposition around the technology foundations required for modern digital and AI-enabled enterprises.
You will connect strategic intent to the architecture decisions required to make it real.
Your mandate spans:
Technology decision advisory.
Help CIOs, CTOs and CDAOs make consequential decisions around cloud, data, AI, integration, enterprise platforms, modernisation and emerging technology.
Architecture challenge.
Independently assess and challenge existing technology strategies and architectures, identifying structural constraints, unnecessary complexity, technical debt and future capability gaps.
Transformation architecture.
Translate target-state architecture into sequenced, investable transformation programs rather than producing architecture diagrams without an execution pathway.
Commercial leadership.
Build propositions, create pipeline, originate engagements and expand architecture-led advisory into wider engineering transformation opportunities.
Capability stewardship.
Develop Deloitte's architecture methods, reference patterns, talent, technology ecosystem and market position.
What you will do
You will:
Advise CIOs, CTOs, CDAOs and architecture leaders on strategic technology choices.
Perform independent architecture and technology-strategy reviews.
Define enterprise technology principles and target-state architectures.
Develop modernisation strategies spanning applications, cloud, data, integration and AI.
Design enterprise AI platform strategies and associated architecture roadmaps.
Help clients determine what should be built, bought, modernised, consolidated, retired or consumed as a service.
Translate architecture alternatives into explicit business, cost, risk and execution trade-offs.
Develop cloud, data and AI platform roadmaps aligned to business strategy.
Shape enterprise architecture for GenAI and agentic AI, including model access, knowledge, integration, orchestration, observability, control and security.
Advise on AI gateways, control planes and common enterprise AI services.
Evaluate hyperscaler, SaaS, platform and technology vendor propositions independently.
Support major technology investment decisions and commercial negotiations.
Connect enterprise architecture to technology operating model, governance and delivery implications.
Develop pragmatic transition architectures and transformation sequencing.
Structure and lead complex technology advisory engagements.
Mobilise specialists across Cloud, AI, Data, Cyber, Engineering and enterprise platforms.
Lead senior architecture forums and executive decision workshops.
Originate and convert advisory and transformation opportunities.
Build signature offerings, methods, reference architectures and reusable IP.
Develop ecosystem relationships with hyperscalers and major technology providers while maintaining independent client advice.
Mentor and develop architecture-oriented advisory talent.
Qualifications
The profile we are looking for
You will likely have
15+ years of relevant experience
across technology consulting, enterprise architecture, cloud/data/AI transformation or related disciplines.
We expect:
Significant experience in consulting, technology advisory or a strongly client-facing equivalent environment.
Deep credibility in enterprise technology architecture.
Demonstrated experience working across more than one of cloud, data, AI, applications, integration or digital platforms.
Experience leading complex architecture or technology transformation programs.
Ability to translate highly technical choices into clear executive decisions.
Strong understanding of modern enterprise AI architectures.
Experience working with at least one major hyperscaler and familiarity with multi-cloud enterprise environments.
Commercial experience including opportunity shaping, proposals, pursuits and client development.
Strong understanding of transformation economics and architectural trade-offs.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams.
Exceptional stakeholder management with credibility at CIO, CTO, CDAO and Chief Architect level.
Relevant undergraduate qualifications in engineering, computer science, information systems or related disciplines are expected. Relevant architecture, cloud or technology certifications are advantageous but will not substitute for demonstrated capability.
Architecture depth
We expect meaningful expertise across areas including:
Enterprise and solution architecture;
Public and hybrid cloud architectures;
Modern data platforms;
AI and GenAI platforms;
Enterprise AI gateways and control planes;
Agentic AI architecture;
Application and platform modernisation;
API and event-driven integration;
Enterprise SaaS ecosystems;
Security and identity architecture;
Observability and operational resilience;
MLOps/LLMOps and AI lifecycle management;
Technology standards and architecture governance; and
FinOps and technology-consumption implications.
You are not expected to be the deepest SME in every domain.
Your differentiator should be the ability to
see across them
and determine how architectural decisions interact at enterprise level.
What will distinguish exceptional candidates
Exceptional candidates may have:
Served as a Chief Architect, Enterprise Architect or CTO-level advisor while maintaining strong consulting and commercial capability;
Built architecture or technology-strategy consulting propositions;
Led major cloud, data or AI modernisation programs;
Designed enterprise-grade AI platform architectures;
Originated consulting work through trusted CIO/CTO relationships;
Experience across several major technology ecosystems rather than attachment to a single vendor;
An ability to challenge prevailing architecture thinking constructively; and
A reputation for converting architecture complexity into clear executive choices.
How success will be measured
You will be accountable for:
building a credible market-facing Platform & Architecture Advisory business;
originating and converting qualified pipeline;
managed revenue and contribution to downstream EAID transformation revenue;
development of distinctive propositions and architecture IP;
client impact and quality of strategic technology decisions;
expansion of advisory engagements into executable transformation;
effective orchestration of the broader EAID capability;
development of strong architecture advisory talent; and
trusted relationships across client technology leadership and strategic technology partners.

Store monitoring instruments appropriately to prevent damage when not in use, such as storing them in protective cases, avoiding extreme temperatures or humidity, and ensuring they are stored securely.

Assess and monitor workers' exposure to hazardous chemicals by sampling and analysing substances to determine their concentration in the air or on surfaces.
Evaluate workplace ergonomics to identify and mitigate factors that could lead to musculoskeletal disorders or injuries.
Examine and evaluate the effectiveness of ventilation systems to ensure proper air exchange and control of contaminants.
Evaluate the use of PPE and ensure that workers are provided with and adequately using the appropriate protective gear for their tasks.
Collaborate with other health and safety professionals, such as industrial hygienists, safety engineers, and occupational health specialists, to address broader safety concerns and contribute to developing comprehensive risk mitigation strategies.

Knowledge of risk assessment methodologies and control measures for mitigating workplace hazards.

Operational Management:
Manage the operations of the Business Unit with regards to the processes, inputs, targets, outputs and resourcing requirements.
Offer technical advice and support to team members on a range of regulatory issues/requirement.
Implement SAHPRA policies and procedures to identify and resolve complex issues and inconsistencies and make recommendations on initiatives.
Lead processes for appeals lodged against regulatory decisions taken by the national regulator.
Manage the development of regulations, regulatory processes and guidelines within the Business Unit.
Perform quality assurance of processes and outputs to ensure compliance with legislative and regulatory requirements.
Apply scientific principles, regulatory requirements, best practices and quality assurance and review applications where applicable.
Conduct reviews and/or adjudicate peer-reviewed reports and provide technical decisions regarding applications.
Manage and support Clinical Technical Advisory Committee.

Allocate program or project resources in line with strategic direction.
Identify and prioritise resources across various initiatives or operations.
Develop and monitor the implementation of the annual operational plan and Business Unit plans.
Ensure operations and processes of the Business Unit are aligned to the relevant legal frameworks, prescribed local and international Guidelines.
Stakeholder Management:
Conduct consultation meetings with representatives from the orthodox medicines industry to advise on administrative and technical issues.
Respond to external enquiries by industry, Business Units within SAHPRA and other external stakeholders.
Participate in industry engagements and regulatory forums regionally and internationally (e.g. Zazibona, WHO, ICH Working Groups, IPRP, Continental initiatives).
Financial Management:
Develop or support the development of the programme’s budget and manage its implementation.
Work together with Finance Unit to develop and manage the Business Unit’s annual budget.
Ensure the effective implementation, management, monitoring of the Business Unit’s budget, and mitigate and report on any variances.
Prepare and submit accurate financial reports within the required timeframe.
Ensure revenue information is collated and provided to the Finance office within the required timeframe.
Manage and ensure effective utilisation of financial resources.
Governance, Risk and Compliance Management:
Develop, review, update and implement policies related to Standard Operating Procedures and Guidelines.
Adhere to SCM and PFMA aspects and other SAHPRA policies and procedures.
Ensure process changes are processed through effective change control processes.
Apply risk management in processes.
Manage all relevant internal and external audits by responding to any non-conformances or audit findings that are raised and develop mitigation reports.
Provide timely and accurate evidence and expert analysis to support the Legal Unit in addressing compliance issues and legal matters.
Ensure deviations or non-conformances are recorded and responded to.
Implementation of Quality Management Systems (QMS) Culture.
Manage the development and continuous monitoring of the QMS in the Business Unit – processes, guidelines in alignment with best practices (i.e., National, Regional, Continental, international).
Manage the development and review of internal policies, in collaboration with senior management. Ensure compliance with implementation of approved processes.
Ensure training records on all processes are maintained.
Compile Business Unit reports as required (monthly reports, internal reports, external reports).
Identify risks for the Business Unit, develop mitigation plans and oversee the implementation of mitigation plans.
Ensure readiness for internal and external audits by maintaining accurate records, documentation, and compliance with audit requirements.
People Management:
Develop (i.e., training, coaching, mentoring) and manage (i.e., recruitment, retaining, onboarding, offboarding, daily operations) of Human Resources within the Business Unit.
Foster a positive and collaborative team culture.
Ensure maintenance of confidentiality, high ethical conduct, efficient, effective high-quality performance of staff members.

Job Description:
Introduction
To drive promotional and statistical forecasting accuracy across an allocated portfolio by partnering closely with Merchandising, Demand Planning, and Supply Planning teams.
The role ensures promotional demand is aligned to merchandise plans, improves stock efficiency, and optimizes working capital through disciplined, insight-driven forecasting.
This role provides strategic direction to the business by developing accurate, forward-looking demand promotional forecasts that balance customer demand with company objectives.
As a core enabler of the S&OP process, Demand Promotional Planning influences top-line growth, profitability, inventory optimization, and long-term capacity decisions.
By anticipating demand patterns, identifying risks and opportunities, and constructively challenging assumptions, the role ensures the business delivers the right product, in the right place, at the right time, maximizing sales and customer satisfaction while minimizing cost, waste, and excess inventory.
Job
Description:
Key Responsibilities
Promotional Forecasting & Demand Planning
Deliver accurate demand forecasts - Act as the subject matter expert (SME) for promotional forecasting accuracy within the allocated portfolio.
Develop, review, and continuously improve promotional demand forecasts to support business targets.
Analyse promotional performance and recommend forecast volume changes to merchandising teams.
Capture and maintain accurate forecast adjustments on a daily basis.
Conduct post-promotion analysis to identify trends, insights, and opportunities for improvement.
Inventory & Supply Collaboration
Partner with Supply Planning to ensure optimized inventory levels, focusing on promotional activity.
Monitor inventory flow and future projections to support open-to-buy management.
Support stock efficiency and working capital optimization through accurate promotional forecasting.
Identify risks and opportunities early by proactively highlight gaps to plan and recommend corrective actions to mitigate risks or capture upside potential.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with Category Managers to improve promotional planning and forecasting outcomes.
Contribute to category SIOP meetings by reviewing upcoming promotions, supplier lead times, and future risks/opportunities.
Ensure alignment to critical path deadlines impacting promotional forecasting within the portfolio.
Support the Demand Planning team in achieving total forecasting accuracy targets through weekly and monthly reviews.
Support continuous improvement. Use analytics, performance tracking (e.g., forecast accuracy, bias), and feedback loops to refine demand planning processes and tools.
Reporting & Analysis
Generate promotional forecasting reports and performance insights.
Provide clear, data-driven recommendations to support decision-making.
Ensure concepts, forecasts, and plans are aligned to agreed budgets and targets
Minimum requirements
Essential:
Forecasting Techniques & Tools
Inventory Management Principles
Supply Chain Fundamentals - FMCG, Supply Chain, and Logistics environment
Strong data analysis and statistical modeling skills
Deep analytical capability
Understanding of customer behavior, market trends, competition, and market share
End-to-end understanding of the promotional planning cycle, product lifecycle, and supply chain optimization
Desirable:
Demand planning principles and forecasting models
Financial planning models and methodologies
Ability to understand and fine-tune forecasting algorithms
Additional Knowledge:
Retail planning processes
Distribution centre operations
Demand forecasting and replenishment experience
Strong statistical reasoning and problem-solving ability
Knowledge of forecasting algorithms
Job Related Skills:
Strong analytical and numerate skills
Well-structured, organized, and detail-oriented
Confident presenter with the ability to persuade and influence
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
Strong business and financial acumen
Ability to forecast consumer trends 9–24 months ahead
Complex decision-making based on data, trends, and opinions
Advanced MS Office proficiency (Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint)
Retail mathematical calculations (e.g. stock turn, margin, variance analysis)
Strong negotiation and stakeholder-management skills

JOB PURPOSE
The Contracts Manager is responsible for the effective management, administration, interpretation, and governance of key contracts across multi-party renewable energy projects, including EPC, O&M, PPA, land lease, Long-Term Service Agreements, consultancy agreements, and other project-related agreements.
The role is accountable for ensuring that contractual obligations are identified, monitored, managed, and enforced in accordance with the relevant project agreements. The Contracts Manager will provide contractual and commercial support to project, operations, finance, legal, procurement, and asset management teams, while proactively identifying contractual risks, managing claims and variations, supporting dispute resolution processes, and ensuring that all notices, approvals, payment milestones, procurement activities, and stakeholder communications are handled in line with applicable contractual provisions and internal governance requirements.
The Contracts Manager will also be required to manage contract-related workstreams from inception to close-out, support procurement and negotiation processes, oversee contract compliance, and contribute to the continuous improvement of contract management practices, tools, trackers, and reporting across ENGIE Southern Africa’s renewable energy portfolio.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Commercial Correspondence and Contract Notices
Draft, review, issue, and manage formal contractual correspondence and notices under various project agreements.
Ensure that all notices are issued within the required contractual timelines and in accordance with prescribed notice provisions.
Maintain accurate notice registers for correspondence issued to and received from project stakeholders, contractors, consultants, lenders, authorities, and other third parties.
Ensure that all contractual correspondence, notices, approvals, and project-related records are properly stored and maintained on SharePoint or other approved document management platforms.
Support project teams in determining when formal contractual notices are required and advise on appropriate wording, timing, and contractual basis.
Review correspondence received from contractors, consultants, service providers, and stakeholders, and coordinate appropriate responses with internal subject matter experts and legal teams where required.
Contract Management and Compliance
Manage the administration and implementation of EPC, O&M, PPA, land lease, LTSA, service level, consultancy, and other project-related agreements.
Ensure that project obligations under the relevant contracts are identified, tracked, monitored, and reported to the appropriate internal teams.

The history of Cape Union Mart dates back to 1933 when the late Philip Krawitz, grandfather of the current Chairman, founded the business on the corner of Corporation and Mostert Street in Cape Town. Cape Union Mart originated as an "Army and Navy Store" and became famous for its "everything from an anchor to a toothpick" product range. Sandwiched between two of South Africa 's largest retailers, Woolworths and OK Bazaars, Cape Union Mart realised that it had to offer something different. Apart from an extensive range of merchandise, the store became known as "the friendly store" and focused on building unique relationships with its customers. During the war years, Cape Union Mart supplied visiting troops with some of the luxuries and necessities associated with the military. Passing whaling ships and foreign fishermen were also catered for with a unique array of merchandise from around the world. In the post-war years, the company grew and prospered under Arthur Krawitz who took over the business from his father in the late 1940's. The company became famous for non-seasonal merchandise and specialised in selling summer clothing to people touring overseas in winter. and vice versa. Cape Union Mart was the first importer of many famous products such as Levi Jeans, Hong Kong anoraks, Norwegian socks and Gore-Tex foul weather clothing.
