Computer Literate.
Exceptional communication skills (spoken, telephonic and written).
Organised and systematic.
Detail orientated.
Must possess and aptitude for basic math and money handling skills.
Punctual.
Able to function under pressure in a fast-moving environment.
Able to manage multiple stores
Self-directed and able to work independently

Experience
Minimum 2 years’ experience in a store management role within a retail/FMCG store operations environment.
Financial management experience (budgets, profit and loss statements, financial ratios, etc.).

Business and Retail Management Diploma(desirable).

We care far more about

Job Description:
ENVIRONMENT:
A provider of tailored Financial Solutions seeks a Data & AI Engineer to build, maintain, and improve reliable pipelines and curated datasets that feed the company’s analytics, reporting, and AI workloads, and you will help run the governed in-house AI platform that sits on top of them.
This is one combined role, not a Data Engineer with an AI paragraph bolted on. Data flows from SQL Server and Azure SQL sources into Fabric, through bronze, silver, and gold layers, and out to the semantic, reporting, and AI consumption layers the business depends on.
Expect the work to sit at roughly two-thirds Data Engineering and one-third applied AI in the first year, shifting further towards AI as adoption grows.
Both halves run inside the same established standards, which cover metadata-driven, incremental, idempotent ELT, source control, gated deployment, and human review of anything AI-generated. You will grow into full ownership of production data and AI assets end-to-end: build it, document it, support it.
DUTIES:
Data Engineering: Governed pipelines and the estate –
Develop and maintain batch and incremental ELT pipelines that ingest, transform, and deliver trusted datasets across our SQL Server / Azure SQL / Microsoft Fabric estate.
Write and optimise T-SQL transformation logic, stored procedures, views, and reconciliation queries, following our standards (CTEs over subqueries, idempotent and metadata-driven patterns).
Build and maintain Fabric pipelines, Dataflow Gen2 flows, and Lakehouse / Warehouse data assets.
Support data modelling: dimensional models, medallion (bronze / silver / gold) layer design, partitioning, and performance optimisation for analytics workloads.
Operate the estate: orchestration, scheduling, monitoring, logging, alerting, and methodical incident resolution for data jobs and platform processes.
Implement data validation, reconciliation, row-count and parity checks so reporting outputs can be trusted and prove it with evidence.
Applied AI: The governed AI platform –
Build and maintain the curated, documented datasets, retrieval indexes, and interfaces that governed AI platform and AI-assisted use cases consume.
Help run the in-house AI platform: content ingestion, indexing, configuration, access control, and routine health checks.
Develop Python automation for AI workloads, covering data preparation, embedding and indexing jobs, evaluation harnesses, and approved API integrations.
Build and evaluate AI use cases such as search, summarisation, classification, extraction, and workflow automation, measuring each against defined success criteria with human-review checkpoints built in.
Enforce data minimisation and anonymisation on every AI path: no personal information, credentials, or production data into unapproved tools, and no uncontrolled egress of data.
Record AI evaluation evidence, including what was tested, what the model produced, what a human reviewer changed, and why, so that AI-assisted output stays traceable and auditable.

Shared: Governance, delivery, and documentation –
Work the governed delivery flow: Git / Azure DevOps source control, feature branches, peer-reviewed pull requests, and gated environment promotion (Dev → UAT → production).
Produce and maintain documentation: pipeline design notes, source-to-target mappings, runbooks, AI use-case and configuration notes, and support procedures.
Collaborate with Analysts, the Head of Data & AI, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into governed, supportable data assets, without business logic drifting into unmanaged reports.
What you’ll work with –
Azure SQL and on-premises SQL Server, which form the core transactional and reporting estate.
The wider Fabric surface, including mirroring and CDC ingestion, deployment pipelines, and capacity management.
Python for transformation, automation, and tooling; DAX exposure on the BI side.
Azure DevOps for repos, boards, CI/CD pipelines, and gated deployments.
Power BI and SSRS as the consumption layer you feed.
The governed in-house AI platform, which covers agent tooling, retrieval and indexing, and the controls that make it safe to use on sensitive data. You will help run it, not just use it.
AI-assisted engineering under policy, meaning sanitised inputs, human review of generated code, and traceable output. It is how the whole team works, and how you will work too.

Establish, maintain, and participate in inter-professional and multi-disciplinary teamwork that promotes efficient and effective health care.

Monitor team performance and support skills development
Implement and reinforce a culture of discipline, compliance, and accountability within the team.

Liaise with procurement and suppliers to manage delivery expectations and resolve any inbound issues.
Escalate critical risks (e.g., stockouts, storage constraints) to the Stores Manager with proposed solutions.

Support 5S initiatives and warehouse layout optimization for safety, efficiency, and cleanliness.
Contribute to CI initiatives led by the Continuous Improvement Specialist.
Drive reduction in material losses and waste through process discipline and performance monitoring

National Diploma or NQF Level 6 in: Supply Chain Management, Logistics/Warehouse Management, Food Technology (advantageous for understanding ingredient handling)

Experience managing raw materials (packaging and ingredients) in a high-volume production environment
At least 2 years’ experience in a supervisory or team leader role
Strong working knowledge of SAP (MM, WM)

Deep understanding of raw materials handling in food/beverage manufacturing
Proficient in MM/WM for material transactions and reporting
Ability to manage warehouse operations and implement FIFO/FEFO rigorously
Strong leadership and communication skills to manage and develop a small team
High attention to detail with a disciplined and organized work ethic
Ability to interpret and act on data to improve performance
Sound knowledge of Food Safety, Quality, and SHEQ compliance standards
Familiarity with 5S, lean warehouse practices, and CI methodologies

Job Description:
Job Description & Summary – Independence Specialist (Manager)
A career in the PwC Southern Africa Independence Team, will provide you with the opportunity to advance and foster integrity-based decision making and conduct by PwC professionals throughout our organisation.
You will focus on supporting the Partner Responsible for Independence (PRI) Team in promoting and monitoring compliance with applicable external independence laws and regulations as well as internal independence policies and procedures to help manage PwC’s regulatory, litigation, and reputational risk.
The PwC South Africa Independence Team is part of the firm’s Risk & Quality group within Internal Firm Services. It is responsible for working with the practice across all Line of Services to ensure that the firm meets its regulatory responsibilities as required under PwC Global Independence policy, US SEC and PCAOB rules, EU rules and other territories’ rules.
Whilst prior Independence knowledge is preferable, what is more important is that you have a willingness to learn a new technical area, a client service mentality, excellent coaching and communication skills and want to join a dynamic team that provides critical business support to the firm in a complex and changing regulatory environment. On the job training on the Independence rules and processes will be provided.
What you’ll create and do
As an Independence Specialist, you’ll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping to solve complex business issues from strategy to execution. Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Participation in the various Independence support systems, processes and activities
Collaborating with the Service Delivery Center (SDC) teams responsible for certain Independence processes and activities
Responding to Independence queries from partners, staff and engagement teams across the firm, promoting Independence knowledge sharing
Delivering training to business units where required
Monitoring compliance with Independence policies, processes and controls
Performing compliance testing over client engagement teams activities
Involvement with the innovation and development of Independence processes and PwC Global initiatives
Participation in ad hoc Independence projects
What you’ll bring to this role
An interest in upskilling for a digital world and technology trends, and an openness to learning new tools and adapting how you work
Previous experience in financial services or audit is an asset
High level of accuracy, attention to detail and experience in analysing data
Strong client service focus in dealing with partners and staff at all levels and areas of the firm
Demonstrated ability to work in a multitasked, fast-paced and changing environment
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
Good time and project management skills
Good judgment and problem-solving skills
What you’ll get in return
Opportunity to interact with partners and practice teams across the firm, and Independence Specialists from across the PwC Global network
Wide exposure to the breadth of the firm’s services and how we deliver these services
Development of technical knowledge of a key area of Firm regulatory risk

The successful candidate will be responsible for obtaining municipal rates figures, clearance figures and rates clearance certificates for property transfers, primarily from the City of Johannesburg, City of Tshwane and Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality.

Matric / Grade 12
Previous experience dealing with municipal rates and clearance certificates is essential.
Experience with the City of Johannesburg, City of Tshwane and/or Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality is essential.
Previous experience in a conveyancing, property or legal environment is highly advantageous.
Previous experience with Deeds Office lodgements and linking lists will be highly advantageous.
Valid driver's licence and own reliable vehicle.
Good computer literacy, including Microsoft Office and Excel.
Strong administrative and organisational skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Duties and responsibilities include, but not limited to:
Municipal Rates Figures & Certificates
Apply for municipal rates and clearance figures for property transfers.
Apply for and obtain municipal rates clearance certificates.
Submit applications and supporting documentation to the relevant municipalities.
Monitor applications from submission through to issue of the certificate.
Ensure all municipal requirements are correctly submitted.
Follow up on outstanding applications and certificates.
Download, receive, check and save municipal documentation on the firm's systems.
Ensure rates figures and certificates are obtained within the required conveyancing timeframes
Municipal Follow-Up & Problem Solving
Conduct regular follow-ups with municipal departments regarding outstanding applications.
Attend the City of Johannesburg, City of Tshwane and Ekurhuleni municipal offices when required.
Resolve queries relating to:
Incorrect municipal accounts
Outstanding or incorrect balances
Incorrect property information
Ownership discrepancies
Incorrect property valuations
Meter readings and municipal services
Payments not allocated correctly
Incorrect clearance figures
Delays in the issuing of clearance certificates
Other municipal account and billing-related issues
Liaise directly with municipal officials to resolve problems.
Escalate complex or unresolved matters to the relevant manager or conveyancer.
Maintain professional working relationships with municipal officials.
Identify when external rates agents must be appointed.
Laise with external agencies (where necessary)
Deeds Office & Lodgement Support
Assist conveyancers and conveyancing teams with preparing Deeds Office lodgement packs.
Check that documents required for lodgement are available and properly prepared.
Assist with arranging documents in the correct order for lodgement.
Prepare and draft linking lists for lodgement.
Ensure linking lists accurately correspond with the documents contained in each lodgement batch.
Assist with checking that all required supporting documents are included before lodgement.
Identify missing, incomplete or incorrectly prepared documents and bring these to the attention of the relevant conveyancer.
Assist with the preparation of documents for physical or electronic lodgement, as applicable.
Assist the conveyancer with resolving administrative issues relating to lodgement.
Maintain accurate records of documents prepared and matters ready for lodgement.
Assist with Deeds Office-related administrative tasks and follow-ups when required.
Conveyancing Support
Work closely with conveyancers, paralegals and transfer teams to ensure municipal and lodgement requirements are obtained timeously.
Monitor municipal and lodgement deadlines in line with the firm's transfer timelines.
Provide regular updates to the relevant conveyancing team.
Identify matters that may impact registration and escalate these proactively.
Assist with urgent municipal and lodgement matters where required to prevent delays in registration.
Assist the conveyancer with general administrative tasks relating to the progression of transfer matters.

Maintain an accurate municipal rates and lodgement tracker for all matters.
Update the firm's systems and spreadsheets regularly and accurately.
Keep proper records of applications, correspondence, payments, figures and certificates.
Ensure all municipal and lodgement documentation is properly filed on the firm's electronic filing system.
Provide regular reports on outstanding rates applications, certificates and lodgement requirements.
Follow up on aged or delayed applications until resolved.
Ensure that all actions and updates are recorded promptly and accurately.

IGrow Wealth Investments Group of Companies, proudly positioned as South Africa’s #1 Investment company, is seeking an analytical, firm but fair Head of Collections (Credit Vetting and Tenant Billing) to join our team in Midrand, Gauteng or Durbanville, Cape Town.
This role serves as the operational backbone of IGrow Rentals' credit risk, tenant billing and collections function. The individual is responsible for vetting prospective tenants' creditworthiness and affordability prior to lease approval, ensuring tenants are billed accurately and timeously each month, and driving the collection of outstanding rental and other charges to minimise arrears and bad debt across the rental portfolio.
IGrow Group of Companies is a scaling business, and this role is intentionally positioned as a foundation for growth. As the group expands its rentals footprint across South Africa and beyond, we foresee a clear and exciting progression path for the right individual.
Minimum requirements (Advantageous):
National Diploma or Degree in Finance, Accounting, Credit Management, Risk Management or a related field.
Minimum 5 years' experience in a credit control, collections, billing or credit vetting role, of which at least 2 years are in a management/supervisory capacity.
Proven track record of managing a collections/credit book and improving arrears/recovery rates.
Experience in property management, rentals or a related financial services environment.
Strong understanding of credit vetting principles, affordability assessment and the National Credit Act.
Strong leadership and people-management skills, with the ability to manage a team responsible for vetting, billing and collections.
Highly numerate, with strong attention to detail and reconciliation skills.
Confident and firm communicator, comfortable handling difficult conversations with tenants and internal stakeholders regarding payments and arrears.
Experience with property management/billing software and CRM platforms (Zoho CRM, WeConnectU RAMS experience prefered).
Strong reporting skills, with the ability to compile and present arrears, billing and collections data to EXCO.
Proactive, solutions-oriented mindset, with the ability to design and implement new processes.
Ability to work independently and take full ownership of the collections and vetting function.
Duties and responsibilities include, but not limited to:
Reporting Structure & Cross-Functional Relationships
Reports directly to the Rentals CEO, with functional oversight of the Collections, Credit Vetting, Tenant Billing and AI Collection Agent sub-functions.
Maintains close working relationships with Portfolio Management, Finance and Legal, while remaining organisationally independent of Asset Management/Portfolio Management, so the role can hold those functions to account without a conflict of interest.
Owns the collection outcome, while Portfolio Managers continue to be responsible for the accuracy of the underlying tenant and lease data, supplying the documentation needed to support collection, keeping investors informed on arrears, and resolving property-level tenant queries and disputes at source.
Works with Finance to keep tenant billing and collections data reconciled; Finance continues to own the general ledger, accounting controls and financial reconciliation.
Reports on collection rates, arrears ageing, recovery rates, bad debt, credit vetting performance and billing accuracy, with visibility at Rentals leadership/EXCO level, while remaining under the direct line management of the Rentals CEO.
Credit Vetting & Tenant Screening
Own and continuously refine the tenant credit vetting process, including affordability checks, credit bureau/TPN checks, reference checks and employment verification.
Set and enforce minimum affordability and credit criteria for tenant approval, in line with IGrow's risk appetite.
Review and approve or decline borderline applications, escalating high-risk cases to the appropriate manager.
Track vetting turnaround times and ensure SLAs are met so as not to delay lease signing.
Regularly review vetting criteria against actual arrears/default outcomes and adjust criteria accordingly.
Ensure that the vetting process is conducted thoroughly on every placement, without unnecessarily declining applications in a way that leads to increased vacancy, while ensuring the collection department is set up for high rental collection rates downstream.
Tenant Billing
Oversee the accurate and timeous monthly billing of all tenants, including rental, utilities, levies and other recoverable charges.
Ensure billing systems and tenant ledgers are correctly configured and maintained, including escalations, pro-rata charges and once-off adjustments.
Manage the resolution of billing queries and disputes raised by tenants or Portfolio Managers.
Reconcile tenant statements against lease agreements and escalation schedules to ensure accuracy.
Ensure the monthly tenant billing process is conducted accurately and on time to allow for the collection process to be conducted promptly and effectively.
Collections & Arrears Management
Lead the collections function for the rental portfolio, driving down days-in-arrears and bad debt write-offs.
Set and manage collections KPIs, including collection rate, arrears ageing and recovery rate, and report on these to EXCO/Management.
Design and implement a structured arrears escalation process, including reminders, demand letters, payment arrangements and legal handover, in conjunction with Legal/attorneys where required.
Manage relationships with debt collection agencies, attorneys and credit bureaus as needed.
Negotiate and monitor payment arrangements with tenants in arrears, escalating non-compliance appropriately.
Reporting & Analytics
Compile monthly collections, arrears and credit vetting performance reports for EXCO/Management review.
Analyse arrears trends by portfolio, agent and property to identify systemic risk areas.
Monitor the financial impact of bad debt and rental losses and recommend mitigating strategies.
Set up daily collection dashboards to monitor team collection progress.
Process, Systems & Compliance
Maintain and improve the systems and processes used for vetting, billing and collections, including CRM and property management/billing software.
Ensure all credit vetting, billing and collections activity complies with the National Credit Act, POPIA and other relevant legislation.
Liaise with Finance to ensure billing and collections data reconciles with the general ledger.
Train and support Portfolio Managers and Rental Agents on vetting criteria and billing/collections processes.
Schedule the collection plan for the month amongst the IGrow Rentals Collections department team members and AI Collection Agents.
Monitor team and AI Agent performance.
Cross-Departmental Coordination
Act as the key point of contact between Rentals, Finance and Portfolio Management on all matters relating to tenant credit risk, billing and collections.
Attend relevant Rentals and Finance meetings to align on arrears risk, write-offs and process changes.
Provide prompt, complete and accurate debt collection notes on all accounts to be made available to the Asset Management department for investor feedback.
Carry delegated authority within this function, including setting and enforcing credit and vetting criteria, approving or escalating borderline applications within agreed parameters, determining collection procedures and deadlines, agreeing payment arrangements within set limits, initiating legal handover recommendations, and requiring billing corrections — extending to holding other departments to account where an arrears issue originates outside Collections.

Job Description:
About the role
We are seeking a Treasury Manager who will report directly to the Group Treasurer and serve as a senior execution partner across Lesaka's funding, liquidity and financial risk agenda.
The role will take day-to-day ownership of debt facilities and covenant monitoring, strengthen cash and liquidity management across the Group, and support the management of interest rate and foreign exchange exposures.
The successful candidate must combine technical treasury depth with disciplined execution, sound commercial judgement and the ability to work across a complex group structure.
Key Responsibilities
Debt funding and working capital management
Manage the Group's debt portfolio, including revolving credit, working capital, overdraft, guarantee and other committed or uncommitted facilities.
Maintain a complete view of facility limits, utilisation, pricing, maturity profiles, security, guarantees and key contractual obligations.
Prepare funding requirements and utilisation requests, coordinate drawdowns and repayments, and confirm that funding is available when required.
Own the covenant monitoring process, including calculation review, sensitivity testing, compliance certificates and the evidence supporting lender submissions.
Track undertakings, reporting deadlines, and other obligations under funding agreements.
Build and maintain effective relationships with lenders, facility agents, debt advisers, legal advisers.
Partner with business units and finance teams to understand working capital drivers and identify practical opportunities to release cash and reduce funding costs.
Liquidity and cash management
Maintain reliable daily and forward-looking visibility of cash, available facilities and liquidity headroom across the Group.
Manage and improve cash pooling, sweeping, offset, netting and intercompany funding arrangements within legal, tax, regulatory and facility constraints.
Optimise the allocation of surplus cash and short-term borrowings to reduce interest expense and improve returns within approved risk limits.
Oversee bank account structures, signatories, mandates, bank fees and cash management services in partnership with finance, legal and operational teams.
Provide timely liquidity reporting to the Group Treasurer and senior management, highlighting forecast pressure points, concentration risk and available mitigants.
Interest rate and foreign exchange risk management
Identify, quantify and report the Group's interest rate and foreign exchange exposures, including exposures arising from debt, cash flows, acquisitions and cross-border operations.
Support the design and execution of approved hedging strategies using appropriate instruments, including swaps, forwards and options where relevant.
Monitor hedge positions, counterparty limits, valuations, settlements and documentation, including ISDA and related confirmations where applicable.
Work with Finance and Accounting to support accurate accounting, valuation, disclosure and control over treasury instruments.
Cash flow forecasting and treasury technology
Own and continuously improve short-term and medium-term cash flow forecasting, including variance analysis, forecast accuracy and clear accountability for business inputs.
Translate business plans, working capital trends, debt service and transaction activity into an integrated liquidity and funding forecast.
Support the selection, implementation and effective use of a treasury management system and related bank connectivity, reporting and workflow tools.
Improve the quality, timeliness and automation of treasury data, dashboards and management reporting.
Governance, controls and stakeholder support
Operate within approved treasury policies, delegated authorities, facility agreements and regulatory requirements, and recommend updates where controls or operating needs change.
Support internal and external audit requests and ensure that findings are resolved within agreed timelines.
Provide treasury input into acquisitions, disposals, new products and other strategic initiatives, with a focus on funding, liquidity and financial risk implications.
Act as a trusted treasury partner to Group Finance, business unit finance teams, Legal, Tax, Risk, Operations and executive stakeholders.
Experience
At least 7 years of relevant treasury experience, with substantial exposure to a complex corporate group, financial institution or similarly regulated environment.
Strong practical experience in corporate debt funding, facility management, covenant monitoring and lender engagement.
Demonstrated experience in liquidity management, cash pooling, cash concentration or offset arrangements and working capital optimisation.
Practical knowledge of interest rate and foreign exchange risk management, including hedging instruments and transaction execution.
Experience building or operating cash flow forecasts and producing decision-useful treasury reporting.
Hands-on experience with a treasury management system, online banking platforms and ERP or financial reporting systems.
Advanced Excel and financial modelling capability. Experience with data visualisation or reporting automation will be advantageous.
Technical knowledge
Corporate funding instruments, debt documentation, guarantees, security structures and covenant frameworks.
Liquidity risk management, cash pooling, intercompany funding and short-term investment principles.
Interest rate and foreign exchange markets, derivatives, confirmations, settlements and counterparty risk.
Treasury accounting concepts, financial controls and relevant regulatory considerations, including exchange control where applicable.
Treasury systems, bank connectivity, cash forecasting methods and management information design.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related discipline.
A relevant postgraduate qualification or professional designation such as CA(SA), ACT, CFA or FRM will be advantageous.
Key working relationships
Internal stakeholders include the Group Treasurer, CFO and executive management, Group Finance, business unit finance teams, Legal, Tax, Risk, Operations, Internal Audit and M&A or strategic projects.
External stakeholders include relationship banks, lenders, facility agents, debt advisers, legal advisers, auditors, treasury technology providers and other financial service providers.
Role context
This is a hands-on senior treasury role. It requires a person who can independently manage detailed funding and liquidity processes while also providing concise analysis and recommendations to the Group Treasurer.
The role will suit someone who is comfortable working across multiple legal entities, responding to time-sensitive requirements and helping to strengthen a centralised Group Treasury capability.

Job Description
Lesaka Merchant Division
Sales Administrator - Mpumalanga (Witbank)
Do you enjoy working with data and turning information into clear, useful insights? Do you love keeping processes organised, spotting the details that matter, and making sure nothing gets missed?
Do you get satisfaction from following an issue through to resolution and helping a team stay on track? Do you enjoy supporting a sales team and helping create smooth, efficient day-to-day operations?
As a
Sales Administrator
, you’ll support the Merchant Sales Team through accurate reporting, effective administrative coordination, and reliable operational support. Working closely with the Senior Administrator and Area Sales Manager, you’ll help keep information up to date, priorities visible, and the team organised so they can focus on delivering results.
Role and Responsibilities
As Sales Administrator, you will provide reliable administrative and reporting support to the Merchant sales team.
You will manage recurring sales reports and dashboards, maintain accurate records, support device and stock administration, and assist managers with operational requirements.
You will work closely with Sales Colleagues, Area Sales Managers, the Senior Administrator, Regional Manager and relevant internal departments to ensure information is accurate, actions are followed up and issues are escalated appropriately.
A key part of the role is using available reports to identify devices that have stopped trading, escalating these matters to the appropriate managers and following up with the relevant department to support resolution.
The role requires strong attention to detail, good organisation and the ability to manage routine responsibilities alongside ad-hoc requests in a busy sales environment.
Day in the Life
You start your day by reviewing the latest information and reports to identify priorities for the sales team. You prepare or update daily, weekly or monthly reports and convert relevant information into dashboards for Area Sales Managers.
You review data relating to devices that have stopped trading and identify matters requiring attention. Where necessary, you escalate these to the appropriate manager and follow up with the relevant department to ensure outstanding issues are addressed.
Throughout the day, you support the sales team with administrative requests, update records, assist with device orders and contribute to stock-taking activities. You may also provide administrative support to the Regional Manager or assist with an ad-hoc project that requires additional coordination.
The role combines independent work with regular interaction across the sales team. You will need to organise your workload, manage competing priorities and communicate clearly when information, action or escalation is required.
The position operates Monday to Friday during standard office hours, with weekend work on a rotational basis when required.
Who You Are
You are an organised and dependable administrator who enjoys working with information, systems and people. You take ownership of your work, pay attention to detail and are comfortable working independently while contributing to a wider team.
Matric / Grade 12.
3–5 years' administrative experience, preferably in a sales or operational environment.
Experience working with data, reports and administrative information.
Experience using CRM systems; knowledge of CR and Freshdesk is advantageous.

Company Details: The HSRC was established in 1968 as South Africa’s statutory research agency and has grown to become the largest dedicated research institute in the social sciences and humanities on the African continent, doing cutting-edge public research in areas that are crucial to development. Our mand...read moreate is to inform the effective formulation and monitoring of government policy; to evaluate policy implementation; to stimulate public debate through the effective dissemination of research-based data and fact-based research results; to foster research collaboration; and to help build research capacity and infrastructure for the human sciences. The Council conducts large-scale, policy-relevant, social-scientific research for public sector users, non-governmental organisations and international development agencies. Research activities and structures are closely aligned with South Africa’s national development priorities. The HSRC’s integrated research programmes provide single points of entry – complete with a critical mass of researchers – for interdisciplinary and problem-orientated research in the following areas: Africa Institute of South Africa Democracy, Governance and Service Delivery Economic Performance and Development Education and Skills Development Human and Social Development Population Health, Health Systems and Innovation Social Aspects of HIV/AIDS, STIs and TB. A cross-cutting entity, Research Use and Impact Assessment, seeks to extend and enhance the use and impact of scientific research from the HSRC and other sources of research; and to manage the HSRC’s relationships, reputation and brand. The organisation is home to about 500 staff members, all dedicated to support the conducting of 150-200 projects per year on social science and humanities research. Our dedicated professional researchers, located in four provinces, are supported by a strong physical and institutional infrastructure, including technical and support positions, deployed countrywide to enable the organisation to respond efficiently and comprehensively to research needs. To strategically manage all these processes, procedures and research projects the HSRC has appointed two deputy chief executive officers responsible for research and operations. On another level, the HSRC seeks to serve as a knowledge hub to bridge the gap between research, policy and action, thereby increasing the impact of research. This role is implemented through collaboration with key constituencies, including government and other research organisations, multilateral agencies, universities, and non-governmental, donor and development organisations. These relationships are being strengthened by the fact that many of our leading researchers serve on international scientific bodies. We also monitor and evaluate policies and programmes providing objective information to assess the country’s progress in achieving its goals. Three examples of these are our contributions to monitor the country’s performance in implementing the South Africa’s national HIV and AIDS strategic plans and policies; assessments of numeracy and literacy in education; and conducting an annual research and development (R&D) survey that informs the national R&D strategy. We have a strong footprint in other African countries through our affiliation with CODESRIA, participation in SADC and NEPAD, as well as hosting African Research Fellows in the organisation. The HSRC also has a global presence and will be hosting the 2015 World Social Science Forum (WSSF) in Durban, South Africa in September 2015 and has hosted the Gender Summit Africa in April 2015. The WSSF looks at demonstrating the global presence, impact and authority of social sciences. The Council is also a member of the UNESCO High Panel: Science for Development where it looks at strategies for promoting sustainable development and advancing poverty eradication. The HSRC has established a BRICS Research Centre as South Africa continues to play an integral part of the BRICS countries. Since April 2014, the Africa Institute of South Africa (AISA) has been incorporated into the HSRC. The Council’s research outputs include reports for users, occasional papers and scholarly articles in peer-reviewed journals, books and a news magazine that allows us to improve the public understanding of science. These are disseminated in print through the HSRC Press, through policy briefs aimed at government and policy-makers, and through the media, including social media platforms, our website, conferences and extensive research networks. The Council has several world-class operational support programmes who are led by the Deputy CEO: Management and Support. The Council’s finance, human resource management, enterprise and risk management, governance, legal and facilities units are well set up to provide good quality support to all research programmes and potential funders of the HSRC.

Job Purpose
The National Distribution Manager is responsible for developing and leading the Company's national distribution strategy to ensure the safe, efficient and cost-effective movement of raw materials and finished goods across the supply chain. The role is accountable for the end-to-end management of inbound, outbound, inter-distribution centre and cross-border transport operations, ensuring products are delivered on time, in full and in compliance with all legislative and customer requirements.
The incumbent is responsible for optimising transport performance through effective carrier management, strategic distribution sourcing, Transport Management System (TMS) governance, company fleet utilisation and continuous cost improvement initiatives. Working closely with Planning, Procurement, Manufacturing, Distribution, Finance and Commercial teams, the National Distribution Manager ensures transport capacity, service delivery and distribution costs are effectively managed to support business growth, customer service excellence and operational efficiency.

National Distribution Planning & Execution

Manage transport rate structures, fuel levy mechanisms and commercial performance measures.
Ensure service level agreements remain aligned to business requirements and customer expectations.
Evaluate supplier performance and implement initiatives to improve commercial outcomes.
Support strategic sourcing initiatives that strengthen long-term transport capability.
Company Fleet & Asset Utilisation
Optimise the deployment and utilisation of company-owned fleet assets across the national distribution network.
Maximise fleet productivity while reducing reliance on external transport providers where commercially viable.
Monitor fleet utilisation, capacity and operational performance.
Coordinate company fleet deployment with distribution planning requirements.
Identify opportunities to improve asset utilisation and operational efficiency.
Support fleet replacement planning and capital investment decisions.
Ensure company fleet operations contribute to overall transport cost optimisation.
Export & Cross-Border Distribution Management
Manage cross-border distribution operations in accordance with applicable customs and legislative requirements.
Ensure export documentation is complete, accurate and compliant with regulatory requirements.
Manage relationships with customs brokers, distribution agents and cross-border transport providers.
Monitor export service performance and implement improvements where required.
Ensure transport providers maintain all required operating licences and permits.

Analyse distribution costs and identify opportunities for operational and commercial optimisation.
Manage distribution invoice validation to ensure compliance with approved rates and contractual agreements.
Deliver sustainable transport cost savings while maintaining required service levels.
Support accurate month-end reporting, forecasting and distribution cost accruals.
Provide meaningful transport cost analysis to support strategic decision-making.

Maintain effective transport governance processes that minimise operational and commercial risk.
Monitor compliance with transport safety standards, documentation and load securing requirements.
Manage transport-related claims, investigations and corrective actions.
Support internal and external audit requirements through effective transport governance.
Ensure transport documentation is maintained in accordance with company policies and legal requirements.
Promote a culture of safety, compliance and operational excellence across distribution operations.

Promote innovation and best practice across national distribution operations.

Escalate concerns appropriately and ensure agreed mitigation actions are tracked to resolution.

Prepare or support submissions to relevant governance forums where decisions or approvals are required.

Building sustainable books of business.
Helping IC’s increase income and productivity.

Coordinating support across Operations, Risk, Compliance and Product teams.
Ensuring advisers can focus on sales and client acquisition.

Job Description:
The Process Engineer will be part of an engineering team providing engineering services and/or field support. Client liaison and maintaining the focus of the project on achieving unprecedented and sustained business results for the client is a large part of the work.
The role will require the engineer to oversee, guide and develop solutions in all areas of the process plant across various systems, unit operations and process equipment. Specific tasks may include the development of process engineering deliverables; solutions to infield problems; and involvement in the execution and commissioning of these solutions.
The Process Engineer may be required to act as Lead Process Engineer, on specific assignments, responsible for coordinating the process engineering team, oversee and guide the development of process engineering deliverables ensuring they meet the project’s scope, are delivered on schedule and budget, and meet Hatch’s quality standards. Experience in Gold Concentrator design.
Key Responsibilities Include:
Perform process engineering tasks on Minerals Processing projects, in a variety of commodities
When requested, act as Lead Process Engineer on projects or studies
Operate with full competence and independence in the execution of all design calculations, design criteria, in the compilation and execution of equipment lists and calculations.
Develop new criteria/calculations where required, maintaining high levels of accuracy. Provide frequent training, guidance and supervision to junior colleagues
Actively engage with clients to understand project requirements
Process scope definition and technology selection
Define the process design criteria
Define the process block flow diagram and unit operations
Compilation of Process Flow Diagrams, along with associated mass and energy balance calculations
Undertake trade off studies to resolve options
Identify, scope and manage process test work (on site or laboratory based)
Conduct capacity analysis for existing plants
Select the equipment for projects
Carry out engineering design calculations and equipment sizing calculations
Prepare specifications of process attributes for equipment, through compilation of process datasheets (or process input to general datasheets).
Compilation of Process Description
Design of the process control logic adhering to appropriate safety standards, and documentation into Functional Descriptions
Display full competence and independence in the compilation of P&IDs and all levels of control philosophies.
Ensure process specifications portray the appropriate information and design intent and review of equipment bids
Liaising with other discipline engineers to ensure designs conform to process requirements
Contribute to hazard studies
Compile operating cost estimates including estimation of consumables, labor, maintenance materials and power
Provide input to capital cost estimates
Prepare well written project reports
Play a lead role in site commissioning of new equipment and process systems
Participate in the preparation of proposals and other business development initiatives.
Qualifications and Experience:
Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering or Mineral Processing degree.
Minimum of 10 years’ experience
Experience supporting engineering studies including scope studies, Preliminary Economic Assessments (PEA), Pre-Feasibility Studies (PFS), and Feasibility Studies.
Extensive design, commissioning and/or operational experience in gold processing facilities
Experience in scoping and management of metallurgical testwork programs (benchscale, pilot scale, on-site testing)
Experience in modelling of gold processing equipment and systems
Strong client focus.
Ability to lead engineering tasks on a project, within the allocated budget and schedule, including mentoring and guidance of junior colleagues and professional interaction with other project disciplines
Ability to manage individuals to attain quality, cost and schedule objectives.

Role Purpose
The Business Development & Digital Solution Consultant is an intermediate-level role designed to support and accelerate Hatch’s Digital Business Development activities across the Africa and Middle East mining markets. The role acts as the commercial, analytical and coordination engine behind early‑stage client engagement, pre‑sales, opportunity development and specialised delivery.
Working closely with the Regional Director - Digital, Business Development Executive – Digital, and global Principal Consultants, this role owns activities across market research, client outreach, pursuit coordination, proposal administration, internal alignment with technical SMEs, early-stage value assessment and project execution.
Over time, the incumbent will be developed into a subject matter expert (SME) able to manage accounts, shape opportunities independently, and close end‑to‑end sales cycles for selected digital products and solutions with opportunities to deliver specific consulting roles on earmarked projects, aligned with candidate's core technical abilities.
Key Responsibilities
Business Development & Client Engagement
Conduct initial client outreach to introduce Hatch Digital capabilities.
Build early-stage client relationships to understand needs, challenges, and value opportunities.
Attend client meetings independently and alongside senior BD leaders.
Manage assigned accounts, and co‑manage key accounts with the Principal Consultant / BD Executive.
Qualify early-stage opportunities and align appropriate internal SMEs.
Pre‑Sales & Opportunity Development
Lead early opportunity assessment, including gathering requirements, value drivers, and solution options.
Conduct market, competitor and technology research across Africa and Middle East mining markets.
Draft initial proposal structures, scope outlines, and solution narratives.
Coordinate with technical teams to close required information gaps and with delivery teams to plan, estimate, and shape solution proposals.
Support financial modelling, value case framing, and preparation of commercial packages.
Proposal & Pursuit Management
Owned for assigned accounts; shared for key accounts.
Administer bid timelines, compliance requirements, and submission quality.
Manage the pursuit tracker ensuring visibility of all leads, pursuits, and proposals.
Prepare pursuit win strategies, including competitive positioning, solution differentiators, pricing considerations, and client value framing.

Job Description:
Position Purpose
The Project Director (PD) Liquid Fuels reporting to the General Manager, Capital & Strategic Projects, R&D and CI (GM C&SP), is accountable for ensuring the efficient and effective scoping and further development of a Transnet Pipelines (TPL) mega programme/ project in the fuels segment. Cognisance must be taken of the Transnet Group fuel business strategy and the delivery of studies/ projects that form part of the mega programme/ project. The PD has the overall accountability for the scope, cost, schedule and quality management of a fuels mega programme/ project in the study phases and the mega project if approved to be implemented.
Position Outputs
The PD Liquid Fuels is to use his/ her extensive knowledge of liquid fuel projects and operations business to further develop the roadmap of Transnet Group’s Fuel Strategy translation into a more well defined TPL Liquid Fuels Strategy and implementation plan. The liquid fuel strategy includes for current fuel business and future business eg. MPP Phase IV Tanks, TFIT phase 1 (diesel/ jet fuel) and phase 2 (petrol), PL6 (jet fuel).
Ensure that the study/ project governance structures eg Sponsor appointment, MANCO, STEERCO are put in place under the Sponsor’s stewardship and endorsed by the GM C&SP and executed safely and in compliance with all regulatory requirements, company policies, standing instructions and safe working procedures.
Develop an appropriate organisation structure for set up of the liquid fuels business and execution of the project, identify functions necessary, and select appropriately experienced and competent personnel for specific positions and delegate responsibilities. Identify part-time team members in conjunction with other functional GMs. Ensure that the set up conforms to the requirements of the TPL Programme Management Office (PMO) and is approved by the GM C&SP. Key stakeholders in the PMO are the GM C&SP and the Senior Manager Project Controls.
Establish specific procedures relevant to fuels business set up and project implementation of each phase and arrange preparation of the Project Charter and Project Execution Plan (PEP).
Identify and apply fuels business best practices in line with ones DoA.
Identify investment risks, apply lessons learned on projects, implement risk mitigation actions and initiatives.
Identify and ensure that the studies/ projects are executed safely and in compliance with all regulatory requirements, company policies, standing instructions and working procedures.
Set study/ project goals and objectives, identify priorities, clearly communicate these to team members and appropriate other parties, and provide leadership in their implementation. Motivate, ensure commitment and build a results oriented team focused on achieving viable and cost effective outcomes for Transnet.
Direct, control and manage through project personnel all aspects of the liquid fuel studies including any in-house engineering, procurement, interfaces, administration functions and all external work undertaken by contractors and consultants throughout the study design phases.
Overview and ensure that work and progress on the liquid fuel studies and mega projects will satisfy the Sponsor(s) and TPL EXCO expectations.
Maintain a relationship with clients at an executive level.
Maintain and display clear “ownership” and accountability for delivery of fuel studies and mega projects’ business outcomes.
Ensure initiation and execution of the work is in accordance with the PEP, such that completion of the study/ project is achieved by the authorised completion date, within the authorised budget and meets the required quality requirements.
Ensure that all communication channels are effectively operating amongst project team members and other functions and that co-ordination and co-operation between disciplines is occurring.
Co-ordinate the development of a study/ project budget derived from the initial or proposal budget and a corresponding study/ project implementation schedule. Conduct monthly project progress and cost estimate review meetings. Responsible for finalising decisions with key stakeholders regarding short term/ long terms and capital versus operating cost trade-offs for the liquid fuel business.
Ensure the final forecast estimate to completion is updated and maintained and that EXCO is briefed monthly of the forecast final costs.
Monitor and measure the work being executed regularly against schedule, milestone deliverables and study/ capital expenditure budgets.
Recommend and implement corrective strategies where needed to best meet Transnet’s overall study/ project objectives.
Transition the study into the project’s execution phase (if it passes gate reviews, business case approval and capital allocation sanctions).
Set the projects goals and business objectives, including scope, cost, time safety, start-up and risk, etc.
Ensure adherence to the project’s authorised Scope of Work, monitor scope status and advise the client accordingly.
Define and delegate the study/ project’s roles and assign levels of approval and authority in accordance with Transnet’s Delegation of Authority (DoA).
Develops the operating and maintenance strategies, commissioning/ project handover based on owner’s team input if the project progresses to the execution and construction phase.
Achieve the LTI and injury/incident frequency rate targets as included in the PEP for the study/ project as a whole through demonstrating personal commitment to safety and by implementing systems both in the office and on site (if project progresses to bankable feasibility study and execution) to promote safety awareness and create a “safety first” culture. Fulfil statutory obligations as Safety Administrator for areas of responsibility.
Be responsible for communication with the client, particularly as regards requests for changes and modifications. Ensure contractual commitments regarding deliverables are met.
Engage in all decision making about the study/ project’s implementation that is not delegated to subordinate project management.
Review and approve the monthly study/ project progress report prepared for the client and/ or for distribution to other parties.
Provide inputs in writing and submission of Business Cases for approval by CAPIC at TPL or FIC at Group level.
Control the project’s capital if it progresses to feasibility (FEL3) and maintains strict controls on variations and contingency. Manages and recommends changes to FFCs and PCNs on PEPs, other than originally stated.
Responsible for developing and concluding decisions with the client/ sponsor about the fuels business short term and medium term goals and objectives.
Sign third party procurement contracts within the approved delegated framework limits as the Client. Manage suppliers, service providers and contracts in terms of performance against project contracts and SLAs.
Participate and attend Procurement Committee meetings and attend bid clarification meetings.
Lead, coach and mentor by supporting staff development and skills transfer especially in terms of fuels business knowledge and practices.
Is to ensure sound capital investment programme/ project planning, execution and management in line with Capital & Strategic Projects business priorities, and aligned with Group and TPL liquid fuel business strategy.
Is to ensure that for the fuel mega projects has an integrated, planned and co-ordinated approach to enable operations to achieve medium to long term business targets and objectives.
Is to provide routine and regular feedback to the Project Sponsor(s), the GM C&SP and the relevant functional leadership in Projects (the Senior Manager Project Controls and Principal Construction Manager) on progress, issues and areas of concern.
Is to be a hands-on senior/ executive manager with significant experience in liquid fuels projects development and execution. As such, he will participate in project related activities, as necessary, during the studies and projects and will be familiar with all aspects of the liquid fuel business projects set up, governance, controls and implementation.
Has the delegated authority (as per DoA) to make decisions and co-ordinate overall needs and direction related to the liquid fuels business in liaison with the GM C&SP.
Will review the progress of mega studies/ mega project regularly with the GM C&SP & Senior Manager Project Controls and the business project team as necessary.
Provides senior level support, advice and guidance to the liquid fuels mega project; and will assist with the resolution of major issues, problems and policy conflicts; removes project obstacles that require high level intervention.
Will be active in reviewing the scope to ensure it meets his customer needs; endorses scope changes for CPOT approval, signs off major deliverables; and signs off on project approvals to proceed to each succeeding project phase as per the PLP process.
Fulfils the role of direct liaison officer with TPL Customers and Stakeholders and supports the GM C&SP in terms of Public Regulatory & Government interactions related to the Liquid fuels business.
Qualifications and Experience
Mandatory; BSc Eng / B Eng / BSc Honours Construction Management or equivalent Professional Registration as PrCPM in terms of SACPCMP requirements Advantageous: Masters / Bachelors in management related disciplines i.e. MBA, MBL, MSc Project Management, BCom is preferred Professional Registration as Pr Eng in terms of ECSA is preferred. PMP Certification/ equivalent is preferred. Experience: Min 12 Years total experience (preferably in hydrocarbons/ petrochemicals) of which Min 8 years within a Senior Project Management position that meets PrCPM registration and Min 4 years Technical experience within the Liquid Fuels industry. Drivers licence code 8 or B

Position Purpose
The Database Specialist is responsible for managing, optimizing, and securing databases across (hybrid) cloud and on-premises environments, predominantly on the Microsoft Azure Cloud platform. The role involves designing, implementing and managing database solutions that ensure high availability, performance, and scalability while supporting the organisation’s ongoing transition and migration of from database services between the cloud and on-premises environments.
Position Outputs
The Database Specialist will: Design, implement, and manage scalable and secure database architectures across hybrid environments.
Optimize database performance through monitoring, indexing, and tuning strategies.
Implement and manage data migration from on-premises databases to Azure cloud services (e.g., Azure SQL, Cosmos DB).
Ensure data security and compliance with regulatory requirements such as POPIA and ISO 27001.
Provide disaster recovery and backup strategies using Azure Backup, Azure Site Recovery, and on-premises solutions.
Collaborate with application, network, and infrastructure teams to support database integration.
Document database environments, processes, and governance policies.
Monitor and troubleshoot database performance using tools like Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, and third-party solutions.
Qualifications and Experience
Qualifications, Experience & Inherent Job Requirements
A Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or a related field.
ITIL Foundation Certification (advantageous).
Must have at least two of the following Certification
Microsoft Certified: Azure Database Administrator Associate.
Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert.
Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Engineer Associate.
Microsoft Certified: SQL Server Database Administrator.
Oracle Database Certification (for organizations using multiple database platforms).
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) – for managing containerized databases.
CompTIA Security+ (for database security expertise) Certified Database Administrator) a plus.
Standard Job Requirements
Driver’s license code 08
Travel as required and approved.
Competencies
Technical Skills and Knowledge
Database Management Systems (DBMS): Expertise in managing SQL-based systems (e.g., SQL Server, Azure SQL) and NoSQL systems (e.g., Cosmos DB, MongoDB).
Cloud Integration: Proficiency in Azure data services such as Azure SQL Database, Azure Synapse Analytics, and Azure Data Factory.
Performance Tuning: Advanced skills in indexing, query optimization, and database tuning.
Data Migration: Experience in migrating large-scale databases to the cloud using tools like Azure Database Migration Service (DMS).
Data Security: Strong knowledge of encryption, role-based access control, and compliance requirements like POPIA.
Backup and Recovery: Proficiency in designing and managing database backup, replication, and disaster recovery solutions in hybrid environments.
Monitoring and Troubleshooting: Experience with Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, and third-party database performance monitoring tools.
Automation: Skills in automating routine tasks using PowerShell, T-SQL, or Python.
Documentation:
Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation of database configurations, schemas, and processes.
Soft Skills Required
Problem-Solving: Ability to troubleshoot complex database issues effectively.
Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills to liaise with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Collaboration: Work collaboratively with infrastructure, application, and security teams.
Adaptability: Quickly adapt to changing environments and technologies.
Attention to Detail: Ensure accuracy and precision in managing data and processes.
Leadership: Guide teams during migrations and service transitions, providing mentorship to junior members.
Strategic Thinking: Align database strategies with business goals and long-term organizational objectives.

Job Description:
We are seeking a registered educational psychologist to join our Student Support team as the school-based psychologist for the Senior Phase (Grades 4 – 7). The psychologist supports learners' emotional, learning, academic, cognitive, behavioural, social and developmental needs within the systems in which they function: family, school and peer group. This is done through direct intervention, consultation with teachers and parents/guardian’s and collaboration with the multi-disciplinary team to coordinate the right support at the right time. The psychologist also plays an active educational role, presenting psychoeducation workshops for learners, teachers and parents and contributing to the school's communications.
Duties and Responsibilities
Learning support, accommodations and concessions
Review existing accommodations and concessions for Grade 4 – 7 learners at regular intervals, and advise teachers, parents and the multi-disciplinary team on whether each remains appropriate, should be adjusted, or can be withdrawn.
Advise on the most suitable accommodations and concessions for each learner, informed by assessment findings, classroom evidence and specialist reports.
Oversee the process of applying for, implementing and monitoring accommodations and concessions for learners with specific learning barriers, in line with school policy and the requirements of the relevant assessment body.
Conduct and interpret phase-appropriate psychological, cognitive and academic assessments, including baseline academic screenings.
Work in partnership with teachers, head of departments to identify and address learners' learning needs, and to promote motivation and engagement.
Support key transitions, into Grade 4 and from Grade 7 into high school and ensure continuity of appropriate support.
Emotional, behavioural and social wellbeing
Provide short-term individual and group counselling.
Assess and intervene around learners' emotional and behavioural needs.
Promote positive peer relationships and a safe, inclusive school climate.
Respond to trauma and crisis situations, supporting learners, families and staff.
Working with teachers, parents and families
Guide and support teachers in meeting learners' learning and developmental needs.
Help families understand their child's needs through parent guidance and communicate regularly about progress.
Connect families with appropriate internal and external service providers.
Psychoeducation and communication
Design and facilitate psychoeducation workshops for learners, teachers and parents on topics relevant to the development, learning and wellbeing of Grade 4 – 7 learners (for example emotional regulation, friendships, digital wellbeing, study skills and transitions).
Contribute regularly to the school newsletter and other school communications, such as articles, wellbeing tips and parent resources.
Multi-disciplinary collaboration
Coordinate and case-manage referrals from stakeholders, including the Head of Academics, Primary School Principal, and monitor referrals to external professionals (e.g. speech-language, remedial and occupational therapy, and external psychologists).
Attend and contribute to regular multi-disciplinary team meetings, and case-manage feedback for learners in a therapeutic process.
Keep accurate, confidential month-to-month records of learners in interventions and therapies.
Promote effective working relationships between teachers and members of the multi disciplinary team.
Professional standards
Uphold the highest standards of professionalism and ethical practice as stipulated by the
Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA), including confidentiality and the management of dual roles.
Maintain HPCSA registration and medical indemnity and continue professional development relevant to this phase.
Report on work to relevant stakeholders, including the Head of Department, Head of Academic and the Primary School Principal.
Minimum Requirements
A master’s degree in educational psychology and current registration with the HPCSA as a psychologist.
A minimum of 5-year work experience.
Experience in psychometric assessment and in recommending and reviewing learning accommodations and concessions.
Appropriate educational experience in a mainstream school is preferable, ideally with learners aged 9 – 13.
A genuine commitment to working with children, adolescents, parents and staff.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including confidence in presenting to groups of learners, staff and parents and in writing for a general audience.
The ability to work as part of a team.
Creativity, and the ability to prioritise, multi-task and work under pressure.
Flexibility and availability to respond to trauma and crisis situations.
Computer literacy, with a sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
A valid police clearance certificate and sexual offenders' register clearance, as required of all staff working in a school.

Job Description:
Job Purpose
To educate clients on the convenience, security and functionality of digital and self-service solutions; processing cash transactions and cash fulfillment (i.e.balancing and replenishment) and performing first line device maintenance in order to meet business goals and exceed the client expectations.
Job Responsibilities
Client Engagement:
Address any concerns relating to the queue flow or digital devices.
Assist client to download online applications and resolve any log in issues.
Assist the client to buy value-added services (e.g. pre-paid data and airtime) online or through a self-service device.
Assist the client to obtain statements, cards and other relevant documentation from self-service zones.
Build and maintain client relationships by keeping clients informed of progress or action taken regarding their applications, queries and requests.
Discover client's service and digital needs through connecting, understanding and delivering financial solutions with care.
Educate clients and potential clients on how to subscribe and service their account.
Educate clients on self-service, digital functionality and features.
Facilitate a conversation with the client to assist them to complete their service needs online.
Identify quality sales leads and enable cross-selling (without advising) through client engagement, fulfilling, making suggestions, referring to the relevant department for action and by capturing it on the client management system.
Meet, greet, establish and clarify client needs and verify documentation and direct clients.
Nurture strong, long-standing client relationships.
Own the client request end to end and route for alternative intervention if not equipped to service the client.
Provide knowledgeable client service that fosters mutual trust and confidence.
Business Operations:
Accept and service cash transactions over the counter.
Action control check list applicable to teller, enquiries and foreign functions daily.
Balance and secure branch stock holding (e.g. cards).
Control the queuing process and prioritise clients with special needs.
Destroy old stock (e.g. cards) identified by reports.
Enable the further processing of inter-bank transfers by preparing all transactional documents and originals (WASTE) in the required format by the required deadline for hand over to couriers.
Ensure ATM/ID availability through balancing and loading of cash and attending to down devices by performing first line device maintenance support.
Execute on cash management (i.e. Treasury and holdings), cash efficiency and recycling strategies within the store.
Load cash, balance and provide first line device maintenance and replenishment of consumables of all store devices.
Minimize losses and ensure corrective action is taken by declaring any discrepancies in cash holdings.
Process client deposits, withdrawal, change for change and transfer requests by following relevant procedure and policies.
Process client forex requests by following the relevant procedures and policies (e.g. FBN, bills and transfers).
Risk and Compliance:
Mitigate risk by controlling counter and drop safe limits according to policy.
Prevent fraud and losses by adhering to mandates, as well as client and transaction authentication procedures and policies.
Nedbank Goals:
Act in the client's interest, inform the client, do what you say and promise, take accountability, and go the extra mile.
Contribute to the success of Nedbank through meeting your service excellence, teamwork and personal development goals whilst adhering to Nedbank security, operational and compliance procedures and policies.
Develop, retain and grow the business by delivering against individual and team goals that support a positive client experience.
Improve digital enticement and migration volumes to self-service devices and online channels.

Ensure the CIB’s technology infrastructure supports business needs, including scalability, security, and regulatory compliance, working in partnership with other teams within Group Technology
Champion the use of data-driven insights to enhance CIB decision-making and customer experiences.
Lead digital transformation initiatives unique to CIB, such as adopting AI or automation for CIBs processes.

Manage dependencies and timelines for Enterprise projects, ensuring minimal disruption to CIB’s operations.
