Job Description:
Introduction
To be the Specialist Pathologist providing oversight for core clinical laboratories at SANBS:
Processing.
Issuing (Blood banks).
Donation testing.
Ensure compliance to relevant legal, regulatory and accreditation standards within area of responsibility.
Plan, implement and monitor medical related initiatives in area of responsibility
Be responsible for accurate and clinically relevant testing and reporting of all testing performed on patient and donor samples in SANBS laboratories.
Strategically contribute to training and education (e.g., of registrars and fellows) in the field of transfusion medicine.
Oversee Infection Prevention Control at SANBS.
Provide a medical consulting and support service in the area of expertise to both internal and external stakeholders.
Provide a medical consulting and support service in the area of expertise to both internal and external stakeholders.
Job description
KEY PERFORMANCE AREAS (KPAS)
KPA 1: Strategic Business Planning & Implementation Relating to Transfusion Medicine.
Participate in the design, development and implementation of systems that will ensure the delivery of high-quality blood products and related services.
Collaborate with the Lead Consultant Patient Blood Management and Transfusion Medicine (LCPBM & TM) and relevant stakeholders, to develop long term strategic plans for the department, aligned with the SANBS vision and mission.
Develop and execute, in consultation with LC: PBM&TM, an approved departmental business plan and supporting budget and ensure deadlines are met.
Monitor budget and expenses for business area and specified projects and ensure targets are met.
Propose potential projects and initiatives in support of the departmental and divisional strategy, obtain approval, implement and monitor the effectiveness thereof.
Conduct feasibility studies and customer surveys, monitor trends and make recommendations for continuous business improvements and sustainability.
Draft, obtain approval, implement and monitor policies, procedures and strategies (as required) to accomplish the Purpose, Vision and Mission of SANBS and external stakeholders.
KPA 2: Improving integral processes in Transfusion Medicine
Ensure compliance with legislative requirements and maintain quality standards in line with the national and international standard for clinical laboratories within area of work.
Oversee core laboratories in all matters pertaining to reporting and testing decisions that may hold clinical impact to patients / blood safety.
Maintain quality management accreditation of the laboratories including local and international accreditations.
Propose potential projects, obtain approval, implement and monitor the effectiveness thereof. Ensure that a change management process is followed when new tests and/or services are introduced.
Ensure up to date validated testing methods and platforms are used in clinical laboratories and that reporting is relevant to our patient population
Provide support to cellular therapy and immunohematology labs as required.
Provide medical oversight and assistance as required to prevent stock-outs, improve delivery of appropriate, quality products to patients and decrease customer complaints.
Provide overall responsibility for sign out of laboratory results including immunohematology and flow cytometry where required.
Aid, provide clinical oversight, monitor, report on and recommend interventions for clinical developments within scope of this role - that may impact on blood requirements, transfusion safety or patient outcomes.
Actively drive and participate in all aspects of the SANBS educational initiatives for all levels of internal and external stakeholders  including but not limited to registrars programs on all Transfusion Medicine related matters.
Design and monitor a system to continuously monitor product and service quality failures and take appropriate corrective action.
Provide clinical oversight, support and advice for all technical and donor related after hours queries during on call periods.

KPA 3: Quality Assurance and Compliance to Standards of Practice, Policies, Procedures and Protocols
Have an awareness regarding Cybersecurity and laboratory data integrity.
Ensure business continuity plans are in place and validated.
Ensure IPC guidelines are upheld and regularly audited.
Ensure successful implementation and maintenance of the Standards for the Practice of Blood
Transfusion in South Africa, GMP, GLP as well as adherence to all relevant legislation with regards to all SANBS activities relevant to area of work.
Ensure successful implementation and maintenance of laboratory accreditation standards such as SANAS 15189.
Effective participation in national initiatives relating to the setting of standards and policy development.
Develop protocols and procedures to guide operational implementation and practice in the specialized area of expertise.
Develop protocols and procedures to define the quality and acceptance criteria for the various blood products and related transfusion services.
Develop protocols and procedures to ensure the equitable and sustainable supply of high-quality blood and blood products, and optimized patient outcomes.
Clinical decision making where deviations from internal protocols are required.
Provide input into technician and technical education programs that will improve SANBS service delivery and enhance the safety of the blood supply.
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to ensure SANBS compliance with National Health Act and other applicable legislation in all applicable sites.
Benchmark best practice and propose standard updates accordingly to LCPBMTM.
Identify risks on an enterprise and departmental level and develop plans to mitigate and reduce.

KPA 4: Customer and Stakeholder Relationship Building
Map and identify key stakeholders in the core laboratories environments.
Ensure Internal and external relationship building and networking to ensure collaboration and build strong cross-functional cohesive teams.
Represent SANBS in consortiums for the establishment of new tests and services.
Leverage Information Technology in line with the SANBS digitalisation strategy
Actively contribute to ensuring that SANBS is considered the centre of excellence in the field of transfusion medicine in South Africa and Africa by training of doctors, presenting research, education of medical professionals, etc.
Participate in review of content in the communication and education of all clinicians and the SouthAfrican community through newsletters, pamphlets, website articles, and radio or televisioninterviews as required.
Collaborate with other divisions in SANBS (e.g. Operations, Marketing, and ICT) as required to synergise integrated outcomes in all matters related to patients and transfusion medicine.
Provide clinical and medical input on external customer related policies and procedures that may impact on patient safety / outcome.
Provide appropriate and clinical best-practice support and advice to SANBS staff dealing with external customers or patients/recipients, as well as marketing related queries, complaints and related issues.
Provide support to external stakeholders as required including meetings with and standardized feedback to all relevant stakeholders as required.
Educate and motivate all role-players in the health care sector within sphere of responsibility.
Support and liaise MM: PBM as required in area of expertise.
Provide appropriate TM and clinical best-practice support / advice to technical staff and medical practitioners (within the post-holders field of competence) on the optimal product selection in the management of complex immuno-haematology cases and other complex

KPA 5: Aligned people Management KPIs
Create development plans for staff. Conduct performance management and monitor performance on on-going basis through mentoring, coaching, and reviews.
Mentoring and coaching of junior pathologists in transfusion medicine and cellular therapies.
Track & encourage individual development by identifying learning and development needs & facilitate attendance of relevant programmes.
Deal with grievances, conflict and disciplinary issues and take appropriate actions in accordance with SANBS Policy.
Ensure regular two-way communication with staff matters such as strategy, values, team building, SOPs, policy changes, etc. to ensure understanding.
Attend meetings and training sessions as required, to remain informed of current field-related developments, to promote knowledge sharing.
Conduct scheduled meetings with direct reports where applicable.
Wherever possible develop successors within own team where applicable.

KPA 6: Conduct Research that leads to Innovative Implementation of Solutions
Participate in cutting edge research in line with best practices in Transfusion Medicine and related fields.
Communicate the outcome of the research to relevant stakeholders and obtain buy-in to improve our value proposition.
Maintain personal development plan that leads to continuous development, improvement and expansion on knowledge and skills.
Establish a portal for innovation that will ensure execution and implementation of viable ideas from employees or stakeholders.
Engage and participate in national and international working groups activities and presentations.
Represent SANBS in national and international working groups activities and presentations.
Research and gather information on new improved technology and equipment.

Job Description:
An organisation with multi-site operations in Durban is seeking a Finance Manager to provide financial leadership and commercial governance. This is a confidential opportunity. This management role offers the opportunity to become a trusted partner to senior management, driving profitability, operational efficiency, and sustainable shareholder value. You will be empowered to shape financial strategy, implement robust controls, and foster a culture of accountability.
This established organisation within the Automotive sector that has multi-site operations in Durban offers stability/growth opportunities within a collaborative/inclusive workplace culture. Employees benefit from flexible working arrangements that accommodate personal commitments alongside generous training support designed to foster professional development at every stage of your career journey. The company prioritises transparency/accountability and empowering its people through open communication channels/supportive leadership structures/process improvement initiatives that encourage innovation without compromising long-term capability or customer experience. As part of this dependable network you’ll enjoy being part of a knowledgeable team committed to delivering sustainable value/shareholder returns while nurturing talent through ongoing mentorship and succession planning opportunities.
As Finance Manager you will play a pivotal role in shaping the financial future of multi-site operations in Durban. Your day-to-day responsibilities will involve partnering closely with senior executives to translate complex financial data into actionable strategies that enhance profitability and operational discipline. You will oversee monthly management accounts with precision—ensuring timely closure of books while providing insightful analysis on variances between actuals versus budget/prior year figures. By monitoring key metrics such as revenue, profit margins, stock ageing, operational productivity, cost efficiency, and facility utilisation—you will ensure each business unit operates efficiently with strong controls in place. You will lead annual budgeting cycles for all departments while establishing disciplined expense management practices that promote accountability among department managers. Your commitment to maintaining robust internal controls will safeguard shareholder assets/cash flows while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements. As a visible presence within operating departments you will engage regularly with managers, executives, operational teams, and finance administrators—building trust through transparent communication/supportive leadership. Ultimately your success will be measured not only by accurate numbers but also by your ability to foster better decisions/effective capital utilisation/sustainable profitability across all business units.
Act as the senior financial and commercial partner to senior leadership and the management team by providing clear insight into profitability, margins, costs, working capital, and return on investment.
Translate complex financial results into practical operational actions that improve business performance across all departments.
Participate actively in strategic and operational decision-making processes alongside senior leaders to evaluate major expenditure, investment, and business-development opportunities.
Take overall responsibility for the accuracy and timeliness of monthly management accounts, profit-and-loss analysis, balance-sheet reconciliations, cash-flow forecasting, and departmental allocation of revenue and expenditure.
Provide dedicated financial oversight for each site and business unit by monitoring revenue, gross profits, stock levels, operational productivity, receivables, facility utilisation, and overall profitability.
Lead the annual budgeting process for all business units by developing comprehensive budgets for all sites, shared functions, and administrative teams.
Establish disciplined expense management practices without compromising customer experience or long-term capability by reviewing payrolls, overtime costs, marketing expenses, utilities expenditures, insurance premiums, repairs and maintenance fees, outsourced services costs, facility expenses, professional fees, IT expenditure, security costs, transport expenses and holding department managers accountable for their budgets.
Maintain strong internal financial controls across all operations by overseeing cash handling procedures; banking activities; stock management; transaction documentation; inventory; work-in-progress; debtor/creditor balances; payroll processing; procurement protocols; supplier payments; credit notes; discounts; journal entries; asset registers; user access permissions and conducting periodic internal reviews to identify control weaknesses.
Ensure compliance with South African accounting standards as well as taxation requirements (including VAT/PAYE), Broad Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) planning/verification obligations, Employment Equity Act mandates, Occupational Health & Safety regulations, Companies Act stipulations and act as primary liaison with external auditors and banks.
Lead and develop the finance administration team by establishing clear organisational structures with defined responsibilities; recruiting new talent; succession planning; managing performance reviews; facilitating training/development opportunities; improving processes through automation and creating a culture where finance is viewed as a commercial support function rather than purely administrative.
The ideal candidate for Finance Manager brings deep expertise in multi-site operations within the automotive sector, supported by the mandatory CA (SA) qualification, and proven experience managing complex financial functions across multiple departments. Your analytical skills enable you to interpret intricate data sets while your commercial acumen drives practical improvements in profitability/margins/costs/working capital returns. You are adept at engaging collaboratively with both senior executives and operational managers and building trust through honest communication/supportive leadership/inclusive team development. Your commitment to process improvement ensures ongoing enhancement of finance systems while your understanding of compliance requirements guarantees audit readiness/governance integrity. You thrive in environments where knowledge sharing/training opportunities are valued and where your ability to nurture talent contributes directly to organisational success.
CA (SA) qualification is essential and non-negotiable.
Extensive experience in financial management across multi-site operations is essential.
Proven track record managing management accounts/budgeting/working capital/financial controls within large-scale organisations.
Strong commercial acumen combined with analytical capability enables you to translate financial information into practical operational improvements.
Experience consolidating financial reporting across multiple sites is advantageous.
Exceptional leadership skills allow you to engage effectively with both senior executives and operational managers while fostering an inclusive/supportive team environment.
Excellent communication skills are required for building trust among stakeholders at all levels, from board members to operational staff.
Ability to develop concise monthly scorecards/KPI dashboards that highlight exceptions requiring management action rather than simply presenting historical data.
Commitment to process improvement/automation/succession planning ensures ongoing development of finance systems/team capabilities within an inclusive workplace.
Understanding of South African accounting/taxation/compliance requirements (including BBBEE/VAT/PAYE/Companies Act) is necessary for meeting audit/governance obligations.

On time order picking 99.9%

Ensure that inventory accuracy is 100%

Ensure proper use of material handling equipment.

Ensure all fire extinguishers are kept clear of obstructions.
Ensure that all staff are adhering to PPE requirements.

Experience: 3+ years in warehouse or supply chain operations, with at least 2-3 years in a supervisory role.
Technical Skills: Ability in MS Excel, WMS platforms, and warehouse reporting tools.

Excellent customer service skills.
A commitment to service excellence and customer satisfaction.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively in all situations.

A strong collaborator yet still able to work independently with minimal supervision.
Excellent communication skills, exceptional organizational ability, high mindfulness, and ability to multi-task.

Company Details: The legal mandate and core business of the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) are to manage, protect and conserve South Africas environment and natural resources. To give effect to this constitutional environmental right and the need for sound environmental management and sustainable development, the DFFE has over a period of time developed a comprehensive environmental management legislative/regulatory framework. This regulatory framework comprises acts of parliament (environmental laws), regulations, policies, norms and standards, and other regulatory tools that are aimed at promoting sound environmental management practices in order to protect and conserve the environment for the benefit of current and future generations. In addition to the development, implementation and ongoing review of a progressive regulatory framework for sound environmental management, other critical environmental management interventions by the DFFE include raising awareness on key environment issues and promoting a culture of environmental activism among ordinary citizens, building capacity within the sector, and establishing and strengthening national, regional and global partnerships to address common environmental challenges. The long-term vision of the DFFE is to have a prosperous and equitable society living in harmony with our natural resources, as outlined in our medium-term strategic plan. To support the achievement of this vision, the DFFE has identified five strategic goals, as follows: Environmental economic contribution optimised; Environmental/Ecological integrity safeguarded and enhanced; Social transformation within our communities; Global agenda influenced and obligations met; and A capable and efficient department. The DFFE is structured into nine budget programmes. Each programme pursues a set of identified strategic outcomes, which are aimed at achieving the commitments of the DFFE to the five-year strategic plan and to ultimately make successive progress towards the realisation of the long-term vision of the DFFE.

The role ensures that payroll is delivered accurately, compliantly, cost-effectively, and in alignment with corporate governance standards, while supporting the organization’s broader people, financial, and business strategy.

Payroll Strategy & Operating Model

Contribute to global payroll transformation initiatives (where applicable), including system upgrades, vendor selection, and regional rollouts.

Oversee end-to-end payroll processing across multiple countries, ensuring accuracy, adhered to timeliness, and consistency.
Ensure correct calculation and payment of salaries, incentives, allowances, benefits, statutory deductions, and off-cycle payments.

Ensure compliance with country-specific payroll legislation, tax regulations, and labour laws across relevant payroll jurisdictions
Implement strong internal controls, segregation of duties, and approval frameworks in line with corporate governance standards.
Maintain audit readiness, including internal audits, external audits, and regulatory inspections.
Identify and mitigate payroll-related risks, including compliance, fraud, system, and operational risks.
Ensure alignment with global policies on data privacy, confidentiality, and information security (e.g., POPIA, GDPR where applicable).
Stay abreast of industry best practices, emerging technologies, and regulatory changes impacting payroll.
Reporting, Insights & Decision Support
Provide analytics on payroll costs, trends, variances, headcount movements, overtime, and statutory liabilities.
Ensure statutory, tax, and regulatory reporting is accurate, complete, and submitted within required deadlines.
Support Reward and HR with payroll data for remuneration reviews, incentives, audits, and workforce planning.
Partner with Finance to support accurate payroll accruals, reconciliations, and financial close processes.
Process Optimization & Technology Enablement
Drive
continuous improvement and automation
of payroll processes to improve accuracy, turnaround times, and scalability.

trusted payroll advisor
to HR, Reward, Finance, Legal, and country leadership teams.

Job Description:
Job Purpose:
The Continuous Improvement Technician is responsible for identifying, analysing, implementing, and sustaining improvements across the production environment. The role supports improved safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and equipment reliability through OEE tracking, time and motion studies, waste elimination, data analysis, and structured monitoring of all continuous improvement projects.
Key Responsibilities:
Continuous Improvement and Lean Manufacturing
Drive improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, 5S, TPM, visual management, and structured problem-solving methodologies.
Identify production bottlenecks, process variation, waste, and non-value-added activities.
Facilitate or support Kaizen events, improvement workshops, and shop-floor problem-solving sessions.
Conduct root cause analysis for recurring operational losses and support corrective and preventive actions.
Support the development, revision, and sustainability of standard operating procedures and standard work.
Verify that completed improvements are embedded, audited, and sustained.
OEE Monitoring and Improvement
Monitor and report Overall Equipment Effectiveness across production lines and equipment.
Analyse availability, performance, and quality losses, including breakdowns, changeovers, minor stops, speed losses, defects, and rework.
Maintain daily, weekly, and monthly OEE dashboards and loss summaries.
Develop and track action plans to improve equipment utilisation, line performance, output, and reliability.
Work with Production, Engineering, Maintenance, and Quality teams to eliminate recurring losses.
Validate performance improvements and quantify operational benefits.
Time and Motion Studies
Conduct time and motion studies for operators, equipment, changeovers, material movement, and production tasks.
Measure cycle times, waiting time, travel, delays, and work content using consistent observation methods.
Develop and maintain standard times and documented work measurement records.
Identify opportunities for improved workflow, workstation layout, labour utilisation, ergonomics, and method standardisation.
Support line balancing, capacity analysis, manpower planning, and productivity improvement.
Communicate findings objectively and support implementation of approved improvements.
Continuous Improvement Project Monitoring
Maintain a central register of all continuous improvement projects, including owners, objectives, milestones, status, risks, projected savings, and realised benefits.
Track projects against agreed scope, timelines, actions, and performance targets.
Coordinate routine project reviews and follow up overdue actions with responsible persons.
Apply clear project governance and escalation where progress, resources, or benefits are at risk.
Prepare concise project status reports for management review.
Verify project closure, benefits realisation, handover, and sustainability controls.
Data Analysis and Reporting
Collect, clean, validate, analyse, and interpret production and operational data.
Monitor OEE, downtime, throughput, yield, scrap, rework, cycle time, labour efficiency, and cost savings.
Build and maintain production dashboards, KPI scorecards, Pareto analyses, and trend reports.
Use data to identify improvement priorities, quantify losses, and support evidence-based decisions.
Present findings and recommendations clearly to production teams and management.
Support automation of recurring reports and project tracking where practical.
Training, Engagement, Safety and Quality
Promote a practical continuous improvement culture on the shop floor.
Coach operators and supervisors in basic Lean tools, standard work, 5S, OEE loss identification, and problem solving.
Encourage employee participation in improvement ideas and recognition programmes.
Ensure proposed changes comply with safety, quality, environmental, and operational requirements.
Participate in risk assessments and change-control activities before implementing process changes.
Minimum Qualifications and Experience:
National Diploma or Degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Management, Production Management, or a related field.
Typically 2 to 5 years of experience in a manufacturing, production, FMCG, packaging, or process environment.
Practical experience with OEE analysis, time and motion studies, production data, and improvement projects.
Experience working cross-functionally with Production, Maintenance, Engineering, and Quality teams.

The academic programme is delivered by excellent teachers, trained to nurture inquiry, explicit thinking, and differentiated learning. The College offers academic support and extension, enriching the core experiences of teaching and learning.

A number of benchmarks, both national and international, provide a framework for evaluating quality.

As a member of ISASA, the College participates in the cycle of institutional evaluation provided through the Independent Quality Assurance Agency (IQAA) and St Stithians is accredited by Umalusi, the South African certification authority.

Grade 12 students write the matriculation examinations of the Independent Examinations Board (IEB). Our matriculants achieve at a high level, with 96-98% obtaining Bachelor degree passes for entry to South African universities and universities in Europe, North America and Australia. View our latest Matric results here.

St Stithians offers a diverse and rich extra-curricular programme, aimed to provide opportunities for a holistic education. All the major sports are offered, supported by excellent sporting facilities and coaching. The cultural calendar and the performing arts are integral to our education.

There is a strong focus on educating leaders, who participate in rites of passage as they move through the schools. Community service activities are integrated into the curriculum, as are outdoor education camps and outings.

Our campus is a place of natural beauty, with various landscape zones, and the College is committed to being an environmentally "green" school.

St Stithians seeks to provide a values-based and top-quality academic education, supported by a diverse extra-curricular offering. Our students matriculate as well-rounded individuals, well prepared to inspire excellence and make a difference both in our own country, the African continent and globally.

From the vantage point of a hot air balloon drifting over the St Stithians Campus, one looks down on a beautiful estate of 105 hectares occupied by a chapel, learning and sports facilities, and a varying landscape and topography.

Company Details:
The National Treasury is responsible for managing South Africa’s national government finances. Supporting efficient and sustainable public financial management is fundamental to the promotion of economic development, good governance, social progress and a rising standard of living for all South Af...read morericans. The Constitution of the Republic (Chapter 13) mandates the National Treasury to ensure transparency, accountability and sound financial controls in the management of public finances.

The National Treasury’s legislative mandate is also described in the Public Finance Management Act (Chapter 2). The National Treasury is mandated to promote government’s fiscal policy framework; to coordinate macroeconomic policy and intergovernmental financial relations; to manage the budget preparation process; to facilitate the Division of Revenue Act, which provides for an equitable distribution of nationally raised revenue between national, provincial and local government; and to monitor the implementation of provincial budgets.

As mandated by the executive and Parliament, the National Treasury will continue to support the optimal allocation and utilisation of financial resources in all spheres of government to reduce poverty and vulnerability among South Africa’s most marginalised.

Over the next 10 years National Treasury priorities include increasing investment in infrastructure and industrial capital; improving education and skills development to raise productivity; improving the regulation of markets and public entities; and fighting poverty and inequality through efficient public service delivery, expanded employment levels, income support and empowerment.

The National Treasury is mandated to promote government’s fiscal policy framework; to coordinate macroeconomic policy and intergovernmental financial relations; to manage the budget preparation process; to facilitate the Division of Revenue Act, which provides for an equitable distribution of nationally raised revenue between national, provincial and local government; and to monitor the implementation of provincial budgets.

As mandated by the executive and Parliament, the National Treasury will continue to support the optimal allocation and utilisation of financial resources in all spheres of government to reduce poverty and vulnerability among South Africa’s most marginalised.

Over the next 10 years National Treasury priorities include increasing investment in infrastructure and industrial capital; improving education and skills development to raise productivity; improving the regulation of markets and public entities; and fighting poverty and inequality through efficient public service delivery, expanded employment levels, income support and empowerment.

The QA Engineer is an executor — their primary focus is on building and running test cases, contributing to the automated test framework, and providing timely, accurate feedback on quality across sprints and releases. They will cover development from the Practice, ATS, and automations teams, operating as part of the shared QA function.
Key Responsibilities
Execute functional, regression, integration, and exploratory testing across all ServiceNow development in line with the test plans defined by the QA Manager.
Write clear, well-structured test cases and test scripts based on user stories and acceptance criteria provided by the Business Analyst.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of automated test scripts within the ServiceNow ATF (Automated Test Framework), expanding coverage across product domains.
Execute regression testing ahead of each release and platform upgrade, using the automated test suite to validate platform stability.
Log, track, and retest defects accurately and in a timely manner, ensuring developers receive clear, reproducible defect reports.
Support UAT coordination activities — setting up test environments, providing test data, and assisting business stakeholders through test execution.
Maintain test cases and test scripts in the shared test repository, keeping them up to date as platform changes are made.
Contribute to quality reporting by providing accurate test execution status, pass/fail rates, and defect metrics to the QA Manager.
Participate in sprint ceremonies — including backlog grooming and sprint reviews — to ensure testability is considered from story creation through to delivery.
Essential Experience & Skills
Proven experience in a QA Engineer or software testing role within a ServiceNow or enterprise platform delivery environment.
Practical experience using ServiceNow ATF (Automated Test Framework) to build and execute automated test scripts.
Strong skills in writing test cases and test scripts from user stories and acceptance criteria.
Experience executing functional, regression, and integration testing within an agile delivery environment.
Ability to write clear, reproducible defect reports and manage defects through to resolution.
Comfortable working across multiple product domains, picking up context quickly and adapting testing approaches accordingly.
Desirable
Experience with platform upgrade testing in ServiceNow, including regression test execution during upgrade cycles.
Familiarity with ISTQB Foundation or equivalent testing qualification.
Exposure to broader test automation tools or scripting in addition to ServiceNow ATF.
ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) or equivalent product knowledge.
Experience supporting UAT with business stakeholders, including test environment setup and guidance through test execution.
Behaviours & Competencies
Detail-oriented — takes pride in thorough, accurate test coverage and clear defect reporting.
Reliable — consistently delivers test outputs on time and to the standard required by the QA Manager.
Collaborative — works well with developers, BAs, and business stakeholders as part of a wider delivery team.

:
Lead, guide and control the development, management, capacity building and continuous improvement of PFA service offerings and quality assurance frameworks and related guides, templates, tools and evaluation grids. Projects Governance and Management
:
Lead and guide the maintenance and continuous improvement of the GTAC project management framework including methodologies, processes and controls, and training materials and guides. Manage the establishment, development and maintenance of the PFA project governance framework system, processes and controls, and training materials and guides. Lead and guide the identification and establishment of multidisciplinary collaboration across practice areas and GTAC projects requiring integrated advisory support, ensuring joint QA arrangements across practice areas. The Procurement Specialist Raw Material is responsible for understanding, communicating, and helping to implement commodity sourcing strategies on a local level (at the market). The Procurement Specialist will gather business requirements in the local market and drive alignment with Category market teams as input into the strategy. Provide the Local Business Partner with information and requirements gathered through the daily business and report to him/her on a regular basis.
Proactively understand the business needs and requirements within commodity environment from a functional and plant level requirements in the business.
Carry out as directed any data retrieval, analysis and representation required, mapping how ordering (S2P) and channels work within the locations serviced and identify improvements to be targeted.

On a monthly basis ensuring accuracy and integrity of the commodity price outlook, with strong collaboration with category teams, Procurement Controller, and Business partners.
As directed by category and sourcing teams, act to integrate innovation, renovation, and post award cost improvement elements from suppliers into all in scope functional or site/production processes, ensuring that all supplies to that site adhere to Nestlé's Suppliers Code and all actions from audit events are acted upon.
Drive risk mitigation strategies to help ensure supply of commodity materials for all factories (e.g., Risk analysis, alternative supplier approvals, and business continuity plans).

B Degree or equivalent tertiary qualification.

Purpose of the Job:
A mechanic in the automotive industry, specialising in used cars, is responsible for inspecting, diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining pre-owned vehicles. The mechanic ensures that used cars meet safety and performance standards and prepares them for sale. This role requires knowledge of various automotive systems, strong diagnostic skills, and the ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
Vehicle Inspection:
Perform thorough inspections of used vehicles to assess their condition and identify any existing or potential issues. This includes evaluating the engine, transmission, suspension, brakes, electrical systems, and other components.
Diagnostic Procedures:
Utilise diagnostic tools, equipment, and technical knowledge to identify and troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and other automotive problems. Conduct diagnostic tests, interpret results, and determine appropriate repair solutions.
Repairs and Maintenance:
Perform necessary repairs and maintenance tasks on used vehicles. This includes addressing engine and transmission issues, replacing worn-out components, repairing electrical malfunctions, and resolving braking and suspension problems.
Parts and Component Replacement:
Identify and source appropriate replacement parts or components for used vehicles. Ensure the compatibility, quality, and proper installation of parts to meet manufacturer specifications.
Documentation and Reporting:
Maintain accurate records of vehicle inspections, repairs performed, parts used, and other relevant information. Complete service reports and documentation required for warranty claims, customer records, and internal purposes.
Test Drives:
Conduct test drives to evaluate vehicle performance, assess repairs, and verify the effectiveness of maintenance tasks. Pay attention to noise, vibrations, handling, and overall vehicle functionality.
Quality Assurance:
Ensure that repaired vehicles meet quality standards and are safe for road use. Conduct post-repair inspections to verify the completion of repairs and identify any additional issues.
Communication:
Communicate effectively with relative parties regarding vehicle repairs, maintenance recommendations, and estimated completion times. Provide explanations of repair work performed and answer any questions or concerns.
Team Collaboration:
Collaborate with other mechanics, service advisors, and technicians to coordinate repairs, share knowledge, and ensure efficient workflow. Assist and mentor apprentice mechanics as required.
Safety and Compliance:
Adhere to safety protocols, guidelines, and regulations to maintain a safe working environment. Comply with industry standards, safety procedures, and environmental regulations.

Cost-to-serve analysis
Asset lifecycle performance

Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Senior Manager: Hospitality contributes to the achievement of organisational objectives by providing strategic leadership and oversight of the Specialist Hospitality line of business. This role is accountable for growing the Specialist Hospitality book of business, expanding market share and maximising sustainable profitability. Responsible for the end-to-end execution of the long-term strategy, ensuring strong financial performance, effective operational management and ongoing alignment with broader business goals.
Responsibilities
Leadership and Direction
Set and clearly communicate the strategy required to achieve the vision of the Specialist Hospitality division, embedding TIH values within the function. Define and drive the key strategic actions required for successful implementation, while inspiring and leading a small, highly specialised team to commit to the strategy and consistently deliver exceptional outcomes in support of the line’s business objectives.
Functional Strategy Formation
Lead the development and execution of the strategy for the Specialist Hospitality division by anticipating macro trends, emerging risks, and complex market opportunities. Ensure strategic alignment and integration with the broader business insurance strategy to support sustainable growth and competitive positioning.
Budgeting & Costing
Take overall accountability for setting, managing, and delivering the Specialist Hospitality division’s budget. Continuously monitor Gross Written Premium and clients on risk against targets and actuals. Oversee the development and performance of the claims ratio, including the impact of IBNR and outstanding reported claims. Manage and monitor investments and ongoing operational costs against budget to ensure profitability and financial discipline.
Risk Management, Reinsurance & Analysis
Provide oversight of risk management for the Specialist Hospitality line of business, including the ongoing review and enhancement of policy wordings to ensure relevance, compliance, and fitness for purpose. Ensure the annual renewal of reinsurance treaties and establish a formalised, structured renewal schedule across all existing business.
Product/Service Development
Lead the development, enhancement and delivery of the Specialist Hospitality product suite by defining and driving the product and service roadmap and managing the associated backlog. Analyse market trends, customer needs, and competitive dynamics to ensure the hospitality offering remains relevant and differentiated through continuous product development. Drive the design and launch of new products aligned to a defined target market and the company’s risk appetite statement.
Operational Compliance
Ensure that all business activities within the Specialist Hospitality division comply with applicable external regulatory requirements and voluntary codes, including TCF, as well as internal policies and standards. This includes minimising business risk and protecting the organisation’s reputation through effective oversight of key operational components such as sales platforms, renewal processes, rating tools and supporting systems.
Marketing
Oversee the marketing strategy for the Specialist Hospitality line of business, including advertising, lead generation, market presence initiatives, broker engagement, and ongoing support to the broker marketing channel to drive sustainable growth and brand positioning.
Organisational Capability Building
Coach, mentor and develop staff supporting the Specialist Hospitality business to strengthen individual capability, build a strong talent pipeline, and support succession planning within the organisation.
Performance Management
Manage and report on performance across the Specialist Hospitality division by setting clear and measurable performance objectives for direct reports and holding them accountable for delivery. Take timely and appropriate corrective action where required to ensure the achievement of annual business and financial objectives.
Customer Relationships Development
Develop and implement a relationship management plan for each distribution channel, such as direct, brokers and group schemes.
Promoting Customer Focus
Develop internal marketing plans and work collaboratively with cross-functional teams to strengthen internal relationships within a large organisation. Build strong external customer relationships by setting, managing and continuously improving customer satisfaction measurement systems and scorecards.
Customer Needs/Experience Research
Lead the research and design of Specialist Hospitality product concepts through structured customer insight approaches, including voice of the customer initiatives. Drive the execution of tools, procedures and initiatives that deepen understanding of customer segments, emerging trends, needs and expectations, and translate these insights into commercially viable product and service enhancements.
Education
Grade 12/ SAQA Accredited Equivalent (Essential) FAIS recognised qualification (Essential) Relevant business degree (Essential) AIISA or FIISA Qualifications (Essential)
Experience
Managerial Experience Experience of planning, managing and organising resources within short / medium timescales within the overall policy framework. (Over 6 years to 10 years), Over 10 years experience in the specialist hospitality industry (Essential) General commercial insurance knowledge (Advantageous)

Job Description
The role is responsible for managing the procurement cycle through delivering effective and efficient procurement of goods and services (new requirements, contracted and non-contracted). Monitor and manage compliance with procurement policies, procedures and agreements in place. Facilitate the DBSA procurement objectives and targets through compliance with strategy and application of policies and procedures.
Key Responsibilities
KEY PERFORMANCE AREAS:
Planning and Standards
Disseminate procurement policies, procedures, processes, templates, delegations, and performance metrics to build awareness and promote understanding.
Train and equip business units to effectively manage or participate in procurement processes, including quotation and tendering activities.
Engage Business Managers to identify upcoming work and determine support requirements from the Supply Chain Management (SCM) Unit.
Plan and coordinate work schedules and timelines to align with sourcing and business demands.
Collaborate with business units to identify and plan for non-contracted spend through the RFQ/RFP process.
Conduct detailed analysis of procurement transactions (spend data) to identify trends, off-contract spend, policy deviations, and compliance gaps for improved planning, risk management, and reporting.
Support the SCM Unit in contributing to the successful delivery of the Division’s financial strategy and operational objectives.
Technical Support and Value Management
Support the financial division in delivering on the key business imperatives pertaining to cost containment, innovation, productivity and business relevance.
Work with the appropriate business unit managers to understand their operational plans, sourcing requirements, budgets, service standards and targets (cost, transformation, etc.).
Develop and maintain the demand pipeline and sourcing plan for the business.
Conduct relevant research and maintain business intelligence to support effective solutions, advice and decision making for business.
Lead and guide decisions on consolidation, rationalisation and relevance of services in line with changing business requirements and alignment to strategic imperatives such as cost containment.
Support business units with drafting specifications/requirements for quotes and tenders.
Support the tender unit and business with analysis of quotes and tender documentation/submissions
Negotiate prices, terms and conditions with suppliers and deliver savings targets to the Bank.
Provide integration and support to internal business units, decentralised operations and related partners/agencies pertaining to supply chain activities.
Facilitate training and awareness sessions for staff involved in supply chain processes to ensure understanding, compliance, and effective participation.
Support the SCM team and division during peak demand periods, staff shortfalls and ad-hoc project-related requirements.
Support the Bank and the SCM team in delivering innovative solutions to improve productivity, service levels and contribute to cost containment.

Procure goods and services to meet user requirements as per agreed service levels.
Manage and administer Request for Quotation process in line with policy, delegations and SLA
Manage and administer end-to-end Request for Proposal process in line with policy, delegations and SLA.
Manage and administer the order process in line with policy, delegations and SLA.
Manage and administer Order expediting and fulfilment.
Communicate contract award and impact to BU (stakeholders and change management).
Liaise and support with Legal and other relevant officials for the purposes of negotiation and contracting.
Maintain accurate records and files (manual & electronic) of all the quotation/tender data.
Maintain full compliance with defined policies, procedures, regulations and standards.
Address transactional queries, gaps in information, incorrect postings, GL, Material Groups, etc., when review and releasing PR and PO's.
Monitor transactional data for the purposes of identifying and expediently resolving deviations and risks to business and policy compliance.
Prepare analysis, comparative schedules and recommendations to RFQ/RFPs for business unit consideration and decision making.
Guide and assist business unit decision-making and solutions supported by credible market research and industry practices.
Prepare quality reports and documentation for SCM consolidation and reporting.
Support supplier performance management by tracking the level of compliance with orders placed with suppliers.
Monitor supplier performance data with business units.
Assess and resolution of supplier queries.
Resolve errors on requisitions and purchase orders as required.
Investigate and address supply non-conformances - administering product defects and recalls.
Review and action open Requisitions and Purchase Orders as per the SLA.
File/archive all source documents about each transaction (these must be complete, accurate and accessible).
Monitor price increases and communicate changes as necessary.
Contribute to items master development (catalogue and supplier).
Ensure compliance with Procurement policies and procedures.
Implement, monitor, report and manage attainment of procurement metrics / SLA.
Support the team and Division with accessing and making available information timeously to Auditors and management in the correct format, content, completeness and accuracy.

Open Order lead-time (weekly).
Open GRV’s (weekly).

retrospective transactions.
deviations from the process.
single source.

Prepare reports (SCM dashboard) for discussion with Business Units (Divisions) - as per the SCM
Dashboard (monthly).

Procurement of quality goods and services at the best possible price and with policies.
Timely and accurate reporting.
Effective and efficient procurement and expediting of goods and services as per the service level agreement.
Performance management as per the service level agreement.
Supporting the transformation strategy.
Effective compliance with all governance requirements.
Effective, accurate and complete records management for audit purposes.
Clean audit.

The Manager: Contracts Management role is a strategic management function located within the Independent Power Producer Office (IPPO).
The IPPO was established in 2010 to provide rapid solutions to South Africa’s severe electricity supply constraints, by procuring new energy generation capacity from Independent Power Producers (IPPs). The IPPO was created as a project office hosted by the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) under a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) between the Department of Electricity and Energy (DEE), National Treasury and the DBSA. The mandate of the IPP Office is to provide specialised services to government, including a) IPP Energy Procurement Management, b) Monitoring, Evaluation and Contract Management, and c) Professional Advisory Services. The IPPO’s skills, expertise and success in mobilising and delivering on time is recognised domestically and globally.
The role has been necessitated for the purpose of overseeing and managing end-to-end IPP project contracts entered into between the Department of Electricity and Energy (DEE), Eskom, and the Independent Power Producers. The portfolio of commercial agreements spans multiple technologies including Renewable Energy, Battery Energy Storage, Gas to Power and Hybrid energy facilities.
Reporting to the Senior Specialist: Contract Management, Economic Development, and Monitoring & Evaluation, the Manager: Contract Management will be responsible for leading the strategic execution, implementation, and compliance monitoring of high-value, complex contract portfolios.
The Manager: Contract Management will further ensure absolute regulatory compliance with frameworks like the PFMA and PPPFA, lead a high-performing team of contract administrators, manage formal dispute resolution processes, and effectively handle strategic partnerships and stakeholder expectations across Eskom, government departments, and private sector IPPs.

Team Coordination: Allocate skills, provide mandates, and evaluate deliverables to ensure streamlined contractual outputs.
Risk and Dispute Mitigation: Clarify contractual ambiguities with the Legal Department to manage risks and prevent compensation or shareholder disputes.
Compliance Management and Monitoring
Lifecycle Compliance: Lead regulatory, legislative, and Eskom governance compliance from project development through to operations.
Agreement Oversight: Monitor IPP and Eskom obligations under PPAs, including construction milestones and technical and Economic Development compliance.
Enforcement and Remediation: Manage due diligence, enforce non-compliance penalty clauses, and act as the key contractual liaison across IPP functions.
Reporting

Data Analysis: Oversee monthly project construction data, energy generation metrics, and project progress toward Scheduled Commercial Operating Dates (SCOD).
Strategic Outputs: Consolidate monthly and quarterly feedback reports for the Head of the IPP Office and track data points supporting the Multi-Year Price Determination (MYPD) allowance.

Job Description
Dis-Chem Pharmacies require the services of a Auxiliary Nurse To provide basic nursing care and pre-consultation support to patients attending the Primary Health Clinic.
Responsible for taking and recording vital signs, facilitating patient flow, obtaining and documenting consent, maintaining accurate patient records, and provide basic administration support Registered Nurse / Professional Nurse.
Minimum Requirements:
Grade 12 / Matric
Higher Certificate in Auxiliary Nursing (or equivalent recognized qualification).
Registered with the South African Nursing Council (SANC) as an Auxiliary Nurse, where applicable
Minimum of 1- 3 yrs experience in primary healthcare, outpatient or clinic environment will be
Computer literate – MS Office
Duties and Responsibilities:
Pre-Consultation Patient Assessment
Assist with the preparation of patients before consultation by performing basic assessments as delegated by the Registered Nurse•
Receive patients in the pre-consultation area in a professional and respectful manner.
Confirm patient identity using the approved patient identification process.
Record reason for visiting or presenting complaint as per clinic procedure.
Take, document and report basic vital signs, including:
Blood pressure
Pulse
Temperature
Respiratory rate
Oxygen saturation, where applicable
Weight
Height
Body Mass Index, where applicable
Blood glucose, where delegated and according to protocol
Identify abnormal vital signs and immediately report these to the Registered Nurse.
Assist with basic screening according to clinic protocols.
Patient Administration
To support accurate and efficient patient administration in the pre-consultation room.
Ensure patient demographic details are verified.
Ensure patient electronic health records are available and updated.
Record all relevant pre-consultation information accurately.
Ensure required documents are signed, completed and correctly.
Capture information on the clinic system.
Ensure accurate handover of patient information to the Registered Nurse or consulting practitioner.
Documentation and Record Keeping
Accurately record all vital signs and observations clearly.
Ensure patient records are complete, legible, dated and signed where required.
Document consent and patient interactions according to facility policy.
Maintain confidentiality and integrity of patient information.
Comply with legal, ethical and facility record-keeping requirements.
Health and Safety
Ensure a clean, safe and hygienic patient and clinical environment.
Adhere to infection prevention and control protocols.
Perform hand hygiene according to protocol.
Use personal protective equipment appropriately.
Clean and disinfect equipment between patients.
Ensure equipment such as blood pressure machines, thermometers, glucometers and scales are clean and functional.
Report faulty equipment to the Registered Nurse or Clinic Manager.
Safely handle and dispose of clinical waste according to facility policy or established procedures.
Maintain cleanliness and order in the pre-consultation room.
Follow occupational health and safety requirements.
Communication and Teamwork
The Auxiliary Nurse must work closely with the Registered Nurse, doctors, reception team and other healthcare workers.
Communicate respectfully with patients, families and staff.
Escalate clinical concerns promptly.
Follow instructions from the Registered Nurse.
Support efficient patient movement through the clinic.
Always maintain professional behaviour.
Participating in clinic meetings, training and quality improvement activities where required.
General
The Auxiliary Nurse must function strictly within the scope of practice for an Auxiliary Nurse and within facility protocols.
The Auxiliary Nurse may not:
Work independently without supervision.
Diagnose patients.
Prescribe medication.
Change treatment plans.
Give clinical advice outside approved protocol.
Perform procedures outside the delegated scope.
Obtain consent for complex clinical procedures without Registered Nurse or practitioner involvement.
The Auxiliary Nurse must immediately escalate to the Registered Nurse if:
Vital signs are abnormal.
A patient appears acutely ill or unstable.
A patient reports chest pain, shortness of breath, severe pain, fainting, confusion or severe bleeding.
There is uncertainty regarding consent.
A patient refuses care or withdraws consent.
There is no clinical, ethical or safety concern.

English and 2nd language – Read, write and speak
Good communication skills, listening

Business acumen

Interpersonal skills

Leadership skills
technical skills
Management skills

Company Details: Cape Union Mart International (Pty) Ltd has been equipping South African adventurers since 1933, and is South Africa's favourite outdoor adventure store. Stocking everything one needs for outdoor pursuits - including hiking, camping, trail running, mountain biking, snow sports, travel and mor...read moree - Cape Union Mart is an essential first step in every adventure. Cape Union Mart has stores across South Africa, and in Namibia and Botswana. The history of Cape Union Mart dates back to 1933 when the late Philip Krawitz, grandfather of the current Chairman, founded the business on the corner of Corporation and Mostert Street in Cape Town. Cape Union Mart originated as an "Army and Navy Store" and became famous for its "everything from an anchor to a toothpick" product range. Sandwiched between two of South Africa 's largest retailers, Woolworths and OK Bazaars, Cape Union Mart realised that it had to offer something different. Apart from an extensive range of merchandise, the store became known as "the friendly store" and focused on building unique relationships with its customers. During the war years, Cape Union Mart supplied visiting troops with some of the luxuries and necessities associated with the military. Passing whaling ships and foreign fishermen were also catered for with a unique array of merchandise from around the world. In the post-war years, the company grew and prospered under Arthur Krawitz who took over the business from his father in the late 1940's. The company became famous for non-seasonal merchandise and specialised in selling summer clothing to people touring overseas in winter. and vice versa. Cape Union Mart was the first importer of many famous products such as Levi Jeans, Hong Kong anoraks, Norwegian socks and Gore-Tex foul weather clothing.

Description
Please read the below in detail. The role is actually a "Field Coach" i.e. someone who does in-store merchandizing, training, relationship building and influencing with store management and staff.
JOB MISSION
Smollan is seeking enthusiastic and motivated Field Coaches who have a genuine passion for running, sports performance, biomechanics, rehabilitation or endurance sport.
You will become the trusted technical and brand expert within assigned specialist running and sporting goods retail environments — building the confidence, knowledge and belief of store teams so that they can guide runners with authority, and ensuring the brand is presented at pinnacle standard on the shop floor.
The role combines performance science, retail training, visual merchandising and community engagement, offering a unique opportunity to apply your knowledge and passion within a leading global running brand.
Top performers will:
Build authentic relationships with retail teams and the local running community
Translate technical product features into performance benefits store staff can confidently explain
Lift the product knowledge and brand belief of every store team in their territory
Ensure brand presentation, seasonal stories and launches show up at pinnacle standard in every door
Become recognised as a credible expert within local running communities
MAJOR ACCOUNTABILITIES
Retail Team Training & Education
Deliver seasonal and ongoing product training to store staff across assigned doors, building confidence and depth of product knowledge.
Explain brand technologies, cushioning systems, support structures and performance benefits in simple, engaging ways.
Provide guidance on running styles, gait, comfort, movement patterns and general biomechanics so store teams can make credible recommendations.
Act as the brand subject matter expert within assigned stores, and the first point of contact for product and technical questions.
Support ongoing education around running performance, footwear innovation and category trends.
Equip in-store teams to be the brand's trusted voice — store teams don't only need to know the product inside out, they also need to believe in the brand's vision for runners.
Visual Merchandising & In-Store Standards
Implement and maintain visual merchandising standards in line with brand guidelines across all assigned doors.
Execute seasonal launches, campaign moments and new product introductions so that in-store presentation matches the ambition of the brand story.
Maintain product visibility, fixture health, signage and category presentation on every store visit.
Identify and escalate opportunities to improve space, positioning and presentation within assigned stores.
Monitor stock availability and range presence on shelf, flagging gaps to the account team.
Insight & Market Feedback
Capture and share consumer feedback, product feedback and competitor activity observed in the marketplace.
Provide sharp, relevant insight from the shop floor to support brand and category decision-making.
Highlight training gaps, category trends and store-level opportunities to the account team.
Reporting & Territory Management
Maintain accurate reporting on store visits, training sessions delivered, merchandising compliance and market feedback.
Work to an agreed call cycle, managing schedules effectively across assigned retail locations.
Complete all administration, reporting and photographic evidence within required timeframes.
Ways of Working
Report into the Smollan account team responsible for the portfolio, working to agreed KPIs, call cycles and training plans.
Work closely with store managers and store teams in assigned doors to secure time, access and buy-in for training and merchandising.
Partner with the brand's local training and marketing contacts as directed by the Smollan account team.
Share best practice with fellow Field Coaches across the national team.
The shape of your day-to-day work will vary significantly, and your style and influence will need to adapt accordingly. You must be collaborative, intuitive and able to build rapport quickly, remaining open to the opinions and expertise of the retail teams you work alongside.
Requirements
REQUIREMENTS FOR SUCCESS
A successful candidate will be expected to clearly demonstrate and articulate experience against the essential requirements below in order to be considered.
Essential
A genuine background in and passion for sport, athletics, running or fitness — as a participant, athlete, coach, club member or through sustained active involvement in sporting communities.
A strong communicator, with the ability to simplify technical concepts and make them engaging.
Comfortable educating and influencing store teams and consumers.
Energetic, self-motivated and confident engaging with people.
Organised, with strong planning and territory management skills.
Available full-time (40 hours per week) on a flexible schedule that includes weekends, evenings and sporting events.
Previous retail sales experience
A valid driver's licence and your own reliable vehicle and comfortable travelling between retail locations as required.
Advantageous
Previous experience in training delivery, coaching or facilitation.
Previous retail, visual merchandising or field marketing experience.
Active participation in running communities, gyms, sports clubs or athletic environments.
Comfort with digital content creation and using social platforms to build community presence.
A completed qualification in Sport Science, Human Movement Science, Exercise Science, Biokinetics, Physiotherapy, Sport Management or a closely related discipline is beneficial, but not essential — passion, technical curiosity and enthusiasm for sport are highly valued.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
Successful Field Coaches consistently:
Leave every store team more knowledgeable and more confident than they found them
Translate performance science into guidance store staff can actually use
Build credibility through technical expertise and genuine passion
Uphold merchandising and presentation standards in every door, every visit
Strengthen retailer confidence in and advocacy for the brand
Become recognised contributors within local running communities

Job Description:
Role Purpose
The Inside Sales Advisor is responsible for converting qualified leads into signed customer contracts through a professional, consultative, phone-based sales process. This is not a generic telesales role.
The role requires a commercially sharp sales professional who can sell subscription-based, financial-value, and technically enabled energy products to customers who may be sceptical, price-sensitive, comparison-shopping, or unfamiliar with solar and prepaid-led energy solutions.
The successful candidate must be able to understand customer needs, explain complex product value propositions clearly, build trust quickly, manage a CRM pipeline with discipline, and close high-quality customers into signed agreements. This JD builds on the original telesales profile, but raises the calibre requirement from basic telesales to technical inside sales, while retaining the core requirements around consultative selling, closing, CRM pipeline management, and customer experience.
We are looking for high-performing inside-sales professionals who can sell subscription-based, financial-value, and technically enabled energy solutions over the phone.
This is not a basic telesales role. You will need to understand customer needs, explain complex product value clearly, build trust with sceptical customers, manage your CRM pipeline with discipline, and close customers into signed contracts. Experience in insurance, telecoms, SaaS, financial services, Solar, Energy, Fibre, or other contract-based product categories will be highly advantageous.
Residential and Light Commercial Energy Solutions
Sales Conversion and Pipeline Management
Convert qualified inbound, outbound, referral, and campaign leads into signed customer contracts.
Sell across residential and light commercial energy products, including solar, backup, prepaid-led, subscription, and adjacent energy solutions.
Run a structured consultative sales process to understand customer needs, electricity usage, property profile, affordability, decision drivers, and objections.
Recommend the right product based on customer requirements and product fit.
Explain pricing, savings, subscription value, contract process, credit requirements, installation journey, and customer obligations clearly.
Close customers effectively into signed contracts.
Maintain an accurate and up-to-date pipeline in the CRM system.
Create follow-up tasks, capture call notes, update sales stages, and record lost reasons accurately.
Proactively manage customer follow-ups to prevent leakage between interest, qualification, contract sent, and contract signed.
Customer Education and Trust Building
Build trust with customers who may be sceptical, cautious, price-sensitive, or comparing alternatives.
Explain complex product value propositions in simple, commercially compelling language. Handle objections related to price, affordability, savings, contract terms, installation, product reliability, and service expectations.
Provide a professional and confidence-building customer experience from first contact through to signed agreement.
Avoid overpromising or misrepresenting product capability, savings, timelines, or contractual terms.
Ensure customers understand what they are signing and what happens next in the journey
Financial and ROI-Based Selling
Hold confident conversations about monthly cost, savings, value, affordability, and return on investment.
Help customers understand the financial benefit of the recommended product versus their current energy cost or alternative solutions.
Position subscription-based products in a way that is clear, credible, and customer-relevant.
Use financial-value framing to support conversion without creating unrealistic expectations.
Identify when a customer is not financially or operationally suitable and escalate or qualify out appropriately.
CRM, Data, and Performance Discipline
Use CRM consistently as the single source of truth for lead status, customer notes, next steps, and pipeline movement.
Maintain accurate records of contact attempts, customer interactions, qualification outcomes, objections, lost reasons, and contract status.
Track and understand personal sales metrics, including contact rate, conversion rate, close rate, pipeline age, follow-up completion, and reasons for lost sales.
Use performance data to improve personal sales effectiveness.
Participate in coaching, pipeline reviews, call reviews, and performance discussions.
Take ownership of personal sales activity, productivity, and conversion outcomes
Brand Representation and Customer Experience
Represent the company professionally in every call, WhatsApp, email, and customer interaction.
Deliver a consistent, high-quality sales experience aligned to the brand promise. Communicate clearly, respectfully, and confidently.
Collaborate with sales supervisors, operations, credit, scheduling, installation, and customer success teams where required.
Support a smooth handover from sales to downstream operational teams.

Minimum Qualifications
Matric required.
Tertiary qualification in sales, marketing, business, finance, technical studies, or a related field is advantageous.
Minimum 2–3 years’ proven sales experience in a phone-based, remote-sales, telesales, or inside-sales environment.
Proven experience selling subscription-based, financial, technical, telecoms, SaaS, insurance, energy, solar, fibre, security, or other contract-based products is highly advantageous.
Demonstrated ability to manage a sales pipeline using a CRM system.
Proven experience in consultative selling, objection handling, follow-up management, and closing.
Experience working in a target-driven or commission-led environment.
Key Competencies
Consultative selling and needs diagnosis.
High-conversion closing.
Ability to rapidly learn and confidently articulate complex product value propositions.
Financial and ROI-based conversation skills.
Trust-building with sceptical customers.
Objection handling.
CRM and pipeline discipline.
Customer focus and service excellence.
Self-awareness of personal sales metrics and performance.
Results-driven and commission-oriented mindset.
Ethical and responsible selling.
Resilience and accountability.
Structured follow-up and pipeline ownership.

Job Description:
Purpose of role:
The Operations Change & Delivery Specialist acts as the operational interface between Prescient Fund Services Operations and ICT project team. The role coordinates operational technology initiatives from requirement clarification through to development tracking, testing, rollout and post-implementation review. The individual is an Operations resource, not an ICT resource, and is accountable for ensuring operational priorities, stakeholder feedback, deadlines, risks and dependencies are clearly managed and visible throughout the project lifecycle.
The role is to create one coordinated Operations voice for technology and development change: clear requirements, clear ownership, clear deadlines, clear feedback loops, and controlled rollouts.
Duties and responsibilities:
Operational Project Portfolio Coordination
Maintain a complete and accurate register of Operations-related ICT projects, enhancements and development initiatives.
Status, owner, priority, due date, blockers and next actions must be current and visible to relevant stakeholders.
Operations and ICT Interface Management
Act as the primary Operations coordination point with ICT project teams. Ensure that operational priorities, requirements, dependencies and timelines are understood, documented and followed through.
Department Head Feedback and Stakeholder Alignment
Obtain structured feedback from relevant department heads and operational stakeholders. Consolidate feedback into clear actions, decisions and escalations so that project direction remains aligned to operational needs.
Deadline, Milestone and Action Tracking
Track deadlines, milestones, testing windows, approvals, rollout dates and action owners. Proactively escalate slippage, unresolved dependencies or decision delays before project delivery is materially impacted.
Business Requirements and Prioritisation Support
Coordinate the gathering and clarification of business requirements. Ensure requirements are sufficiently clear, agreed by Operations, and prioritised before ICT development work proceeds.
Testing, Sign-off and Rollout Coordination
Coordinate Operations involvement in user acceptance testing, release readiness, business sign-off, training/communications and controlled rollout into production.
Risk, Issue and Dependency Management
Maintain visibility of operational risks, ICT dependencies, resource constraints, unresolved decisions and delivery blockers. Escalate matters with clear impact, proposed resolution and required decision.
Governance, Reporting and Continuous Improvement
Prepare concise status reporting for management forums. Capture lessons learned after rollout and recommended improvements to the project/change process, control environment and stakeholder engagement model.
Required qualifications and experience:
Relevant financial qualification / post graduate qualification.
Extensive experience within a fund administration, investment operations, or fund services environment.
Proven ability to operate at a senior level within an operations function, taking ownership of deliverables and driving outcomes through collaboration with multiple stakeholders and team members.
Strong understanding of investment operations processes, controls, and service delivery within a regulated financial services environment.
