Company Details:
The new South African government signaled its intention to review the South African competition law regime in the White Paper on Reconstruction and Development in 1994 (Notice 1954 Gazette 16085 of 23 November 1994). The need for a new competition policy in South Africa must be seen in the context o...read moref a historical legacy of excessive economic concentration and ownership, collusive practices by enterprises and the abuse of economic power by firms in dominant positions. It was also recognized, however, that the South African economy and society was in a state of transition, in terms of a broader restructuring of the economy, the effects of globalization and trade liberalization and the need to redress past inequality and non-participation in the national economy. A fundamental principle of competition policy and law in South Africa thus is the need to balance economic efficiency with socio-economic equity and development.

The Evolution of Competition Policy in South Africa

The origins of competition policy in South Africa lie with the Regulation of Monopolistic Conditions Act, 1955 (Act No. 24 of 1955). A review of the Act in the 1970s found that it had been unsuccessful in preventing a dramatic increase in oligopolies. As a result, the Maintenance and Promotion of Competition Act, 1979 (Act No.96 of 1979) was introduced and the Competition Board, tasked with administering the Act, was established.

The 1979 Act was amended in 1986 to give the Competition Board further powers, including the ability to act not only against new concentrations of economic power but also existing monopolies and oligopolies. Despite the amendments, however, it was widely recognized that technical flaws in the Act prevented the effective application of competition law on both substantive and logistical grounds.

The Department of Trade and Industry embarked on a three-year project, consulting with experts and stakeholders, to arrive at a new competition policy framework for South Africa in 1995. In November 1997, the Department of Trade and Industry released Proposed Guidelines for Competition Policy entitled ”A Framework for Competition, Competitiveness and Development”. These guidelines formed the basis for negotiations with the National Economic Development and Labour Council (NEDLAC). The objective of the NEDLAC process was to reach agreement between business, government and labour on the policy principles, which would shape and inform competition legislation. A NEDLAC agreement on competition policy was concluded on 20 May 1998. After a fourteen-week public consultation process, the Competition Act, 1998 (Act No, 89 of 1998) was passed by Parliament in September 1998. Certain provisions of the Act were brought into effect in October 1998 to allow for the establishment of a new institutional framework. The remaining provisions of the Act became effective on 1 September 1999.

The New Competition Act

The stated purpose of the Competition Act, 1998 (Act No. 89 of 1998) is to promote and maintain competition in South Africa in order to achieve the following objectives:

To promote the efficiency, adaptability and development of the economy;
To provide consumers with competitive prices and product choices;
To promote employment and advance the social and economic welfare of South Africans;
To expand opportunities for South African participation in world markets and recognize the role of foreign competition in the Republic;
To ensure that small and medium-sized enterprises have an equitable opportunity to participate in the economy;
To promote a greater spread of ownership, in particular to increase the ownership stakes of historically disadvantaged persons.
Three institutions are created in terms of the Act to achieve the above objectives:

The Competition Commission
The Competition Tribunal
The Competition Appeal Court

Ensures that everyone within the program strictly abides by Company and Client policies and procedures. Recognizes and rewards top performers while carrying out disciplinary action / consequence management for non-performers.

Bachelor’s Degree in any course, preferably Business or Business Management.
Two (2) to three (3) years Call Center Operations, Customer Service, Business Process Outsourcing, or Telecommunications experience in an Asst. Managerial or Managerial capacity.
Proficient in call center operations and organization required.
Prior knowledge of client-specifics preferred.
Proficiency with MS Office applications (i.e. MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc...) and other call center-specific software / systems (i.e. CMS/IEX, Baleen, Blue Pumpkin, etc...).
Required skills + qualities (technical):
Client relations. Leadership and people-management skills.
Project management skills.
Excellent oral and written English communication skills with professional communication skills both verbal and written business correspondence; planning, organizing and coordination skills
Adaptive to changing work schedules and working hours.
Active listening skills.
Operates with minimal supervision.
Customer orientation.
Time Management and Multitasking skills.
Detail-oriented, Analytical, Problem-Solving and Decision-Making skills.
Presentation Skills.

Job Title: Senior Manager: Credit Risk Strategy (Home Loans) - Johannesburg
Job Description:
Job Summary
To manage Home Loans collections risk strategies within SA, focusing on developing, implementing and monitoring payments and collections and strategies.
An outcome of the role is to ensure strategies are developed, implemented and maintained payments collections and recoveries strategies to achieve stated impairment rates within risk appetite.
Collaborate with other stakeholders and teams to develop leading-edge predictive techniques and modelling is applied to ensure competitive and sustained advantage.
Job Description
Accountability: Strategy, Planning and Risk Management
Manage the implementation of leading-edge payment and collection strategies in Home Loans.
Manage and development collections and high-risk account management strategies (preventing a customer rolling into collections) using leading-edge techniques / scoring to maximize collections, including the ownership of implementation of the strategies (Example TRIAD, Collections Scorecards).
Review and optimize Forbearance strategies for Home Loans to ensure recoveries are maximized whilst rehabilitating the customer.
Participate in the strategy setting and design of the Collections Operations and External Debt Collectors incentive programmes to ensure their effectiveness in motivating collectors and ensuring performance is improved to attain budgeted targets.
Participate in strategy setting and design for the payments solution across the different payment types, including DebiCheck, RMS and other, to ensure improved instalment collection performance.
Maintain documentation of end‐to‐end credit collections strategy.
Develop strategy and policy tests to challenge and enhance current strategies.
Understand the interaction between the macro environment and credit performance and adjust credit collections strategies to accommodate stressed events – based on macro expectations.
Ensure Management Information (MI) in place or is developed to monitor strategy performance and effective implementation/adherence by quality checking MI teams reports and reviewing the information the relevant product committees.
Ensure that the required portfolio reviews are completed, review the results and make recommendations to the business leaders on how their business activities should be tweaked to improve portfolio performance.
Ensure systems used for implementing collections strategies are fit for purpose and identify and specify enhancements by confirming strategies are working as required and as per implementation plans.
Accountability: Stakeholder and Relationship Management
Coordinate and communicate collections activities with the respective BUs, Risk, technology and Operations teams.
Drive close collaboration with the Operations and Technology teams and instill a co-operative and conducive working relationship.
Secure support from Collections and Recoveries Operations, Risk Teams, MI, Business teams, Finance and HR to deliver collections programs.
Participate in the BU / Manco meetings to ensure adequate communication and understanding of senior managers in the BU around the analytics-based methodology used by Risk and decision-making, and the benefits thereof.
Support the BUs to deliver impairment targets and Loan Loss Rates aligned with the forecasting by providing proactive analysis and guidance on how to manage credit risk within acceptable levels.
Liaise with various internal stakeholders (e.g. Risk Management, Collections Operations, Risk Head, IT and Enablement, Group Risk) to secure their respective support in the implementation of changes to the strategies and support implementation.
Review and report strategy performance and trends to the Head: Home Loans collections and recoveries strategy, Operations Manco, Home Loan Exco and other relevant committees as required.
Accountability: People and Culture
Builds and sustains a culture that aligns to RBB’s aspirational colleague experience to deliver the target customer experience and financial performance.
Ensure delivery of business goals by aligning Performance Development (PD) Plans of direct reports to the business goals.
Instil a performance development culture through directing the PD process and adhering to the PD calendar.
Ensure delivery of business goals by managing and developing colleagues on a project-by-project basis to deliver on the desired business goals.
Pro‐actively identify development areas of indirect reports within the HL collections strategy team and assist with development plans to address them.
Assist with the interview process for HL Risk function to attract and retain talent, with the assistance from the HR Business Partner.
Identify team capabilities and develop a succession plan, with the assistance from the HR Business Partner.
Initiate disciplinary action process as and when required, with the assistance of the Employee Relations Consultant.
Effectively lead team members and ensure their efforts are recognized.
Ensure execution of plans seeking to address employee related issues ‐ e.g. Employee Survey (EOS) action plans.
Accountability: Control
Accountable for ensuring an optimal and complaint control environment within the product that appropriately balances collections activities and customer experience with the need to grow to achieve the financial ambitions and balance sheet aspirations of RBB.to address employee related issues ‐ e.g. Employee Survey (EOS) action plans.
Education and experience required
Honours Degree in Mathematics and / or Statistics or equivalent NQF level 8 qualification. (Preferred)
3 years of relative banking experience of which 2 years should be in a senior role (preferably Retail Banking).
Highly numerate and literate.
Well-rounded credit professional with sufficient management experience.
Knowledge and skills:
Knowledge of / in dealing with Retail Bank clients (Expert).
Proven record of accomplishment in credit management & Sanctioning (Expert).
Financial analysis and interpretation skills (Advanced).
Stakeholder Management Skills (Advanced).
Decision Management using predictive models (Expert).
SAS Skills (Expert).

The ability to analyze and quickly grasp the implications of a situation, relating data from different sources, critically evaluating and integrating information / facts, and diagnosing a problem.

The ability to set ambitious goals, maintain a bias for action, drive delivery and take accountability for the outcome.

Collaboration and Influencing
Ability to build an extensive and collaborative network amongst different stakeholders within and externally of the organization (at the most senior levels) that supports the achievements of the business goals.

Ensure data quality is assessed and embedded as an integral part of new solution and project development, rather than tested only after delivery

Gather and interpret functional requirements from Data Owners, model owners, and business stakeholders; translate into governance and reporting solutions
Draft governance documentation and reporting to a standard suitable for internal governance and team use

Decentralized Clinical Trial Study Leads (DCTL) are an integral part of clinical trial delivery to improve patients’ lives and bring therapies to the market faster. The DCTL role requires strong project management skills, customer and site facing engagement experience, creativity/innovation and the ability to thrive in a dynamic setting.
The DCTL may oversee studies ranging from fully decentralized trials to hybrid studieswhich require liaising withtraditional project delivery teams. Critical to the success of DCT is the ability to collaborate across multiple teams and stakeholders including but not limited to technology & IT , mobile nursing, site support services, regulatory, site startup, etc. DCTL’s also follow established SOP and policies focused on project delivery, productivity and quality resulting in strong project financial performance and customer satisfaction.
Responsibilities
Essential Functions
Accountable for the strategic development and delivery of DCT studies in line with agreed upon contracts while optimizing speed, quality and cost of delivery, ensuring consistent use of study tools and training materials and compliance with system updates, standard processes, policies and procedures.
Serve as DCT project oversight and/or contact with customers and own relationship with the project’s key customer contact(s)
Set objectives for the DCT project team according to agreed upon contract, strategy and approach, effectively communicate and assess performance, providing feedback and leadership.
Collaborate with other functional groups within the company where necessary, including the core study team, to develop and/or support the preparation of integrated study management plans, support milestone achievement and manage study issues and obstacles.
Monitor progress against contract and prepare/present project information proactively to all stakeholders internally and externally.
Supervise problem solving and resolution efforts to include management of risk, contingencies and issues. Take accountability for proactive contingency plans to mitigate risks.
Achieve project quality by identifying and proactively managing quality risks and issues, responding to issues raised by project team members and /implementing appropriate corrective and preventative action plans.
Ensure the financial success of the project including optimal management and assignment of resources to achieve project goals and profitability.
Forecast and identify opportunities to accelerate activities to bring milestones and revenue forward and implement appropriate actions to achieve.
Identify changes in scope and manage change control process, including securing customer agreement to financial and milestone updates as necessary.
Identify and communicate lessons learned and best practices to promote continuous improvement.
Other Functions May Include
Participate in bid defense preparations. Lead bid defense presentations in partnership with Business Development for 100% Virtual studies or as a component of the larger team for integrated hybrid DCTs studies. Understand project strategy and operationalize the agreed upon approach.
Adopt corporate initiatives and changes and serve as a change advocate when necessary.
Provide input to line managers on their project team members’ performance relative to project tasks. Support staff development. Mentor less experienced project team members on assigned projects to support their professional development.
Educate and train other teams and partners on the processes, capabilities and structure of the DCT organization.
Communicate/collaborate with IQVIA business development representatives as necessary.
Mayparticipate in executive committees as part of program leadership.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree Life sciences or related field Req
Requires 5 years relevant clinical research experience or equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
Requires advanced knowledge of and experience implementing Project Management methodologies, ideally within the clinical research space.
Broad knowledge of DCT(current challenges and opportunities to improve clinical trial delivery) and other related job areas, typically obtained through advanced education combined with experience.
Knowledge of clinical trials - Knowledge of clinical trial conduct, and skill in applying applicable clinical research regulatory requirements i.e. ICH GCP and relevant local laws, regulations and guidelines, towards clinical trial conduct. Broad protocol knowledge, therapeutic knowledge desired.
IQVIA Core Competencies - Ability to demonstrate all IQVIA competencies (Client Focus, Collaboration, Communication, innovation, Ownership).

Experience managing sales, stock, margins and operational KPIs.
Experience in a high-volume retail environment will be advantageous.
Experience in liquor retail and knowledge of liquor legislation will be highly advantageous.
Knowledge & Skills
Strong commercial and financial acumen.
Strong stock and inventory management skills.
Knowledge of liquor products and categories.
Understanding of liquor legislation and responsible alcohol sales.
Customer service orientation.
People management and leadership capability.
Planning and organisational skills.
Problem-solving and decision-making ability.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to analyse sales and operational information.
Computer literacy, including MS Excel.

Key Responsibilities
Commercial & Financial Management
Drive the achievement of departmental sales, gross profit and budget targets.
Monitor daily, weekly and monthly sales performance and take corrective action where required.
Analyse sales, margin, waste, stock loss and other relevant performance indicators.
Identify opportunities to grow sales and improve departmental profitability.
Implement promotional activities and ensure effective execution of liquor campaigns and deals.
Manage departmental expenses in line with budget and company guidelines.
Drive productivity and efficient utilisation of departmental resources.
Liquor Department Operations
Manage the daily operation of the Liquor Department to ensure smooth and efficient execution.
Ensure adequate stock availability across key liquor categories.
Maintain high standards of merchandising, product presentation, pricing and promotional execution.
Ensure shelves, displays and promotional areas are correctly maintained.
Ensure correct receiving, storage, replenishment and rotation of liquor products.
Monitor stock movement and identify slow-moving, excess and fast-moving products.
Ensure effective management of stock counts and investigate variances.
Maintain high standards of cleanliness, housekeeping and overall department presentation.
Stock & Inventory Management
Maintain effective stock control processes to minimise stock losses and improve availability.
Monitor stock levels and ensure timely replenishment.
Investigate stock discrepancies, shrinkage and potential losses.
Ensure correct receiving and verification of liquor deliveries.
Conduct and oversee regular stock counts.
Implement appropriate measures to minimise theft, damages and stock losses.
Work closely with the Inventory and Store Management teams to resolve stock-related issues.
Liquor Compliance & Risk Management
Ensure full compliance with applicable liquor legislation and licensing requirements.
Ensure the store operates within the conditions of its liquor licence.
Ensure responsible sale of liquor and compliance with age-verification requirements.
Ensure employees understand and adhere to legal requirements relating to the sale of liquor.
Maintain required liquor documentation and records.
Ensure compliance with Pick n Pay policies, procedures, health and safety requirements and operational standards.
Identify and mitigate operational, legal, security and reputational risks within the department.
Customer Service
Deliver a consistently high standard of customer service.
Ensure customers receive knowledgeable and professional assistance with liquor products.
Resolve customer complaints and queries effectively and promptly.
Monitor customer feedback and identify opportunities to improve the shopping experience.
Ensure the department is well presented, accessible and easy to shop.
People Management
Lead, coach and develop the Liquor Department team.
Ensure employees understand their roles, responsibilities, KPIs and performance expectations.
Allocate duties and manage staffing according to operational requirements.
Conduct regular performance discussions and provide constructive feedback.
Identify training and development needs within the team.
Manage attendance, timekeeping, discipline and employee relations in accordance with company policies.
Build a high-performing, customer-focused team culture.
Identify and develop talent for succession and future leadership opportunities.
Merchandising & Category Execution
Ensure liquor ranges are merchandised according to company standards and category principles.
Maintain accurate pricing, ticketing and promotional communication.
Ensure promotional displays are implemented on time and maintained throughout the promotion.
Monitor competitor activity and identify opportunities to improve the department's competitiveness.
Ensure premium, high-volume and strategic product categories receive appropriate focus.
Security & Loss Prevention
Work closely with Store Management and Security to minimise liquor-related stock losses.
Identify risks associated with high-value and high-risk liquor products.
Ensure appropriate controls are followed when receiving, storing and selling liquor.
Investigate unusual stock movements and report suspected theft or fraudulent activity.
Ensure employees comply with security and loss-prevention procedures.
Reporting & Administration
Monitor and report on departmental performance.
Maintain accurate operational and stock-related records.
Prepare relevant reports and provide feedback to Store Management.
Use available business intelligence and reporting tools to identify trends and performance gaps.
Ensure all required administrative processes are completed accurately and on time.

Job Description:
Job Description
Dermalogica South Africa is seeking a commercially driven Junior Trade Marketer: Retail and Concept Stores to support the execution of trade marketing initiatives that bring brand strategy to life in retail, create consumer demand and drive sell-out performance across retail partners and Dermalogica Concept Stores.
Reporting to the Trade Marketing Manager / Marketing Manager, the role will support the planning and execution of retail campaigns, product launches, promotions, visual merchandising, consumer activations and in-store experiences.
The role is responsible for ensuring marketing activity is translated effectively into the retail environment, with a clear focus on execution excellence, consumer engagement, conversion and commercial results.
The role works closely with Sales, Retail Operations, Education, Ecommerce, Marketing, stockists and agency partners to ensure activations are delivered on time, to brand standards and with clear commercial objectives. The role will also monitor retail performance, gather field insights and recommend opportunities to improve execution and drive demand.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Retail Trade Marketing & Activation
Support the development and execution of retail activation plans aligned to key trading periods, product launches, campaigns and commercial priorities.
Coordinate and execute in-store campaigns, promotions, launches, consumer activations and events across retail partners and Concept Stores.
Translate marketing campaigns and brand strategies into clear, impactful and commercially focused in-store executions.
Ensure activation plans are adapted to the requirements, opportunities and trading environment of individual retail partners and Concept Stores.
Coordinate campaign timelines, POS materials, sampling, promotional mechanics and other trade requirements to ensure activations are delivered effectively.
Monitor activation execution and proactively identify and resolve issues that may impact visibility, consumer engagement or sales performance.
Driving Consumer Demand & Sell-Out
Support initiatives designed to create consumer demand, increase footfall and convert consumer engagement into retail sales.
Implement trade activities that support improvements in conversion, average transaction value and repeat purchase.
Identify opportunities to maximise the commercial impact of product launches, promotions and key trading periods.
Work with retail and store teams to ensure they understand the consumer proposition, product focus, promotional mechanics and key selling messages behind each activation.
Support initiatives that connect consumer education, treatment experiences and retail recommendations to drive product purchase.
Monitor sell-out performance and identify opportunities to improve activity and drive incremental sales.
In-Store Trade Execution & Retail Excellence
Ensure trade marketing activity is executed consistently and effectively across retail environments and Concept Stores.
Conduct regular store visits to monitor campaign visibility, merchandising, POSM, promotional execution, product availability and the overall consumer experience.
Maintain and uphold Dermalogica visual merchandising and brand standards across retail environments.
Identify execution gaps and work with relevant teams to implement corrective actions.
Ensure POS materials, campaign assets and promotional collateral are deployed correctly, on time and maintained throughout the campaign period.
Provide regular field feedback and recommendations to improve future activations and in-store execution.
Support the delivery of a consistent and premium Dermalogica consumer experience across all retail touchpoints.
Retail Partnerships & Stakeholder Management
Build collaborative relationships with retail teams, Concept Store teams, stockists and external partners to support effective trade execution.
Support the development of retailer activation proposals, presentations and commercial plans.
Work with retail teams to align on activation objectives, execution requirements, consumer messaging and sales opportunities.
Act as a reliable point of contact for day-to-day trade marketing execution and activation requirements.
Gather feedback from retail partners and identify opportunities to improve activation effectiveness and commercial performance.
Commercial Performance & Insights
Track retail sell-out performance and analyse the impact of activations, promotions and product launches.
Compile monthly reporting on activation execution, sell-out performance, campaign effectiveness and key retail insights.
Monitor competitor activity, shopper behaviour and retail trends to identify opportunities to drive demand.
Use store visits, retail feedback and performance data to identify execution gaps and commercial opportunities.

Job Description
Dermalogica South Africa is seeking a customer-focused and data-driven CRM Specialist to take ownership of customer relationship management activity across ecommerce and retail channels, ensuring CRM platforms, customer data, lifecycle journeys and retention initiatives are effectively managed and optimised.
Reporting to the Ecommerce Manager, the CRM Specialist will be responsible for implementing and optimising personalised customer communications, loyalty initiatives, customer lifecycle programmes, segmentation strategies and retention activity that drive customer engagement, repeat purchase behaviour and lifetime value.
Success in this role will be measured through customer retention, repeat purchase rate, customer lifetime value, loyalty programme performance, CRM-driven revenue contribution, database health and campaign effectiveness.
KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
CRM Campaign
Management
Plan, execute and optimise CRM campaigns across email marketing, SMS marketing, loyalty communications, customer lifecycle journeys and automated customer communications.
Build, deploy and quality-check customer communications according to the CRM calendar.
Ensure all communications align with Dermalogica’s brand guidelines and customer strategy.
Coordinate campaign assets and approvals with internal and external stakeholders.
Monitor campaign performance, identify optimisation opportunities and implement continuous improvements.
Customer Lifecycle Marketing
Develop, maintain and optimise customer lifecycle programmes, including welcome journeys, first-purchase journeys, abandoned cart programmes, post-purchase communications, re-engagement campaigns and VIP customer programmes.
Identify opportunities to increase customer retention, repeat purchases and long-term customer value.
Ensure customers receive relevant communications at key stages of their journey.
Loyalty Programme Management
Manage the day-to-day performance, communication and optimisation of Dermalogica’s loyalty programme.
Monitor customer participation, engagement and programme performance.
Coordinate loyalty campaigns, rewards and customer communications.
Identify opportunities to improve customer loyalty and long-term engagement.
Assist in implementing global loyalty initiatives within the local market.
Customer Segmentation & Personalisation
Develop and maintain customer audience segments using behavioural, transactional and demographic data.
Support customer profiling and audience development initiatives.
Implement personalised communication strategies to improve engagement and conversion.
Ensure customer communications are relevant to customer interests and purchasing behaviour.
CRM Reporting & Analytics
Track, analyse and report on CRM campaign performance, including open rates, click-through rates, conversion rates, revenue contribution, retention rates, database health and loyalty metrics.
Produce weekly and monthly CRM performance reports.
Develop actionable insights to improve campaign effectiveness and customer engagement.
Monitor customer trends and provide recommendations to support business growth.
Ecommerce, B2B & Retail CRM Support
Collaborate with Ecommerce, Retail and Marketing teams to align CRM activity with key business priorities.
Support product launches, promotional campaigns and seasonal activity through CRM channels.
Ensure CRM campaigns support both online and retail customer acquisition and retention objectives.
Assist in driving customer engagement across ecommerce and retail touchpoints.
Customer Data Management
Own customer database quality and data integrity, ensuring customer information is accurate, current and fit for segmentation and reporting.
Ensure customer records, opt-ins and consent management processes comply with company policies and applicable regulations.
Assist with data cleansing and ongoing database optimisation.
Support audience creation and campaign targeting requirements.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Work closely with Brand, Ecommerce, Retail and Global CRM teams to ensure consistency across customer communications.
Coordinate campaign requirements with designers, content creators and platform partners.
Share customer insights and recommendations with key stakeholders.
Support broader digital marketing initiatives where required.
QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS
Degree, Diploma or equivalent qualification in Marketing, Digital Marketing, Business, Communications or a related field.
CRM platform certifications and email marketing certification would be advantageous.
EXPERIENCE REQUIRED
Minimum 3-5 years’ experience in CRM, email marketing, customer retention, marketing automation or digital marketing, with proven ownership of CRM activity
Advanced Excel skills and strong reporting capabilities.
Proven experience managing customer lifecycle, retention and loyalty campaigns from planning through to reporting and optimisation.
Experience with CRM and email marketing platforms such as Klaviyo, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Dotdigital, Mailchimp, HubSpot or similar CRM platforms.
Experience configuring CRM workflows, customer segments, automation journeys and campaign reporting dashboards would be advantageous.
Understanding of customer segmentation and personalisation strategies.
Experience working in an ecommerce or retail environment.
Knowledge of loyalty programme management and customer engagement strategies.
Experience using reporting and analytics platforms such as Google Analytics 4 (GA4), CRM reporting tools and ecommerce reporting dashboards.
Experience with Shopify or similar ecommerce platforms would be advantageous.
KEY COMPETENCIES
Customer Centricity:
Passionate about understanding customer behaviour and improving customer experiences, with a focus on developing long-term customer relationships.
Analytical Thinking:
Uses data and customer insights to drive decision-making and identify opportunities to improve engagement and retention.
Results Orientation:
Accountable for CRM performance and customer growth metrics, with a drive to improve customer lifetime value and retention.
Attention to Detail:
Delivers accurate and high-quality campaign execution while maintaining strong database and campaign governance standards.
Planning & Organisation:
Effectively manages multiple campaigns and deadlines, demonstrating strong project coordination skills.
Communication & Collaboration:
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across departments and stakeholders.
Work Environment:
This role is based out of our Cape Town office.

Job Description:
Job Description
homechoice is a leading South African homeware retailer. For over 40 years we’ve helped our customers create beautiful homes they love with an innovative range of quality products they can afford.
The Sales Associate is responsible for delivering an exceptional in-showroom customer experience by converting customer visits into sales through effective product demonstration, needs analysis, and accurate order processing.
The role focuses on frontline sales execution, customer service, administration, and adherence to operational standards, supporting the Store Supervisor and Showroom Manager in achieving sales and service outcomes.
What you will love doing in this role
Sales Execution & Conversion
Actively engage customers on the showroom floor to understand their needs and convert interactions into sales.
Demonstrate products effectively, clearly communicating features, benefits, pricing, and promotional offers aligned to the current catalogue.
Achieve individual sales targets, conversion rates, and productivity expectations.
Support acquisition activities, including account openings and order processing.
Customer Experience
Deliver a consistently positive, professional, and customer-focused sales experience.
Guide customers through the full customer journey, including product selection, ordering, payments, and after-sales processes.
Resolve basic customer queries and escalate complex issues to the Store Supervisor or Showroom Manager.
Build customer trust through accurate information, ethical selling, and clear expectation setting.
Product Knowledge & Pricing Accuracy
Maintain strong knowledge of products, categories, pricing, and promotions.
Ensure all selling and quoting is accurate and aligned to approved catalogues and systems.
Stay informed of product updates, promotions, and sales initiatives.
Administration & Order Processing
Capture customer orders, documentation, payments, refunds, and credits accurately and timeously.
Ensure all required customer documentation is complete and compliant.
Maintain accurate records and system entries to support reporting and audits.
Stock Handling & Showroom Standards
Support basic stock handling activities, including receiving assistance, stock movement, and floor replenishment.
Ensure products are handled with care to prevent damages.
Maintain high standards of housekeeping, visual presentation, and merchandising on the sales floor.
Follow stock control procedures and report discrepancies or risks.
Compliance, Quality & Risk Awareness
Adhere to all policies, procedures, quality standards, and internal controls.
Follow cash handling procedures when processing payments, refunds, or credits.
Participate in required training, inductions, and policy sign-offs.
Escalate risks, errors, or non-compliance to the Store Supervisor.
Teamwork & Performance Support
Work collaboratively with team members to achieve showroom targets.
Support promotions, campaigns, and activations as instructed.
Be flexible in supporting operational requirements, including shifts, weekends, and public holidays.
What you’ll need to do this role
Grade 12 / Matric (minimum requirement).
Minimum 1 years’ retail sales experience.
Customer-facing sales experience within a target-driven environment.
Availability to work shifts, weekends, and public holidays.
Homewares retail experience (advantageous).
Clear credit and criminal record.

Customer-focused with a strong service mindset.
Persuasive, confident, and professional communicator.
Detail-oriented with a focus on accuracy and quality.
Resilient, adaptable, and able to work in a fast-paced environment.

Company Details: Established in 1984, ACDC Dynamics is the leading manufacturer, importer and distributor of quality products in the electrical, electronics, pumps and tools industries. Employing over 700 staff, ACDC Dynamics has its Head Office in Edenvale, Johannesburg with branches in Germiston, Cape Town, Pin...read moreetown and Riverhorse in KZN.Manufactured items from ACDC Dynamics includes transformers, power supplies, electronic timers, distribution boards, motor starters, MCCs and power factor correction systems. Since October 2006, ACDC Dynamics has manufactured and distributed Rhomberg Electronics, a long established premium brand whose products include timers, counters, temperature controllers, relays and sensors. These products are manufactured in Cape Town and distributed world-wide through the Rhomberg distributor network. The manufacturing facilities form part of our Cape Town branch in Paarden Eiland and are certified ISO9001:2008 by SABS.At its head office in Edenvale, there are 3 manufacturing workshops. The electronics workshop produces plug-in timers and relays. The transformer workshop manufactures power supplies and air cooled transformers from 1.5VA to 50kVA, up to 1000V. The panel workshop produces PFC systems, pump starters, MCCs, DBs, automatic changeover switches (ATS & AMF) and automation control systems with PLC, drives and telemetry. It has an estimating and engineering team to oversee stock and custom products production. ACDC Dynamics markets to specifiers, consulting engineers and architects, pulling back to distribute its products through OEMs, Franchises and electrical wholesalers throughout Southern Africa.70 of the leading electrical wholesalers are appointed as official Distributors who keep stock and have trained staff to support ACDC Dynamics products. End users, electrical contractors and small OEMSs are referred to Franchises or Official Distributors, foot print permitting. This places ACDC Dynamics products within easy reach of anyone in Southern Africa. ACDC Dynamics products are specified in projects ranging from stadiums to mines, hotels to homes and from farms to breweries.ACDC Dynamics continues to develop its distribution footprint of Franchises in Southern Africa. A Franchise is an independently owned electrical wholesaler whose products are primarily sourced from ACDC Dynamics and trades with the brand ACDC Express. ACDC Dynamics further supports these franchises through the ACDC Express company, in that it provides its business model for implementation, as well as administrative and marketing support. One of the focused directions for ACDC Dynamics is going “green” with the company offering an extensive range of power saving products, including LED lighting, plus alternative and hybrid power supply systems with on and off-grid solutions, combining Solar PV and wind generators with mains electricity and conventional diesel and petrol back-up generators.Solar water heating systems supplied by ACDC Dynamics are also an important part of this initiative. The company is committed to providing fast, efficient and friendly service. Internal systems are constantly evaluated and upgraded where needed, always keeping in mind, that the end goal is to make life easier for customers. The company provides national sales and technical call centres. Orders and enquiries may be processed through this website, as well as viewing copies of invoices, credit notes and POD’s. ACDC Dynamics has also implemented a sign-on-glass system in a bid to remove any unnecessary paperwork from the order process.ACDC Dynamics is proud of its Apprentice school, an initiative that is run once every two years. The two year apprenticeships trains electricians, electronic mechanicians and armature winders. One of the company’s many strengths is its’ catalogue, which is widely recognised as a benchmark in the electrical industry. At over 1000 pages the 2019/20 catalogue is is our biggest, boldest catalogue yet, and stands as proof of ACDC Dynamics’ determination to keep evolving and providing the most up to date products possible. The Rhomberg catalogue is additional to this. Many short form catalogues are also available, in order to better service any customers with more specific interests. Product ranges include Alarms, Hygiene, Industrial and Domestic Automation, Telemetry Systems, Pumps, Switchgear & Instrumentation, Energy Management and Power Factor Control, Solar and Wind generators, Tools, Wire, Adhesives and consumables, cable and wire management products, and the most comprehensive range of Lighting including energy saving lighting using CFL, inductive and LED technologies. Leading international brands from ACDC Dynamics include C&S (India), Datalogic (Italy), Gewiss (Italy), Terasaki (Japan) and Weicon (Germany).

Job Description:
Job purpose
The Support Lead is responsible for leading the IT Support function and ensuring consistent delivery of efficient, customer-centric and ITIL-aligned support services. The Support Lead will lead and develop the support team, monitor service performance, manage escalations, identify opportunities for improvement and drive the adoption of self-service, automation and AI-enabled support capabilities.
The role is accountable for people leadership, service performance, operational effectiveness, customer experience, escalation management and continual improvement.
The role is not primarily a hands-on technical support position. While the Support Lead is expected to maintain sufficient technical knowledge to provide guidance and manage complex escalations, day-to-day technical resolution remains primarily the responsibility of the Support Team.
Key responsibilities
PERFORMANCE LEADERSHIP & TEAM PERFORMANCE
Lead and manage the IT Support team, creating a high-performing, customer-focused support culture.
Set clear expectations regarding service quality, productivity, customer experience and professional conduct.
Provide coaching, mentoring and ongoing development to team members.
Conduct regular performance reviews and manage performance in accordance with organisational processes.
Identify skills gaps and implement appropriate development and training plans.
Support recruitment, onboarding and development of new team members.
Manage team capacity, workload allocation and resource planning to meet business demand.
Manage schedules and rosters to ensure appropriate service coverage, including after-hours requirements.
Develop a pipeline of capable support resources and identify opportunities for career progression within the team.
Promote collaboration, accountability and knowledge sharing across the support function.
SERVICE DELIVERY & ITSM
Lead the day-to-day delivery of IT Support services in accordance with agreed SLAs, policies and ITIL-aligned processes.
Ensure incidents and service requests are appropriately logged, prioritised, assigned, monitored and resolved by the Support Team.
Monitor ticket queues, backlogs, ageing tickets and workload distribution.
Ensure appropriate escalation of tickets that cannot be resolved within the Support Team.
Ensure effective use of Jira Service Management and approved support channels.
Monitor service performance and identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement.
Ensure appropriate adherence to Incident Management, Request Fulfilment, Escalation Management, Knowledge Management and Continual Improvement practices.
Work with direct and internal IT Management team to identify and implement improvements to service delivery processes.
INCIDENT, ESCALATION & MAJOR INCIDENT MANAGEMENT
Act as the operational escalation point for complex, high-priority and business-critical support issues.
Provide technical guidance to the Support Team when incidents require additional expertise.
Coordinate escalations with Infrastructure, Applications, Security, vendors and other relevant technology teams.
Support the coordination and communication of major incidents affecting business operations.
Ensure appropriate stakeholder communication during significant service disruptions.
Monitor escalated incidents through resolution and ensure ownership is maintained.
Participate in post-incident reviews and ensure agreed corrective actions are followed through.
Identify recurring incidents and trends and collaborate with relevant teams to support root-cause analysis and problem management.
SERVICE PERFORMANCE & REPORTING
Own and monitor IT Support performance against agreed KPIs and SLAs.
Analyse service desk data to identify trends, performance gaps and opportunities for improvement.
Provide regular performance reporting to the direct manager and relevant stakeholders.
Use data to coach the team and improve individual and overall team performance.
Monitor key indicators including:
SLA achievement
First Contact Resolution
Mean Time to Resolve
Ticket backlog
Ticket ageing
Reopened tickets
CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE & STAKEHOLDER MANAGEMENT
Promote consistent, professional and customer-centric support experience across all support channels.
Monitor customer feedback and identify recurring service issues.
Ensure customer complaints and escalations are managed professionally and appropriately.
Ensure support communications are clear, timely and appropriate to the audience.
Identify opportunities to improve the end-user experience and reduce customer effort.
AUTOMATION, AI & SELF-SERVICE
Identify opportunities to reduce repetitive and avoidable support demand through automation, self-service and AI.
Drive adoption of approved AI-enabled support capabilities, including AI chatbots, WhatsApp AI and other digital support channels.
Monitor the effectiveness and quality of AI-assisted support services.
Identify gaps in AI responses, workflows and knowledge content and coordinate improvements with relevant stakeholders.
Ensure appropriate human oversight of AI-enabled support processes.
Promote self-service and knowledge-based support to empower users to resolve appropriate issues independently.
Own the effectiveness of the IT Support knowledge management capability.
Ensure knowledge articles, FAQs, troubleshooting guides and support documentation are accurate and current.
Ensure knowledge is readily accessible to both support teams and end users.
Encourage the Support Team to contribute to and maintain the knowledge base.
TECHNICAL SUPPORT & OPERATIONAL OVERSIGHT
Maintain sufficient technical knowledge to provide guidance and support escalation management.
Provide technical direction to Support Team members when issues exceed their current capability.
Review complex technical issues and ensure appropriate escalation where required.
Oversee the effective delivery of desktop, endpoint, application and connectivity support by the Support Team.
Support the planning and execution of technology upgrades and changes affecting end users.
SECURITY, RISK & COMPLIANCE
Ensure Support Team activities comply with relevant information security policies, standards and procedures.
Ensure security-related incidents are appropriately identified and escalated.
Collaborate with SecOps and other relevant teams on security-related support matters.
Ensure appropriate controls are considered when implementing automation, AI and self-service solutions.
Promote security awareness and good technology practices within the Support Team and user community.
Ensure appropriate handling and escalation of security and data-related risks.
CONTINUAL SERVICE IMPROVEMENT
Identify opportunities to improve service quality, efficiency and customer experience.
Use service data, customer feedback and operational trends to identify improvement opportunities.
Lead or participate in initiatives to improve IT Support processes and services.
Identify opportunities to eliminate repetitive work through automation and self-service.
Identify recurring incidents and support problems and work with relevant technology teams to reduce recurrence.
Measure the impact of improvement initiatives and communicate outcomes to stakeholders.
Promote a culture of continual improvement within the Support Team

Minimum 5 years’ experience in IT Support, Service Desk, Technical Support, Customer Service or IT Service Management.
Proven experience leading or supervising a technical support team.
Working knowledge of IT Service Management principles and practices
Experience managing service performance against SLAs and KPIs.
Relevant IT, Business, Management or related diploma/degree, or equivalent practical experience.

People leadership
Coaching and mentoring
Customer focus
Stakeholder management
Problem solving
Decision making
Analytical thinking
Conflict resolution
Change management
Continuous improvement

Accountability
Innovation and adaptability
Ability to work effectively under pressure

Job Description:
Role Purpose
The Opex Controller owns the operating cost base of the Merchant Division end to end - how costs are captured at source, allocated, reported and analysed, and the budget and forecast the division is held to. The role exists to give every cost centre owner, the divisional executive and Group Finance a single trusted view of what the division spends, why it is moving, and what is being done about it.
The division operates across multiple legal entities and jurisdictions, spanning merchant acquiring, cash management, lending and software, and carries a recharge from Group.
As a subsidiary of a US-domiciled dual-listed parent, SOX 404 and SEC obligations sit alongside IFRS reporting. This is a controllership role with a strong business partnering edge: the successful candidate will produce the numbers, interrogate them, challenge the owners of the spend, and drive the process, system and policy discipline that keeps the cost base under control.
Key Responsibilities
Cost Collation, Allocation & Close
Collate opex across all Merchant entities into a single consistent divisional view, allocated accurately to cost centres and owners; investigate and clear misallocations, suspense-held and unallocated costs.
Govern the cost centre hierarchy - additions, closures, mergers and owner changes - and its mapping to divisional and Group reporting structures.
Validate the opex base before release: accrual completeness and release, prepayment amortisation, cut-off, classification, and support for manual journals.
Reconcile the divisional view to entity trial balances and Group submissions and meet the divisional and Group close timetable including the quarterly cycles supporting the listed parent.
Reporting, Analysis & Dashboards
Produce monthly reporting at cost centre, owner and executive level to a published timetable, reconciled to the ledger and requiring no rework by recipients.
Provide variance analysis against budget, forecast and prior period with commentary that explains drivers, separating underlying movement from foreign exchange translation and one-off items.
Build and maintain dashboards for high-scrutiny categories - travel, professional fees, contractors, connectivity, software and licensing, amongst others - giving owners self-service visibility between reporting cycles.
Link the costs to drivers and propose cost improvement initiatives.
Budget & Forecast
Run the divisional opex budget end to end - timetable, templates, assumptions, guidance, consolidation, review and sign-off - built bottom-up by cost centre against documented drivers rather than prior-year uplift.
Challenge submissions on volume, headcount, rate and inflation assumptions, and require justification for growth above agreed parameters.
Maintain the rolling in-year forecast with a quantified risks and opportunities register, escalating movements early, and track forecast accuracy by cost centre.
Deep Dives, Savings & Business Partnering
Run a rolling programme of deep dives into material expense lines, decomposing spend by vendor, entity, cost centre and driver.
Identify duplication, contract overlap, unused licences, off-contract spend and out-of-market pricing; quantify the opportunity, recommend action, and track savings into the run rate.
Act as the finance point of contact for opex, equipping cost centre owners to manage their spend, and partner with the Merchant Central Services Lead on the central services cost base and the basis on which it is allocated to business units.
Prepare and act as secretariat to the monthly divisional cost review forum, and escalate persistent overspend or non-engagement to the Finance Lead.
Group Recharges & Intercompany
Review and challenge recharges received from Group - basis, allocation keys and quantum - and allocate them onward to entities and cost centres on a documented methodology.
Own intra-divisional charging where costs are incurred in one entity on behalf of others, and ensure intercompany balances agree across entities before close.
ERP, Procurement & B-BBEE
Represent divisional cost management in the ERP rollout: define and enforce the financial dimension standard, validate data quality through migration, train users, and use the system to automate the monthly cycle.
Enforce procurement compliance - purchase order coverage, no-PO-no-pay, three-way matching and delegation of authority routing - report exceptions by cost centre, and partner with Procurement on vendor master quality and the contracted spend and renewals view.
Maintain the divisional measured procurement spend base, reconciled to the ledger, and partner with Procurement to keep supplier B-BBEE evidence current on the vendor master.
Report preferential procurement recognition in-year, model the effect of pending sourcing decisions, flag those with an adverse scorecard consequence before they are taken, track Enterprise and Supplier Development spend, and prepare the schedules and audit trail for annual verification.
Policy, Controls & Audit
Propose, draft and implement divisional expenditure policies, and drive adoption, training and monitoring once approved.
Operate and evidence assigned opex controls to Group SOX standard, enforce discipline over expense approval, purchase order compliance and journal support, and support Group SOX and internal audit through walkthroughs, testing and remediation.
Support the external audit on opex, accruals and expense cut-off within the audit timetable.
Minimum Requirements
Qualifications & Experience
CA(SA), newly qualified or with up to approximately three years’ post-qualification experience; CIMA with equivalent depth will be considered.
Articles at a recognised firm with multi-entity group exposure; financial services, payments or fintech clients an advantage.
Management accounting, cost centre reporting or opex budgeting experience in a multi-entity or divisional environment, including intercompany and cost allocation.
Hands-on ERP experience; involvement in an ERP implementation or a Microsoft Dynamics 365 environment is a strong advantage. Exposure to a SOX or equivalent control environment is an advantage.
Skills & Attributes
Advanced Excel and strong modelling capability; data visualisation skills, or the aptitude to build them quickly.
Sound IFRS grounding applied practically to expense recognition, accruals, prepayments and cut-off.
Able to work with large, imperfect multi-entity datasets and produce reporting that stands up to challenge.
Willing to challenge - comfortable questioning senior stakeholders and holding a position with evidence rather than assertion, without damaging the relationship.
Structured and self-directed, able to build process in an environment that is still forming and see work through to completion.
Clear communicator, able to explain financial information to non-financial owners and write commentary an executive can act on.

Job Description:
Job Purpose:
To contribute to the development of integrated reputation management, marketing and communications strategies by managing Brand South Africa's Regional Offices in Asia Pacific & Australasia / UK & Europe / Americas. This also includes:
Promoting South Africa as a competitive destination by managing;
Collaborating with, and implementing brand and communications programmes in partnership with stakeholders; as well as
Building nation brand advocacy amongst South Africans in the diaspora.

Bachelor's Degree in Political Science /Marketing / Business Management / Communications or equivalent.
Preferred: Postgraduate degree in Political Science / Marketing / Business Management/ Communications (e.g. MBA will be an added advantage).

10+ years combined experience in marketing/ Communications/ Public Relations/ Stakeholder Relations at a senior/management level (of which 5 years must be at a senior management level).
International experience or function in an international coordination role.
Key Performance Areas:
Brand Positioning & Reputation Management:
Adapt South Africa's positioning in the market, strengthen the national brand, and manage perceptions around South Africa's competitiveness, investment climate, tourism, culture, and international reputation.
Monitor perceptions of the country within the assigned market and proactively identify opportunities or risks affecting the nation's reputation and develop programmes that will seek to ensure that the country brand is enhanced.
Support media engagements and identify positive storytelling opportunities that reinforce the national brand.
Provide Head Office with regular market intelligence on emerging issues that influence international perceptions of South Africa.
Regional marketing and communications execution.
Translate Brand South Africa's corporate strategy and annual business plan into a regional marketing and communications plan, and deliver it on time and within budget.
Design and execute region-facing campaigns and activations in partnership with South African stakeholders.
Secure stakeholder buy-in for campaigns and initiatives, covering content, tone, roll-out mechanisms, budget, target audiences, shared ownership, timelines and outputs.
Report on campaign performance against agreed objectives, including audience reach, engagement, media coverage, key-message penetration, digital performance and demonstrable return on investment.
Feed stakeholder input, research and environmental scanning back to Head Office to refine activation plans.
Stakeholder and partnership management.
Build and sustain strategic relationships with government representatives, business leaders, investors, media, industry bodies, tourism and cultural institutions, and diaspora networks in the region.
Secure partnerships and collaborations that amplify Brand South Africa's messaging through joint advocacy, thought leadership and market activation.
Track stakeholder sentiment and emerging issues affecting South Africa's reputation, and convert these into actionable recommendations.
Work in close coordination with South African diplomatic missions in the region, with due regard to the Department of International Relations and Cooperation's country and regional strategies.
Align with the Head Office stakeholder team where stakeholders are similar locally and abroad.
Risk and crisis management
Identify, document, escalate and mitigate strategic, operational, reputational and stakeholder risks affecting Brand South Africa's activities in the region, in line with the organisation's governance framework.
Maintain and review the regional risk register and report on key risks, emerging issues and mitigation measures to Head Office.
Maintain crisis preparedness and respond promptly and appropriately to reputational incidents affecting the Nation Brand.
Governance, compliance and reporting
Ensure that all regional activity complies with Brand South Africa's policies, the Public Finance Management Act, Treasury Regulations, supply chain management prescripts and applicable host-country law.
Report monthly and quarterly against the organisation's performance measurement framework and business plan scorecard, and contribute to the strategic plan, annual performance plan and annual report.
Protect the Brand South Africa corporate identity, copyright and brand alignment across all regional and partner materials.
Scan the wider public policy environment to identify opportunities for future work and to build relationships with policymakers and influencers.
Meet planning department's timelines for reporting.
Financial management
Manage the regional budget, monitor expenditure against approved plans, and account for variances.
Comply with Head Office supply chain management processes in all regional procurement.

Where applicable, delegate work assignments and tasks to appropriate individuals, providing sufficient direction so desired business outcomes can be achieved.
Implement Brand South Africa policies and procedures as required.
Provide direct reports with leadership, direction, and coaching to achieve work objectives and improve performances and skills.
Be a change champion for culture transformation, lead and guide the team through change.
Build and manage relationship with staff members.
Manage risks and address issues as the arise.
Performance Management (where applicable) - ensure the team members achieve their Performance Objectives as per individual agreements.
Staff Development (where applicable), motivation and training.
Recruit respective staff and select.

Thorough knowledge of the workings of the business and macro-economic environment (domestic and international).

Conversational.

Working knowledge of systems and processes and how they contribute to organisational performance.
Advanced knowledge of how to determine value from a customer perspective.

Ability to develop content for media across various platforms – including print, broadcast and digital.

Above average interpersonal and communication skills to engage credibly with stakeholders at different levels and with different needs (public relations).

Change management.

Proven ability to perform under pressure.
Above average level of perceptiveness and discernment, i.e. ability to read situations correctly and respond accordingly to instil confidence and direction.
Networking ability, i.e. building and maintaining relationships for business and collaborative opportunities.
Service-oriented, i.e. desire to serve and be customer-oriented.

Special requirements, based in markets and or willing to travel.

Job Description:
Purpose of the Role:
Partnering closely with the Junior Compliance Manager, the Compliance Administrator provides structured administrative support to Dis-Chem Life’s Compliance function by maintaining accurate records, coordinating compliance processes, supporting monitoring activities, and ensuring regulatory documentation is complete, current, and audit-ready.
Operating in a regulated financial services environment, this role helps ensure that clients, internal teams, and relevant stakeholders operate within applicable regulatory frameworks, internal policies, and ethical standards. The role strengthens the compliance environment by keeping processes organised, evidence reliable, and stakeholders supported.
Success in this role is defined by accurate compliance administration, efficient stakeholder support, timely monitoring support, reliable issue tracking, and disciplined follow-up on actions, deadlines, registers, and compliance evidence.
Role Summary
The Compliance Administrator is responsible for supporting the core compliance administration activities that underpin the effective operation of Dis-Chem Life’s Compliance function.
At a high level, success in this role requires the ability to operationalise regulatory requirements through accurate record keeping, document control, FICA/KYC and financial crime administration, intermediary onboarding and monitoring, representative onboarding, compliance monitoring support, reporting, and reliable follow-through on actions and deadlines.
The Compliance Administrator works closely with the Junior Compliance Manager and cross-functional business stakeholders to ensure that compliance records, registers, evidence packs, policies, procedures, and reporting inputs are complete, well organised, and maintained in line with internal and regulatory standards.
Benefits:
Join a high-impact compliance function within a growing, regulated insurance business.
Gain practical exposure to compliance administration, FICA/KYC, financial crime controls, monitoring support, and regulatory documentation.
Work closely with the Junior Compliance Manager and key business stakeholders.
Build a strong technical and administrative foundation for long-term career progression in compliance.
Contribute directly to maintaining accurate records, audit-ready evidence, and effective compliance support.
Key Responsibilities
Compliance Administration, Records, and Registers
Maintain compliance registers, trackers, folders, and evidence repositories.
Capture, update, and validate compliance data in line with internal standards.
Perform checklist reviews to identify missing, expired, or incomplete records.
Support document control, filing, and audit-readiness across compliance processes.
Maintain regulatory obligation registers, compliance calendars, breach logs, complaints registers, gifts and conflicts registers, and compliance attestations.
Compile evidence packs for compliance reviews, audits, regulatory inspections, and management reporting.
Intermediary and Advisor accreditation and monitoring
Compile supporting documents and complete onboarding checklists for intermediary applications
Conduct license checks on intermediaries and perform continuous monitoring
Maintain and update the intermediary database ensuring accuracy, completeness and audit readiness
Identify and escalate risks or compliance concerns identified during the onboarding or monitoring processes.
Representative onboarding and license registration
Assist with checking, validating, and submitting onboarding documentation for new representatives.
Ensure all representatives are correctly registered on the Dis-Chem Life FSP licence.
Maintain an accurate and updated Representative register
Support ongoing updates to representative records and regulatory information.
Coordinate with external licensing authorities to resolve registration or licensing issues.
Stakeholder Support
Provide administrative support for compliance-related queries across the business.
Respond to or escalate queries within reasonable timelines.
Assist stakeholders with locating, completing, and submitting required compliance documentation.
Maintain professional communication and follow-up on outstanding compliance actions.
FICA and Financial Crime Compliance Administration
Maintain FICA, sanctions screening, and KYC records accurately and within required timelines.
Update FIC reporting evidence, registers, and related records.
Support sanctions screening and KYC administration.
Escalate screening exceptions, missing documentation, and overdue reviews promptly.
Compliance Monitoring and Controls
Assist with compliance monitoring activities across Dis-Chem Life.
Track compliance findings and ensure remedial actions are implemented.
Support internal audits, regulatory inspections, and compliance reviews.
Provide recommendations to strengthen control frameworks and prevent regulatory breaches.
Soft Skills:
Exceptional integrity, ethics, and professional judgment.
Analytical, detail-oriented, and highly organised.
Strong analytical skills
Adaptable, resilient, and able to perform under pressure in a deadline-driven environment
Self-managed, accountable, and results-oriented
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Collaborative mindset with the ability to work independently.
Customer Service Orientated
Ability to thrive in structured and unstructured environments.
Skills and Experience:
Minimum of 1–3 years’ experience in compliance administration, financial services administration, insurance, or regulated financial services environment
Working knowledge of FAIS, FICA and POPIA, requirements, knowledge of Long-Term Insurance Act and related regulatory obligations advantageous
Strong administrative, data-capturing, filing, reporting, and document-control skills
Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, especially Outlook, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint
High attention to detail, confidentiality, and ability to follow structured processes and deadlines
Clear Criminal Record essential
Qualifications:
Minimum NQF level 5 qualification
Compliance, Risk Management, Business Administration, Legal Studies , or a related field certification is advantageous.

Job Description:
Job Description
This role is designed for Retail Sales Professionals ready to launch a career in Financial Services!
We're looking for individuals who thrive on the retail floor, naturally connect with people, and have a talent for creating opportunities wherever they go. You are someone who builds relationships with ease, earns trust quickly, and has probably been told more than once that you can talk to and sell to anyone.
This opportunity is ideal for experienced retail sales professionals who don't just work in sales but genuinely enjoy engaging with customers and delivering exceptional service. If retail sales is where your strengths shine and you're ready to make your mark in the financial services industry, this could be the perfect next step in your career.
Purpose of the Role
This role is for a retail sales professional who knows that every conversation is an opportunity.
At Dis-Chem Life, thousands of customers walk through our stores every day. Behind every customer is a family, a goal, a responsibility, or someone they care about.
Your role is to build meaningful connections, identify needs, and introduce financial solutions that provide protection, security, and peace of mind.
Success in this role comes from connecting with people, building trust, and creating value through authentic conversations. We're looking for someone who is confident, approachable, naturally engaging, and skilled at turning customer interactions into sales opportunities.
This opportunity is ideal for a retail professional who has built their career through face-to-face sales, relationship building, and customer engagement. Someone who thrives on the retail floor, actively creates opportunities, and understands that great sales often begin with a genuine conversation.
Summary of the Role
As a Retail Financial Sales Consultant, you will actively engage customers on the retail floor and turn everyday store visits into meaningful financial conversations.
This is not a desk-based role. You will be expected to confidently approach customers, ask the right questions, understand their needs and introduce suitable Dis-Chem Life insurance solutions.
Key Responsibilities
Proactively engage customers throughout the store rather than waiting for customers to approach you.
Identify suitable opportunities to start conversations with customers in a natural, respectful and confident way.
Ask thoughtful questions to understand customers’ immediate needs, financial concerns and family responsibilities.
Introduce and explain Dis-Chem Life’s funeral, individual life and other insurance solutions in simple, relatable language.
Turn initial conversations into meaningful consultations and quality sales opportunities.
Recommend solutions that are relevant to the customer’s needs, circumstances and affordability.
Build trust quickly through strong listening, confident communication and genuine interest in the customer.
Guide customers through the digital quotation, application and verification process.
Use a tablet, computer, CRM system and other digital tools to manage customer information, follow-ups and sales activity.
Maintain an active pipeline of prospective customers and follow up consistently on opportunities.
Work collaboratively with store teams, including customer-facing employees, to create awareness and generate appropriate customer referrals.
Achieve agreed sales, conversion, activity and customer-service targets.
Maintain accurate records and complete all required customer and compliance documentation.
Protect customers by following all approved sales, advice, quality and Treating Customers Fairly requirements.
Take ownership of product knowledge, training and ongoing professional development.
Represent Dis-Chem Life professionally and contribute positively to the customer experience inside the store.
INTERPERSONAL SKILLS AND BEHAVIOURAL REQUIREMENTS
Naturally personable and comfortable engaging with people from diverse backgrounds.
Confident initiating conversations and building rapport with customers you have never met.
Strong relationship-building skills with the ability to establish trust quickly.
Excellent listening skills with the ability to identify customer needs and opportunities.
Communicates information clearly, simply and confidently.
Resilient and able to remain positive and motivated in the face of rejection.
Self-motivated and able to maintain momentum during both busy and quieter trading periods.
Results-driven with a strong desire to achieve and exceed targets.
Takes pride in personal presentation and professional conduct.
Highly accountable, disciplined and dependable.
EXPERIENCE AND PROFESSIONAL REQUIREMENTS
2 + Years proven experience within a customer-facing retail sales environment.
Demonstrated success in face-to-face sales, promotions, customer acquisition or consultative selling.
Experience working in a fast-paced retail environment with high customer volumes.
Ability to work retail hours.
Proven ability to engage customers, generate opportunities and convert conversations into outcomes.
Comfortable promoting, demonstrating, consulting on and closing products or services face-to-face.
Proven track record of working towards and achieving sales or performance targets.
Minimum Requirements
Matric (National Senior Certificate ), NQF4 or equivalent qualification.
Demonstrated experience in a customer-facing retail sales environment.
Proven face-to-face sales experience in which you were required to approach, engage, advise or sell directly to customers.
A track record of working towards individual sales, conversion, revenue or customer-activity targets.
Strong spoken communication, listening and relationship-building skills.
Computer literacy and confidence using tablets, mobile applications, digital forms and customer-management systems.
A professional, well-groomed and brand-appropriate personal presentation.
The ability to work retail hours, including weekends and public holidays when required.
Reliable transport to and from the allocated store.
Willingness to complete financial-services product, compliance and regulatory training.
Ability to meet the applicable Fit and Proper requirements as the role develops.
Advantageous Qualifications and Experience
The following would strengthen your application but are
not entry requirements
:
An NQF Level 5 qualification.
A diploma or degree in finance, financial planning, business, marketing, retail management or a related field.
Previous experience selling insurance, financial products, mobile contracts, memberships, automotive products or other consultative consumer solutions.
Experience conducting product demonstrations, activations, promotions or in-store campaigns.
Experience working in a traditional retail environment.
The Reality of the Role
This role requires you to be active and visible on the retail floor.
You will speak to customers who did not necessarily arrive at the store planning to discuss insurance.
You will need to create interest respectfully, earn their attention and show them why the conversation may matter to them and their families.
Some customers will say yes. Some will say no. Others will require patient follow-up. You must be comfortable with all three.
If you prefer waiting for customers to approach you, avoiding sales targets or working mainly behind a desk, this role will not be the right fit.
But if you know how to work a retail floor, enjoy connecting with people and want to turn your sales ability into a meaningful career in financial services, we want to hear from you.

A second "gateway" into St Stithians is offered to entrants of Grade 8 as they embark on their high school journey in the Boys’ College of 780 students and the Girls’ College of 530 students.

Grade 12 students write the matriculation examinations of the Independent Examinations Board (IEB). Our campus is a place of natural beauty, with various landscape zones, and the College is committed to being an environmentally "green" school.

St Stithians seeks to provide a values-based and top-quality academic education, supported by a diverse extra-curricular offering. Our students matriculate as well-rounded individuals, well prepared to inspire excellence and make a difference both in our own country, the African continent and globally.
