Job Title: Technologist | Medical Scientist | Medical Laboratory Scientist | Genetics | 6-Month Contract | Centurion
Job Description:
Description
As a Technologist or Medical Laboratory Scientist in Genetics, you will play an important role in supporting the delivery of high-quality molecular genetic testing services.
Working within a dynamic Molecular Genetics Laboratory, you will process specimens in accordance with established standards and laboratory requirements, helping to ensure accurate and reliable outcomes for patients and healthcare providers.
This role offers the opportunity to contribute to a collaborative and high-performing environment where scientific excellence, continuous learning, and professional accountability are valued.
You will be part of a team that takes pride in advancing diagnostic services while fostering a culture where people are supported to grow, develop their expertise, and make a meaningful impact through their work.
Requirements
Qualification Requirements
To be successful in this position, you will hold a BSc Honours Degree and be registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) as a Medical Scientist in Human Genetics / Genetics or Molecular Genetics, Medical Laboratory Scientist (Cytogenetics) or Bachelor of Health Sciences in Medical Laboratory Sciences Medical Technologist (Cytogenetics). These qualifications will provide the scientific foundation and professional standing required to perform confidently within a specialized Molecular Genetics environment while maintaining the standards expected of the profession.
You will bring a minimum of two years’ experience within a Molecular Genetics or Human Genetics laboratory environment. Through this experience, you will have developed a sound understanding of laboratory practices, specimen processing, quality requirements, and scientific methodologies relevant to molecular diagnostics.
Experience working within a collaborative team environment will enable you to contribute effectively while continuing to build your technical expertise. You will also be eager to share knowledge with colleagues and support the development of emerging scientific talent within the laboratory.
Skills Requirements
Success in this role requires strong computer literacy and the ability to use technology confidently and effectively as part of daily laboratory operations. You will be comfortable working with laboratory systems and digital tools to support quality, accuracy, and efficiency.
Strong communication skills are equally important. You will be able to read, write, and speak fluently in both English and Afrikaans, enabling you to interact professionally with colleagues, clients, and stakeholders while building positive and trusted relationships.
You will also possess sound numerical reasoning skills, allowing you to perform routine calculations accurately and confidently. Combined with a strong attention to detail and a commitment to quality, these skills will support your ability to deliver work of a consistently high standard.
Role Impact
In this role, you will contribute to the laboratory’s success by receiving and processing specimens in a manner that supports the timely delivery of results and excellent service to healthcare professionals and patients. Your scientific expertise will assist in the development and evaluation of assays, contributing to innovation and the ongoing enhancement of laboratory services.
You will play an active role in accreditation and quality control activities, helping to uphold the standards that underpin confidence in our results and services. Through knowledge sharing and practical guidance, you will support the training and development of learner scientists, contributing to a culture of learning and professional growth.
Beyond the laboratory, you will help maintain positive client relationships and represent the organisation with professionalism and integrity. Your contribution will support a people-centred environment where collaboration, continuous improvement, accountability, and scientific excellence come together to make a meaningful difference every day.

Job Description:
Description
As a Learner Scientist, you will embark on a meaningful learning journey that combines scientific knowledge with practical laboratory experience. This role offers the opportunity to develop technical expertise while contributing to the delivery of quality diagnostic services that support patient care.
Working alongside experienced professionals, you will gain exposure to laboratory operations, scientific methodologies and quality standards, building the foundation for a successful career in the scientific field. Through structured learning, hands-on experience and continuous development, you will contribute to a culture that values curiosity, collaboration, accountability and excellence.
Requirements
Role Qualification Requirements
To be considered for this opportunity, you will have completed one of the relevant BSc Honours Degree in either Genetics/ Human Genetics/ Biochemistry/ Molecular Biology/ Cell Biology/ Haematology or Forensic Genetics discipline that provides a strong foundation in laboratory science and research principles.
You will demonstrate a passion for science, a willingness to learn and a commitment to developing the professional and technical capabilities required to succeed within a dynamic laboratory environment.
While previous laboratory experience may be advantageous, this role is designed for individuals who are eager to apply their academic knowledge in a practical setting and build their professional capability. Exposure to basic laboratory techniques through academic study, research projects or practical training will enable you to adapt quickly to the laboratory environment and contribute effectively to daily operations.
You are motivated by learning opportunities and are committed to developing both your technical expertise and professional skills through mentorship, collaboration and hands-on experience.
Skill Requirements
You possess strong analytical thinking and a keen attention to detail, enabling you to approach scientific work with accuracy and care. Your computer literacy allows you to work effectively with laboratory systems, documentation and data management tools, while your communication skills enable you to engage professionally with colleagues and stakeholders.
You have a solid understanding of scientific principles and are eager to expand your knowledge through practical application. Your ability to follow procedures, maintain quality standards and work responsibly with laboratory equipment and specimens supports a safe and effective laboratory environment.
You are naturally curious, organised and proactive, with a willingness to learn from others and embrace new challenges. Through a collaborative approach and a strong sense of accountability, you contribute positively to team objectives and continuously seek opportunities to grow your expertise and professional confidence.
Role Impact
As a Learner Scientist, you will play an important role in supporting laboratory operations while developing the skills and knowledge required for future scientific responsibilities. Your contributions will help ensure that laboratory processes are performed accurately, efficiently and in accordance with established quality standards.
By embracing learning opportunities and actively participating in laboratory activities, you will build the capabilities needed to support future scientific and operational needs. Your commitment to quality, continuous improvement and professional growth will contribute to a positive laboratory culture and strengthen the organisation's ability to deliver trusted and reliable diagnostic services.
This role provides an exciting opportunity to grow your scientific career while making a meaningful contribution to a team dedicated to excellence, innovation and outstanding service.

Job Description:
Description
As a Branch Administrator, you play a vital part in keeping our laboratory and Care Centre running smoothly. You ensure that everyday administrative activities are completed accurately, on time, and with care—supporting specimen processing, quality service delivery, and seamless operations.
Your work helps create a High Performance Culture by enabling dependable, efficient processes, and it sets the tone for Employee Engagement by ensuring every patient and colleague interaction feels considered, professional, and people‑centred. Through dependable support and clear ownership, you also help empower leaders to focus on clinical excellence, reinforcing Leadership Empowerment and Accountability across the branch.
Requirements
Role Requirements
Grade 12 (Matric) is essential. This foundation enables you to handle sensitive information responsibly, follow established procedures confidently, and contribute to a consistently high standard of service.
Experience of 0–4 years in administration is suitable for this role. Exposure to a pathology or medical environment would be advantageous, yet what matters most is a strong eye for detail, well‑developed organisational skills, and a calm, professional manner. You are comfortable taking ownership of tasks, asking for support when needed, and working in line with quality standards.
Skills Requirements
You bring a thoughtful, thorough approach to routine administrative work and demonstrate care, consistency, and attention to detail in everything you do. You ensure information and documentation are accurate and complete, follow procedures and instructions carefully, and manage your time effectively to meet deadlines in a busy, service‑driven environment.
You communicate clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing, and you build positive working relationships with colleagues, clinicians, patients, and other stakeholders. You are confident using standard office applications and relevant systems, and you handle confidential data discreetly and responsibly.
When a routine issue arises, you recognise it quickly and take appropriate action or seek guidance; when you see a potential delay, you act early to prevent disruption.
Role Impact
Your impact is felt every day,by patients, colleagues, and the wider care team. You ensure the backbone of the branch is strong by completing core administrative activities accurately and timeously. This includes capturing information, preparing documents, maintaining orderly records, and handling routine correspondence so that the right information reaches the right people at the right time.
You help to shape a welcoming, efficient Care Centre experience by greeting patients, guiding them through requisition forms, logging details in the laboratory information system, conducting benefits checks, answering calls, resolving routine enquiries, and assisting with account and billing questions. You confidently process card or cash payments and generate pro forma invoices where needed, all while maintaining professionalism and empathy.
You also support the smooth flow of laboratory operations. You receive specimens and verify that they match the tests requested, label and batch them according to protocol, and prepare them correctly for onward processing. When required, you help ensure that reports reach doctors or wards promptly and reliably.
These actions may feel routine, yet together they are pivotal: they reduce rework, prevent delays, and uphold quality. By taking clear ownership of tasks and collaborating with your team, you enable leadership to focus on decision‑making and service excellence.

Description
As our Payroll Manager, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring that every employee's payroll experience is accurate, compliant and seamless. This position is responsible for leading and managing the end-to-end payroll function, ensuring employees are paid correctly and timeously while maintaining the highest standards of governance, control and legislative compliance.
Working closely with stakeholders across People, Finance and Remuneration and Benefits, you will create confidence in payroll processes, drive continuous improvement and ensure payroll information supports informed business decision-making. Beyond managing processes and systems, you will lead a team that delivers a trusted and reliable service, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and excellence. Through your leadership, you will help create a people-centred environment where employees feel valued and supported, while enabling the organisation to maintain effective and sustainable payroll practices.
Requirements
Qualification Requirements
To be successful in this role, you will hold a relevant NQF Level 6 qualification, such as a Diploma or equivalent in Payroll, Finance, Accounting or a related field. A recognised payroll qualification or professional designation, such as a SAPA Certified Payroll Practitioner certification, will be advantageous and will demonstrate your commitment to ongoing professional development within the payroll profession.
You will bring a strong foundation of payroll and financial knowledge, coupled with a passion for delivering service excellence and upholding professional standards in a complex and evolving environment.
You have built a successful career within payroll, supported by a minimum of seven years of relevant experience, including at least three years in a leadership or management role. Your experience has enabled you to develop a comprehensive understanding of managing end-to-end payroll operations within a large and complex organisation, where accuracy, confidentiality and compliance are essential.
You have extensive experience working with Sage 300 People and are confident in managing payroll processing, reconciliations, statutory submissions, reporting, employee benefits administration and payroll governance. Your background includes collaborating with diverse stakeholders, supporting audit processes and leading payroll teams through periods of change and continuous improvement.
Most importantly, you have demonstrated the ability to build capable and engaged teams, creating an environment where people are empowered to perform at their best while delivering a dependable payroll service that employees and leaders can trust.
Skills Requirements
As an experienced payroll professional, you possess a strong understanding of South African payroll legislation, employee taxation and statutory requirements, supported by sound knowledge of payroll accounting principles and financial controls. You are highly proficient in Sage 300 People and understand the importance of system integrity, governance and accurate reporting.
You are naturally analytical and enjoy solving complex problems, identifying root causes and implementing practical solutions that strengthen processes and improve outcomes. Your attention to detail is matched by your ability to maintain a broader strategic perspective, ensuring payroll operations remain efficient, compliant and aligned with organisational requirements.
You are an organised and proactive leader who thrives in an environment where careful planning and sound judgement are essential. Through clear communication and strong stakeholder engagement, you build trusted relationships across the business and work collaboratively to resolve challenges and enhance service delivery.
Your leadership style is grounded in integrity, accountability and respect for others. You create clarity, empower team members to take ownership of their work and support their growth through coaching, knowledge sharing and continuous learning. You understand the importance of developing capability for the future while maintaining the confidentiality and professionalism expected when handling sensitive employee and organisational information.
Role Impact
In this role, your impact will extend far beyond payroll processing. You will help create a reliable and trusted payroll experience that supports employee confidence and organisational stability. By maintaining effective governance, controls and compliance, you will safeguard the integrity of payroll operations and contribute to sound business practices across the organisation.
Your leadership will shape a high-performing payroll team that is empowered, engaged and committed to delivering service excellence. Through continuous improvement and the effective use of systems and technology, you will identify opportunities to enhance efficiency, strengthen controls and improve the overall employee experience.
You will play an important role in supporting leaders and stakeholders with accurate payroll information and insights, enabling informed decision-making and organisational planning. By developing team capability, fostering accountability and encouraging a culture of learning and growth, you will contribute to building a sustainable payroll function that supports both current and future organisational needs.
This is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution by combining technical payroll expertise with people-focused leadership, ensuring the payroll function remains a trusted partner in supporting our employees and organisational success.

Identify and develop leadership talent through coaching, structured development, and performance management frameworks.

Job Description:
Job Summary
The Groups & Events Admin Support provides comprehensive administrative and operational support to the Groups & Events Coordinators and Groups & Events Manager, ensuring the effective coordination and smooth execution of group bookings, meetings, conferences, weddings, social events and other functions. The position plays an important role in maintaining accurate booking information, supporting the team with reporting and administration, and ensuring that all event requirements are communicated to the relevant departments in a timely and professional manner.
The role requires a comprehensive knowledge of the One&Only’s facilities, outlets, services and activities in order to effectively support the Groups & Events team and provide accurate information when required.
The position is responsible for preparing, formatting and distributing daily and weekly reports, including GRC reports from Opera, Weekly Transaction Reports, Lost Business Reports, Provisional Reports, BQT Forecasts and Deposit Schedules. The position also supports the preparation of information for weekly Commercial Meetings and monthly Groups Meetings by extracting, formatting and maintaining relevant reports and shared workbooks, ensuring that all required feedback is captured and up to date.
The Groups & Events Admin Support is responsible for maintaining accurate and current information within Opera Sales & Catering, including updating follow-up activities, entering new group and catering enquiries, capturing bookings that have been turned away due to availability, and ensuring that all relevant booking information is recorded correctly.
This includes enquiry notes, proposed rates, activity follow-ups, special requirements and future actions required by the Groups & Events Coordinators and Manager.
The role also assists with entering rooming lists and ensuring that all guest notes, special requirements, billing instructions and routing are correctly captured.
A key responsibility is the preparation and coordination of function documentation. This includes compiling contracts from approved Opera templates, assisting with the preparation of function sheets for clients and internal events, preparing function pack cover pages, printing function packs and BEOs, and ensuring that all documentation is distributed to the relevant operational departments within the required timelines.
The position assists in preparing the Daily One with information relating to upcoming groups and events, ensuring that operational teams have sufficient information and preparation time to deliver a seamless guest and event experience.
The role also provides administrative support with client and event requirements, including arranging halal and kosher catering upon request, coordinating parking vouchers from the V&A Waterfront, and assisting with additional event-related requirements. The position works closely with internal departments and external suppliers to ensure that all arrangements are confirmed, accurately documented and completed according to client requirements.
The Groups & Events Admin Support also assists with the financial administration of events by preparing pro forma invoices, monitoring deposit requirements and payment deadlines, allocating deposits and payments to the relevant blocks and PM accounts, and following up on outstanding payments. The role supports the billing process by ensuring that all function accounts are accurately maintained, daily billing is completed, payments are received and accounts are finalised within the required timelines. This includes assisting Accounts with commission payments, refunds, credit card refunds and other financial adjustments, as well as processing supplier payments for parking, audio-visual services, décor and other event-related suppliers.
The position requires a high level of organisation, accuracy, attention to detail and confidentiality, as well as the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced luxury hospitality environment. The role works closely with the Groups & Events team, Revenue, Sales, Finance, Food & Beverage and other operational departments to ensure that all group and event requirements are accurately captured, communicated and executed.
The ultimate objective is to provide reliable administrative support that enables the Groups & Events team to deliver seamless, personalised and exceptional experiences for clients and guests while ensuring that all operational and financial processes are completed accurately and efficiently.
Skills, Competencies and Requirements
Diploma or Qualification in Hospitality Management
Good communication, interpersonal and customer service skills.
Ensuring compliance with hygiene and health and safety legislation/guidelines.
Sense of urgency, attention to detail and a can do attitude

Company Details:
Who we are
Established in 1940, we are a national development finance institution set up to promote economic growth and industrial development. We are owned by the South African government under the supervision of the Economic Development Department.

Our vision
We aim to be the primary source of co...read moremmercially sustainable industrial development and innovation to benefit both South Africa and the rest of Africa.

Our mission
Our mandate is to contribute to the creation of balanced, sustainable economic growth in South Africa and on the rest of the continent.

We promote entrepreneurship through the building of competitive industries and enterprises based on sound business principles.

Our values
Everything we do is directed by our values:

 Passion
 Partnership
 Professionalism

Our mandate
The Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa Limited (IDC) was established in 1940 by an Act of Parliament (Industrial Development Corporation Act, No. 22 of 1940) and is fully owned by the South African Government.

The IDC was mandated to develop domestic industrial capacity, specifically in manufactured goods, to mitigate the disruption of trade between Europe and South Africa during the Second World War.

We have contributed to the implementation of South Africa's industrial policy for more than 70 years and established, among others, the petro-chemicals and minerals beneficiation industries. We have stimulated large industrial projects in these industries - acknowledged today as the cornerstones of the country's manufacturing sector - and influenced the establishment of industries in fabricated metals, agriculture and clothing and textiles.

During the 1990s, our mandate was expanded to include investment in the rest of Africa. The Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique was the first such venture. We secured investors from around the globe to establish a major industrial enterprise in a country plagued by decades of civil war. The smelter illustrated the viability of large projects on a continent often shunned by investors. Currently, our investments in Africa include mining, agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and telecommunications.

The IDC's funding is generated through income from loan and equity investments and exits from mature investments, as well as borrowings from commercial banks, development finance institutions (DFIs) and other lenders.

We align our priorities with government's policy direction and remain committed to developing the country's industrial capacity, as well as playing a major role in facilitating job creation through industrialisation.
Our industrial development role
As a key implementing agency of industrial policy, the IDC's activities currently centre on the National Development Plan (NDP), the New Growth Path (NGP) and the Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP). We identify sector development opportunities aligned with policy objectives and develop projects in partnership with stakeholders.

By developing industrial capacity the IDC achieves specific outcomes. The most important of these is to enable job creation through the companies we fund. In addition, IDC funding continues to promote regional development and integration, economic empowerment of communities and growing black industrialists. The IDC remains committed to promoting environmentally sustainable growth and increasing sectoral diversity to boost the local production of goods. The corporation also plays a critical role, directly and through its sefa subsidiary, in promoting entrepreneurial development and growing the SME sector.

While our funding activities focus mainly on the private sector, we work closely with different levels of government agencies and sector organisations to coordinate industry development. We also support government in other areas related to its development objectives, such as research and management of government funds allocated to achieving specific outcomes. We pro-actively develop and implement strategies in the rest of Africa to create and integrate value chains across the continent. Our aim is to use the strengths of different countries in the region to establish a more competitive industrial base.

The monitoring specialist is required to complete high quality monitoring reviews from planning to reporting, to contribute to the implementation of the CRAD’s compliance monitoring methodology and processes, and to ensure that IDC and all its subsidiaries are conducting business in accordance with applicable pieces of legislation and regulations and relevant codes and standards.

A bachelor’s degree in business related discipline; LLB, B Com Law, BA Law, Risk Management
Post-graduate Compliance Qualification is mandatory
CPRAC Qualification from CISA will have an added advantage
A bachelor’s degree in business related discipline; LLB, B Com Law, BA Law, Risk Management

Roles and Responsibilities
Develop a risk based annual compliance monitoring plan to ensure coverage of key compliance risks across IDC and subsidiaries for board approval. Work with the Compliance Manager to regularly assess the relevance and focus of the Compliance Monitoring Plan
Execute the board approved compliance monitoring plan and ensure that monitoring reviews are strategic and structural to deliver the required level of assurance within the agreed timelines as per the compliance monitoring schedule.

dentifying and risk rating of the applicable provisions
identifying, analysing and testing controls;

present the monitoring outcomes to business stakeholders;

Job Description:
Description
AI systems & agent-building:
Designs, builds and iterates the AI agents and workflows that run the brand's marketing inside the Marketing AI system - not just directing an existing system, but constructing and refining it. Extends this beyond content and campaign production to the operational side of the role itself: building agentic workflows - not manual processes or one-off automations - that make reporting, admin, approvals and day-to-day coordination run smoother and faster. Owns quality control on all AI-generated output before it goes external.
Brand voice & copywriting:
Owns tone-of-voice consistency across every channel and format. Uses the Marketing AI system's tooling to generate copy, drawing on approved copy documents and signed-off CI and brand guidelines, and signs off all copy for campaigns, social, web, sales collateral and internal comms before it's used. Maintains the reference material that trains the AI agents to write in-brand.
SEO, AEO & website:
Runs on-page SEO and keeps website content accurate and current. Creates blog and website content structured specifically for AEO - written and formatted to be easily surfaced and cited by AI answer engines - alongside testing and improving how those engines represent the brand. Tracks organic traffic and ranking performance as part of ongoing KPI reporting.
PR, thought leadership & long-form content:
Sources and shapes thought leadership - SME and leadership interviews, LinkedIn articles, award submissions and case studies. Owns the newsletter and long-form editorial calendar.
Production & outsourced resource management:
Books and briefs the outsourced content creator and plans shoot schedules with the outsourced videographer. Reviews raw and edited content for brand fit before publishing. Tracks outsourced spend against budget.
Comms approval:
Final reviewer of all outward-facing and internal comms for the brand before publication.
Social scheduling & posting:
Owns the content calendar and posting cadence across all social channels. Briefs all content into the Marketing AI system, which drafts, queues and schedules posts. Tracks growth across all channels - followers, engagement and reach. Being upskilled toward managing paid social spend directly.
Community management, inbox & reviews:
Owns inbound DMs, comments, shared-inbox queries and public review responses across the brand. Being upskilled toward AI-assisted triage and response drafting. Escalates anything sensitive rather than handling it solo.
New vertical & new-business marketing:
Identifies and pursues marketing opportunities in new verticals and new business, and builds collateral to support pitches.
Partnership collaboration:
Co-develops OEM co-marketing and cross-group partnership opportunities alongside the Head of Marketing.
Client retention marketing:
Supports the sales/BD motion with case studies, campaigns and collateral for winning and retaining global clients.
CSR/incentive funding activation:
Identifies opportunities within existing client relationships to activate CSR or employee-initiative funding into live CX campaigns.
Lead Gen Funnel:
Owns culture comms feeding CX's recruitment funnel. Builds nurture content for warm leads not yet ready to convert, and win-back campaigns for lapsed leads.
Internal comms.
Owns the internal comms calendar and content for Ignition CX, coordinating with EX, and other parts of the business on major announcements (EX retains sign-off on employee lifecycle comms).
Requirements
A tertiary qualification in Marketing, Communications or a related field is an advantage, but equivalent hands-on experience is equally valued and will not be treated as a lesser path into this role.
Experience
Experience working across multiple channels and formats in one role is more relevant here than depth in a single specialism, given the breadth this role covers, built through doing the work directly, not only directing others who did it. This must be paired with genuine, hands-on fluency in AI tools, not passing familiarity: real experience directing or building AI agents/workflows, a track record of AI-assisted work done.
SKILLS AND CAPABILITIES
Directing and building agentic AI workflows - not just prompting, but constructing, refining and maintaining multi-step AI agents across both marketing production and internal operational processes such as reporting, admin and approvals.
Quality judgement on AI-generated output - knowing when AI-drafted copy, content or campaign material is genuinely ready to publish versus needs human correction, before it goes external.
AEO-structured content writing - producing blog and web content specifically formatted to be surfaced and cited by AI answer engines, distinct from traditional on-page SEO.
Social channel growth management - running a content calendar and posting cadence across multiple platforms while tracking follower, engagement and reach growth, with a path toward managing paid social spend directly.
Community, inbox and public review management, including sound judgement on what requires escalation versus independent handling.
Outsourced production management within an approved spend threshold - briefing and coordinating content creator and videographer resources against budget.
DIGITAL AND AI FLUENCY
At Ignition Group, digital and AI fluency is not a nice-to-have — it is a core performance requirement for every role, at every level. As AI and automation reshape how work gets done, the ability to work confidently and responsibly alongside these tools is as fundamental as any technical or professional skill.
What this means in practice:
Digital fluency — navigating and using digital platforms, tools, and systems relevant to your role with confidence and competence
AI tool adoption — actively using approved AI productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot/Claude/CodeX) to improve the quality, accuracy, and efficiency of your work
Data literacy — reading, interpreting, and applying data and AI-generated outputs to make better decisions, not replacing your judgement but sharpening it
Automation awareness — recognising tasks and processes that can be improved through automation, and contributing to those improvements
Learning agility — staying curious, upskilling continuously, and adapting as tools and practices evolve
Responsible and ethical AI use — understanding data privacy obligations, the limits of AI-generated content, and applying sound human judgement at all times
